For clients that cannot speak MCP natively and only connect to OpenAPI tool servers (for example Open WebUI's External Tools / OpenAPI type), the server has a built-in OpenAPI layer — no extra mcpo proxy or container required:

  • GET http://<host>:8080/openapi.json — an OpenAPI 3.1 spec generated dynamically from the currently enabled tools
  • POST http://<host>:8080/tools/<tool_name> — invoke a tool with the arguments as a JSON body

In the client, just fill in the base URL http://<host>:8080; it fetches /openapi.json and lists every tool.

Note: by default (PUBLIC_TOOLS_AUTH_MODE=none) /mcp and the OpenAPI bridge perform no authentication. When exposing them publicly, set PUBLIC_TOOLS_AUTH_MODE=bearer with a high-entropy PUBLIC_TOOLS_BEARER_TOKEN, and have clients send Authorization: Bearer <token>. See Configuration.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Check the services and each module's status:

curl http://localhost:8080/openapi.json | head  # currently registered tools

Per-module row counts and service health are on the admin console's Dashboard and Service health pages; every tool (including unregistered ones and why) can be browsed and tried on the MCP tools page (/admin/mcp).

You can also call the health_check tool directly:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/tools/health_check \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'

The response includes DB / cache / per-module status, the server version and build (git sha), tools_version, the loaded terminology editions (terminology), the installed IG packages and default_ig.

For code-level tests see Testing.

docs.title: Admin Console
docs.text: The admin console is a session-authenticated operator interface mounted at /admin, used to upload source files, run and schedule data imports, manage model endpoints, settings and external FHIR servers, and monitor background jobs in real time. It is enabled by default (ADMIN_ENABLED=true) — it is the only way to import data; once the data is loaded you may set it to false to shrink a public deployment's attack surface (MCP tools, the worker and scheduled imports keep running).

docs.title: Enabling it and signing in
docs.text:
Set the following in .env and restart app:

ADMIN_ENABLED=true
ADMIN_USERNAME=admin
# One of the two: a plaintext initial password (hashed into the DB on first boot), or a precomputed hash
ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD=
# Generate a password hash (Node):
#   node -e "console.log('sha256$' + require('crypto').createHash('sha256').update('change-me').digest('hex'))"
# ⚠️ Every $ must be written as $$ in .env (Docker Compose expands $ as a variable
#    reference, and a hash starting with a letter gets silently truncated).
#    Compose collapses $$ back to a single $.
ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH=sha256$$...
ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET=<openssl rand -hex 32>
ADMIN_SESSION_TTL_MINUTES=240
ADMIN_MAX_UPLOAD_MB=512
# pgcrypto symmetric key for external FHIR servers' OAuth tokens / client secrets.
# Falls back to ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET when unset.
FHIR_SERVER_SECRET_KEY=

Password hashes support sha256$<hex> and pbkdf2_sha256$<iterations>$<salt>$<hex>. When both ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD and ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH are set the former wins, and both are used only on first boot, while the database has no credential row. /admin opens when ADMIN_ENABLED=true, ADMIN_USERNAME, and ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET all have values, and at least one of ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH / ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD is set (404 = console off, 503 = on but misconfigured, 401 = wrong credentials).

The sign-in URL is http://<host>:8080/admin (through the nginx front door; the app container publishes no host port).

The admin console needs the admin-worker container running alongside it (the background job runner). docker compose up -d starts both.

Important: FHIR_SERVER_SECRET_KEY (or its fallback, ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET) must be identical on the app and admin-worker containers. The worker uses this key to pgp_sym_decrypt external FHIR servers' OAuth tokens and client secrets; if the worker's key is empty or different, background jobs raise Illegal argument to function (empty key) or Wrong key or corrupt data (mismatched key).

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
The admin interface is the React SPA in web-v2/ (Vite + React 19 + Mantine 8). Its static build is served by a dedicated web-v2 container (with its own nginx); the root nginx/nginx.conf routes /admin pages to web-v2, while /admin/api/* and /admin/ws go straight to app. Access control is enforced by the backend API's session cookie (default name tw_health_admin_session, overridable with ADMIN_SESSION_COOKIE); without a session the SPA redirects to /admin/login.

The old Next.js front-end (web/ + web/admin-app/) has been replaced. It is kept only in the compose profile legacy-web for rollback and is not started by default.

The sidebar (web-v2/src/layout/nav.ts) has five sections:

Section Pages (paths relative to /admin) Purpose Overview Dashboard /, Jobs /jobs System status at a glance; the import / embedding / sync job queue, step timeline and live logs (see Jobs & Scheduling). Data Terminology /terminology (per module /terminology/<icd\|loinc\|snomed\|rxnorm>), Drug /drug (drug explorer /drug/explorer), Health supplements /data/health_supplements, Food nutrition /data/food_nutrition Per-module source files, imports, schedules, data preview, embeddings, maintenance mode and clearing; terminology modules also get a browser (see below). FHIR IG library /fhir/ig, FHIR servers /fhir-servers FHIR IG import / dependency packages / removal protection; registration, authentication and health checks for external FHIR R4 servers. Integrations Model endpoints /models, MCP tools /mcp, External services /integrations Provider accounts and profiles for embedding and the analysis LLM; MCP endpoints, tool catalog and playground; OCR (MinerU / Indra), object storage, TFDA, FHIR package registry and worker settings. System Service health /health, Backups & settings /system, Account security /security Infrastructure probes and worker heartbeats; system backups and settings export / import; password and passkeys.

The corresponding backend modules are in node-server/src/admin/*.ts (adminApp.ts is the routing entry point).

Besides passwords, sign-in also supports passkeys / WebAuthn (node-server/src/admin/webauthn.ts), managed on the Account security page (a new password set there must be at least 12 characters, also enforced server-side); passkeys only work over HTTPS on the RP domain (or on localhost for development). See Configuration.

docs.title: MCP tools page (/admin/mcp)
docs.text:
Backed by node-server/src/admin/adminMcp.ts (GET /admin/api/mcp/overview, GET /admin/api/mcp/tools, POST /admin/api/mcp/tools/{name}/invoke), with three tabs:

  • Overview: public endpoints (/mcp, /openapi.json, /tools/{name}, JWKS, OAuth callback), auth mode, server version and copy-ready client configs.
  • Catalog: all 68 tools defined in mcp.ts and whether each is registered; an unregistered tool shows why (gating table and row-count threshold); tools and groups whose module is in maintenance carry a 「維護中」 (under maintenance) badge.
  • Playground: runs any registered tool with pre-filled examples, through the same handler as POST /tools/{name} (rate-limited); while the tool's module is in maintenance the Run button is disabled with the reason shown.

docs.title: Model endpoints (/admin/models)
docs.text:
Embedding and analysis-LLM endpoints are never read from environment variables. They live in these tables (migration 20261016_llm_providers_and_routes.sql):

Table Contents admin.llm_providers Provider accounts: a named account of a provider type (several per type allowed) with URL, credentials and account-wide limits. admin.llm_routes Profiles: a strategy (single / fallback / round_robin / load_balance) over a set of members; kind is analysis or embedding. admin.llm_route_members Members: a model on a provider account (with its own knobs), or another profile (nesting; cycles are rejected). admin.llm_role_routes Which profile each role (analysis / embedding) uses.

The old admin.llm_profiles table was renamed admin.llm_profiles_legacy and is kept for rollback only.

  • Provider adapters: node-server/src/providers/registry.ts registers 24 adapters — OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Mistral, Cohere, Voyage, Jina, DeepSeek, xAI, Groq, OpenRouter, Together, Fireworks, SiliconFlow, DashScope, Moonshot, Zhipu, Volcengine, MiniMax, OpenAI-compatible servers (vLLM, LM Studio, LiteLLM…), Ollama, and ChatGPT. Legacy values vllm / google / azure / claude resolve to the new ids (migration 20261015_llm_provider_registry.sql also rewrites stored rows).
  • ChatGPT sign-in: the chatgpt provider uses OpenAI's "Sign in with ChatGPT" PKCE flow (admin/chatgptOAuth.ts). The redirect can only be a local loopback, so the operator pastes the browser's final URL back into the console to finish the exchange; tokens are stored in admin.llm_providers.oauth and never leave the server.
  • Embedding identity (fingerprint): admin/embeddingIdentity.ts stores the vectors of a fixed set of probe texts as the system's embedding identity (admin.embedding_identity / admin.embedding_fingerprints, defined in db/schema.sql and db/migrations/20261021_embedding_identity.sql; the code also creates them at runtime with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS as a safety net). A new endpoint may join an embedding profile only if every probe reaches cosine ≥ 0.95 — i.e. it is the same model. Switching models while vectors exist goes through a guarded flow: turn the embedding role off → stop embed jobs → wipe vectors (re-typing every *_embeddings vector column in the same transaction when the size changes, e.g. 1024 → 2560) → adopt the new identity → re-queue every module's embed job.
  • No identity row yet, but vectors exist (data loaded by older versions): on the first embedding profile save, role binding, or the Overview button "確認現有向量的模型並建立指紋" (confirm the model of the stored vectors), the system takes a few stored vectors with their source text (verified against source_hash) and asks the role's endpoints, then every other embedding profile's endpoints, then the endpoints being added, to re-embed them; the first one that reproduces them is adopted. An unreachable or 404 endpoint is skipped, never adopted. If none matches, the API answers embedding_identity_unresolved (listing why each endpoint failed) instead of a raw HTTP error.
  • Every error carries a code: model-endpoint failures (profile save, role binding, account / model test, fingerprint check, switch, settings import) answer with code + params; the console translates them into Chinese with the next step and keeps the raw server text in a collapsible "技術細節" (technical details). The main codes are listed under "Changing the embedding model" below.
  • Role-level knobs (embedding timeout / batch size / concurrency, analysis max retries) live in the embedding / analysis groups of admin.app_settings.

docs.title: Changing the embedding model (switch flow)
docs.text:
Editing a profile cannot change the embedding model. Saving a member with another model (or another vector size) is refused (HTTP 409, embedding_model_change_requires_switch) and the console shows a guidance dialog instead: the current model and size, the requested model, how many vectors would be rebuilt and an estimated time, and a "改用切換模型流程" (use the switch flow) button that opens the switch dialog pre-filled with the same account, model and parameters. Binding a profile of a different model to the embedding role behaves the same way.

Switch steps (Model endpoints → Overview → Embedding → "切換模型…"):

  1. Pick the account, model and vector size, then run the pre-check (POST /admin/api/llm/embedding/precheck, no side effects). It calls the new model and reports, before anything is deleted:
    • embedding_model_not_found: the server does not serve that model; the models it does serve are listed and can be picked with one click.
    • embedding_dims_unsupported: the vectors are not the configured size. Without dimensions sent, the model's native size differs (Qwen3-Embedding-4B is 2560); with it sent, the server rejected or ignored it. Two fixes: use the native size, or (Matryoshka models) enable "send dimensions" — vLLM must then be started with --hf-overrides '{"is_matryoshka": true}', otherwise it answers HTTP 400.
    • embedding_switch_same_model: the endpoint already produces the system's vectors — no switch needed, add it to the profile as a fallback.
    • On success it shows the returned size and whether the vector columns will be re-typed (e.g. 1024 → 2560).
  2. With vectors present, type REINDEX and run it. The system shuts the embedding role, stops embed jobs, wipes the vectors and re-types the columns, adopts the new identity, creates and binds a new profile, and queues a rebuild for every module that had vectors. Semantic search falls back to keyword matching meanwhile; ~600k vectors take roughly 1–2 h on a shared GPU (0.6B), about 3 h with the 4B model. When the GPU also serves production's live queries, lower batch_size (e.g. 8) under External services → Embedding before the rebuild and keep concurrency at 1: the smaller the batch, the shorter a single query waits behind one (measured with Qwen3-Embedding-4B: live single-query p95 ≈ 110–170 ms at batch 16, ≈ 80 ms at batch 8). batch_size is read when each job starts, concurrency applies live; a member's rpm caps only the average rate, not the peaks.

Query instruction. The model member's "query instruction" parameter decides whether search queries carry a task description. The default, "auto", prefixes Instruct: <task>\nQuery: <query> for the Qwen3-Embedding family (and gte-Qwen2-instruct) with one English task sentence per module (ICD, LOINC, SNOMED, IG concepts, food, health supplements) and leaves other models alone; it can also be "off" or a custom sentence used for every module (params.query_instruction: absent / off / text). Only query vectors are instructed — stored vectors and the identity-fingerprint probes never are — so changing it needs no re-index.

The Overview's embedding card probes every member of the role (cached 60 s): a failing member shows "Embedding route degraded: member X failing (reason) — failing over to Y" with a fix hint; the Service health page's embedding row uses the same probe.

docs.title: Settings and precedence
docs.text:
Bootstrap variables (DB / Redis / MCP transport / ADMIN_* auth) originate in .env. On first boot, ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD (hashed) or ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH is written into admin.admin_credentials, and subsequent sign-ins validate only against the hash in the database. Seeding uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so once the credential row exists, editing .env or restarting the service never overwrites a working password. Passwords and passkeys are both managed under Account security (/admin/security).

The other external-system settings (MinIO, TFDA base URL, FHIR package registry, worker tuning) are seed-only: .env is read exactly once, on first boot, for keys not yet present in admin.app_settings. Afterwards manage and test them under External services (/admin/integrations); editing .env has no effect on an already-seeded database. TFDA and registry can be edited there (applied hot); MinIO and worker tuning are read-only groups.

OCR settings live in the ocr group of admin.app_settings. They are not seeded from .env and are configured and tested only under External services → OCR: provider mineru (default, external MinerU) or indra (the bundled CPU OCR container ocr-indra, http://ocr-indra:8000), plus an optional fallback provider. Field reference: Drug Service → OCR providers.

Settings export / import (format version 3) under Backups & settings (/admin/system) moves a working configuration between installs: it carries every admin.app_settings group, the provider accounts / profiles / role bindings (keys included), and the passkeys with their RP ID. Older v1 / v2 exports still import. The export contains secrets in the clear — store it like a credential.

docs.title: System backups
docs.text:
The Backups & settings page lets you select settings and credentials, the PostgreSQL database, and MinIO object storage individually. Creating a backup only queues a system_backup background job; the worker streams the PostgreSQL custom dump and the MinIO objects into a ZIP chunk by chunk, then writes it back to the system-backups/ prefix in MinIO with a multipart upload — the whole backup is never assembled in a single HTTP request or in Node's memory. Once finished, it can be streamed down from the backup history through a same-origin API.

Backups contain API keys, login credentials, and medical data, and should be managed as production secrets. The database dump restores with PostgreSQL 16 pg_restore; the object storage files are in the ZIP's object-storage/ directory.

docs.title: Source files
docs.text:
Upload each module's source files in the sources section of its module page (ICD-10-CM CMS order-file zip, ICD-10-PCS, LOINC zip, SNOMED RF2, RxNorm zip, FHIR IG package.tgz, and so on), optionally specifying a source role (such as an IG dependency package or the optional WHO ICD-10 source). The system blocks duplicate uploads by file fingerprint (SHA-256); files are stored in MinIO and fetched back when a job runs.

Content is checked at upload time, so a wrong file is refused right away (with a zh-TW reason): file type (magic bytes); release archives must contain the member the loader needs (LOINC LoincTable/Loinc.csv, SNOMED sct2_Concept_*, RxNorm RXNCONSO.RRF, the ICD-10-CM / PCS order file, UMLS MRCONSO.RRF; archives whose directory cannot be listed, such as zip64, skip this check); CSVs must have their required columns (drug index; LOINC Taiwan mapping loinc_code,name_zh; reference ranges loinc_code,age_min,age_max,gender,range_low,range_high). An IG upload import reads package/package.json first and answers 422 — without creating a job — when the file is not a FHIR package.

When an import job binds its sources, a single-file source role uses its active version; only when the role has no active version does it fall back to the most recent upload.

Uploads must send Content-Type: application/octet-stream (the SPA does), or express's JSON parser intercepts them and returns 413.

docs.title: Terminology browsers
docs.text:
The Terminology module pages and the IG library include read-only browsers backed by GET /admin/api/terminology/* (node-server/src/admin/termViz/):

Browser API prefix Contents ICD-10-CM tree / WHO ICD-10 tree icd/cm/*, icd/who/* Chapter → category → code hierarchy, paths and search ICD-10-PCS axes icd/pcs/* Tables by the first three characters, filtered on axes 4–7 SNOMED CT graph snomed/* Concept neighbourhood (parents / children / attribute relationships) and search LOINC axes loinc/* Six-axis facet filtering, term detail, LA / LP / LL codes RxNorm rxnorm/* Summary, search by TTY, concept detail IG CodeSystem tree ig/codesystem* Concept hierarchy and search for CodeSystems inside an IG package

docs.title: Maintenance mode
docs.text: The drug, icd, loinc, snomed, ig and rxnorm modules can be switched into maintenance mode (POST /admin/api/module-maintenance; state lives in the maintenance group of admin.app_settings), to pause a module's MCP tools while its data is being reloaded or cleared: calls to the tools of a module in maintenance (over /mcp, /tools/* and the admin playground) return error code MODULE_MAINTENANCE immediately (English + Traditional Chinese message), while the tools stay in tools/list (no tool-list churn for clients). The state is cached for 5 seconds, so a toggle takes effect within about 5 seconds. ICD-10 and FHIR Condition follow icd, Drug and FHIR Medication follow drug, Lab follows loinc, FHIR IG follows ig; rxnorm has no tools of its own, so its flag is informational. The module page shows the tools as "paused (under maintenance)" and the MCP tools page marks the tool cards 「維護中」 (under maintenance). The error format is in the API reference.

docs.title: External FHIR servers
docs.text:
Register external FHIR R4 servers on the FHIR servers page, configuring the permitted resource types and operations, OAuth authentication (including private_key_jwt key generation, with the public JWKS hosted at /fhir-client/<id>/jwks.json), the token strategy, and the health check path. After the OAuth Authorization Code callback the browser is sent back to /admin/fhir-servers.

The MCP side consumes them through list_fhir_servers / get_fhir_server_status / crud_fhir_server, with the server handling tokens on the caller's behalf — the caller never touches any secret.

crud_fhir_server is the only tool in the system that can produce a write: write operations require the server's allow-list to permit them and the caller to pass confirm_write=true.

docs.title: Error messages and next steps
docs.text:
Every admin API error response (HTTP ≥ 400) keeps its original error (English) and detail (raw technical text) and also carries:

Field Content code Stable machine code, e.g. SOURCE_MISSING, DB_SCHEMA_OUTDATED, UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE, JOB_ALREADY_ACTIVE message_zh What happened (Traditional Chinese) hint_zh What to do next (which page, which setting, which command)

node-server/src/admin/adminErrorCodes.ts produces them in one place: known English messages first (missing source files, out-of-range settings, OAuth failures…), then the technical cause found in detail (PostgreSQL errors such as a missing table / column → apply the migration, duplicate key, foreign key; connection refused, DNS, timeout, TLS, upstream HTTP status; MinIO). When nothing matches, the message still names the failed operation and gives a generic next step. Responses that already carry a code (model-endpoint API, IG removal, MODULE_MAINTENANCE) are left alone. Toasts show the explanation, then the next step; the raw text appears only as small "技術細節" (technical details).

The same explanations apply to:

  • External services "Test connection" (OCR / MinIO / TFDA): results gain message_zh / hint_zh.
  • Service health probe rows and the dashboard infrastructure status: message_zh / detail_zh + hint_zh.
  • Failed background jobs: last_error_zh / last_error_hint_zh (job detail, and "why the last import failed" on module pages).
  • Gateway errors: when the app does not answer (nginx returns a 502 / 504 HTML page) the console says the backend is not responding and how to check it.

docs.title: DB health gate
docs.text: node-server/src/dbHealth.ts is the central DB health monitor: when PostgreSQL is unreachable, it locks every mutating operation and shows an overlay in the UI, preventing imports or edits while the database is unhealthy.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• node-server/src/admin/adminWorker.ts is a standalone process (the admin-worker compose service, a separate image built from Dockerfile.worker). It polls admin.import_jobs to claim queued jobs, runs the matching load stage, and writes admin.import_job_steps / admin.import_job_logs.
  • node-server/src/admin/adminJobs.ts provides the job API (create / query / cancel / pause) and the execution logic for every job type.
  • node-server/src/admin/adminJobStaging.ts provides the staging / promote mechanism for heavy imports (write to admin.stage_* tables first, then swap atomically in one transaction; each terminology's edition row is written in the same promote transaction).
  • node-server/src/admin/adminSchedule.ts manages schedules (admin.module_schedules); the worker checks next_run_at every ADMIN_SCHEDULE_SCAN_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 60 s) to trigger periodic imports.
  • node-server/src/admin/adminWs.ts pushes live logs and progress to the UI over WebSocket (/admin/ws).

Changing job / loader code means rebuilding the worker too

admin-worker and app are two images. After changing adminJobs.ts, *Service.ts or loaders/*, rebuilding only app leaves the worker running stale code with no error:

bash docker compose build admin-worker && docker compose up -d --no-deps admin-worker

docs.title: Job types
docs.text:
Job type Module Description icd_import / loinc_import / snomed_import / rxnorm_import / ig_import Matching module Imports from source files uploaded through the admin console (source files live in MinIO and are fetched when the job runs). ig_import also downloads missing dependency packages from the FHIR package registry and records each package's install_origin (manual / dependency); it finally indexes the imported packages for the IG concept search and queues ig_embed. health_supplements_sync / food_nutrition_sync Matching module Fetched from the TFDA Open Data API. drug_index_import drug Imports the 36_2.csv license index into drug.licenses and queues enrichment. drug_enrichment drug Crawls the TFDA site for insert / label / appearance assets and uploads them to MinIO. drug_analysis drug Insert PDF → OCR (MinerU / Indra, optional fallback) → analysis LLM → drug.insert_analysis. icd_embed / loinc_embed / snomed_embed / health_supplements_embed / food_nutrition_embed Matching module Backfills the *_embeddings vector tables (needs a usable profile on the embedding role). ig_concept_index ig Builds / backfills the IG concept-search index (CodeSystem names, designations in every language, supplements, linked names, optional UMLS synonyms) and the thesaurus, then queues ig_embed when needed. See IG Concept Search. ig_embed ig Embeds IG concept names (fhir.concept_embeddings, content-addressed, incremental). umls_import ig Optional (UMLS licence): loads UMLS synonyms (fhir.umls_terms) from the source ig/umls_metathesaurus, then queues ig_concept_index. system_backup — System backup (see Admin Console).

All three drug stages run natively in TypeScript (node-server/src/loaders/drugIndex.ts, drugEnrichment.ts, drugAnalysis.ts).

docs.title: Control and concurrency
docs.text:
• Pause / cancel: checkpoint-based — the worker checks admin.job_control_requests at safe points, so a pause never leaves half-written data.
  • Heartbeat: the worker writes admin.worker_heartbeats periodically; after ADMIN_WORKER_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS (default 45 s) without an update it is considered lost and its running jobs are reclaimed and re-queued. On startup the worker also reclaims running jobs left under its own name.
  • Concurrency limit: ADMIN_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS (default 4) bounds how many jobs run at once; per-module resource slots additionally prevent concurrent writes to the same module.

docs.title: Checks before a job is created
docs.text:
POST /admin/api/jobs checks a few preconditions before queueing (node-server/src/admin/jobPrechecks.ts), so problems are reported immediately with a zh-TW explanation instead of failing later in the worker:

  • Duplicate whole-module jobs: icd_import, loinc_import, snomed_import, rxnorm_import, umls_import, ig_concept_index, the two TFDA syncs, every *_embed and system_backup are refused with 409 JOB_ALREADY_ACTIVE (plus active_job_id) while a job of the same type is queued / running / paused. ig_import and the drug jobs are not limited (they can target different packages / licenses).
  • Drug insert analysis prerequisites: drug_analysis (except retry_stage=normalize) and drug_pipeline return 409 when OCR or the analysis LLM is not configured (OCR_NOT_CONFIGURED / ANALYSIS_LM_NOT_CONFIGURED, pointing to External services → OCR or Model endpoints).
  • No live worker: the job is still queued (a worker picks it up once it is back), but the response carries worker_warning and the console says the job will not run yet. Whenever no worker is heartbeating, every page also shows a "background worker offline" banner with the start command.

A failing lookup lets the request through (fail-open); the worker then reports the real error.

The worker's service dependency check before a job runs (e.g. the drug jobs need MinIO, OCR and the analysis LLM) re-probes any service whose last stored probe in admin.service_probes is error, and fails the job (permanent_failed) only if it still fails — once a service is fixed there is no need to run a manual probe on Service health first.

docs.title: Self-healing when the analysis LLM is unavailable
docs.text:
When a drug_analysis job pauses because every profile on the analysis role failed (last_error_code = 'llm_unavailable'), the worker re-claims it automatically once admin.import_jobs.next_retry_at passes; the backoff doubles per attempt (2 min → 30 min cap), and a manual resume skips it. A paused job that a human paused, or whose error code is not llm_unavailable, is never auto-resumed.

A single LLM call times out after 600 s by default, with 3 transport retries; override it per member with the timeout_ms parameter on the model endpoints page.

docs.title: Auto-chaining (drug pipeline)
docs.text:
The three drug stages chain automatically: when drug_index_import completes it queues drug_enrichment, and when that completes it queues drug_analysis.

Jobs created by auto-chaining carry a batch cap, DRUG_AUTOCHAIN_BATCH_LIMIT (default 200 licenses), and re-chain the next batch from their own completion. This drains the backlog gradually while still giving the operator a chance to stop between batches.

Manually queued jobs are not protected by the batch cap

The batch cap only applies to jobs created by auto-chaining. If you manually queue drug_enrichment through the API or UI without specifying a limit, that job processes the entire backlog in one go (potentially tens of thousands of crawls against the TFDA site). Pass an explicit limit when you need to bound it.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: Job progress, the step timeline, and live logs are available on the admin console's Jobs page (/admin/jobs); each module page also lists that module's jobs.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: The system exposes three interfaces, all served through the nginx front door (:8080 by default).

docs.title: HTTP endpoint overview
docs.text:
Endpoint Method Authentication Description /mcp POST / GET / DELETE Optional bearer The MCP streamable-http endpoint (path set by MCP_PATH). /openapi.json GET Optional bearer An OpenAPI 3.1 spec generated dynamically from the currently registered tools. /tools/<tool_name> POST Optional bearer OpenAPI bridge: invoke a single tool with the arguments as a JSON body. /admin/api/* Varies Session cookie Admin console REST API (present only when ADMIN_ENABLED=true). /admin/ws WebSocket Session cookie Live job logs and progress. /fhir-client/<id>/jwks.json GET None Public JWKS for external FHIR OAuth clients. /fhir-oauth/callback GET — OAuth2 Authorization Code callback endpoint.

PUBLIC_TOOLS_AUTH_MODE=bearer protects /mcp, /openapi.json, and /tools/* together. The token is set by PUBLIC_TOOLS_BEARER_TOKEN; cross-origin browser calls additionally require the origin to be listed in PUBLIC_TOOLS_CORS_ORIGINS. none is only suitable for trusted local or private networks.

The backend also has a /health endpoint, but nginx does not proxy it (reaching it through the front door returns 404). To check from the front door whether app is alive, hit /openapi.json instead. Per-module row counts are on the admin console's dashboard; health_check (POST /tools/health_check) also reports module status, server version, build sha and loaded terminology editions.

docs.title: OpenAPI bridge
docs.text:
For clients that cannot speak MCP natively and only connect to OpenAPI tool servers (such as Open WebUI's External Tools).

# Fetch the current tool list
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' http://localhost:8080/openapi.json

# Invoke a tool
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/tools/search_medical_codes \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"keyword": "diabetes", "limit": 3}'

The tool list grows and shrinks with each module's data-load status (row-count thresholds in REQUIREMENTS, exported as MODULE_REQUIREMENTS, in moduleStatus.ts), so the content of /openapi.json differs according to the deployment's data state. mcp.ts defines 68 tools in 12 groups; the FHIR Servers, Clinical Calculators and System groups (15 tools) are always registered. The admin console's MCP tools page (/admin/mcp) shows the full catalog, why each unregistered tool is missing, and a playground for calling registered tools.

A registered tool only means the required source data exists — it does not mean semantic embeddings have been fully backfilled. When vectors are incomplete, the related search falls back to, or mixes in, keyword/BM25. Check each module's embedding count on its page in the admin console and run or schedule the corresponding *_embed job.

docs.title: Maintenance mode
docs.text:
The admin console can switch the icd, loinc, drug, snomed, ig and rxnorm modules into maintenance mode (POST /admin/api/module-maintenance). While a module is in maintenance, calls to its tools (over /mcp, POST /tools/<name> and the admin playground alike) return an isError result immediately, before the tool runs:

{"ok": false, "data": null, "warnings": [],
 "error": {"code": "MODULE_MAINTENANCE", "module": "loinc", "tool": "query_loinc", "retryable": true,
           "message": "Module 'loinc' is under maintenance (data is being updated); query_loinc is temporarily unavailable. Retry later.",
           "message_zh": "模組「loinc」維護中（資料更新中），query_loinc 暫時無法使用，請稍後再試。"}}

POST /tools/<name> returns this JSON with HTTP 200 (like every other tool error). Mapping: ICD-10 and FHIR Condition → icd; Drug / TFDA and FHIR Medication → drug; Lab / LOINC → loinc; SNOMED CT → snomed; FHIR IG (including grounding / completeness) → ig. rxnorm has no tool group of its own, so its flag gates no tool; Health Supplements, Food Nutrition, FHIR Servers, Clinical Calculators and System are never affected. To avoid tool-list churn for clients, tools under maintenance stay in tools/list / /openapi.json. The state is cached for 5 seconds, so a toggle takes effect within about 5 seconds; a failing state lookup fails open.

docs.title: Tool error format
docs.text:
A failed tool call (over /mcp, POST /tools/<name> or the admin playground) tells the calling LLM a code, the reason and the next step (node-server/src/toolErrors.ts). POST /tools/<name> still answers HTTP 400 with the original error: "tool_call_failed", tool and detail, plus:

Field Meaning code e.g. INVALID_ARGUMENTS, UNKNOWN_TOOL, TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE, DATA_NOT_LOADED, SERVER_SCHEMA_OUTDATED, DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE, QUERY_TIMEOUT, INTERNAL_QUERY_FAILED message / hint What went wrong and what to do next (English, for the LLM) retryable Whether retrying unchanged can succeed problems, unknown_parameters, expected_parameters, example_arguments For argument errors: per-parameter problems (parameter, rule, example value), parameters that do not exist (with "did you mean"), the full parameter list and example arguments

SQL / connection errors are no longer passed through to the client (the raw text goes to the server log only). Transport failures against an external FHIR server are classified as UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT, UPSTREAM_DNS_FAILED, UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE, UPSTREAM_TLS_ERROR, UPSTREAM_CONNECTION_RESET or UPSTREAM_AUTH_FAILED. Tool results that find nothing gain hint / suggestions (e.g. nearby ICD codes, concept_found: false, installed_igs when an IG is not found); existing fields are unchanged.

docs.title: health_check (System group)
docs.text:
Always registered, no arguments. Call it before any workflow to confirm the modules you need are online. Returns JSON:

Field Description status ok when the database is reachable, otherwise degraded database / cache ok / error (Postgres query, Redis ping) db_health Snapshot of the DB health monitor (state, healthy, since, last_ok_at, last_error …) services Whether each module meets its registration threshold: icd, drug, health_supplements, food_nutrition, fhir_condition, fhir_medication, lab, ig, snomed version Server version (SERVER_VERSION in toolVersions.ts, currently 1.1.0), same as MCP initialize serverInfo.version build Git sha baked in at image build time (BUILD_SHA build arg); dev when unset tools_version Tools that carry their own version, and those versions (see FHIR IG Tools → Tool versions) lexicon_version / lexicon_sha256 Version and hash of the Taiwan clinical-record lexicon used by grounding terminology Loaded terminology editions, e.g. icd10cm (2026-04-01), icd10 (WHO ICD-10, optional), loinc (2.80), snomed (<module>/<YYYYMMDD>); read from icd.editions, loinc.editions, snomed.editions ig_packages Installed IG packages (package_id#version), default IG first default_ig The default IG (package_id#version), or null when none is set

docs.title: Admin console REST API
docs.text:
Every path starts with /admin/api/ and requires the session cookie (named tw_health_admin_session by default; ADMIN_SESSION_COOKIE renames it). The main endpoints:

Group Endpoints Authentication POST /admin/api/login, POST /admin/api/logout, GET /admin/api/me, /admin/api/passkeys/* (incl. login/options, login/verify, register/options, register/verify), POST /admin/api/privacy/password Overview and health GET /admin/api/overview, GET /admin/api/health, GET /admin/api/services, POST /admin/api/services/probe, GET /admin/api/workers Modules and sources GET /admin/api/modules, GET|POST /admin/api/modules/{key}/clear, GET /admin/api/modules/{key}/versions, GET /admin/api/modules/{key}/preview, POST /admin/api/modules/{key}/schedule/trigger, POST /admin/api/uploads, POST /admin/api/module-sources/{activate,deactivate,delete}, POST /admin/api/module-maintenance Jobs GET|POST /admin/api/jobs, GET /admin/api/jobs/{id}, GET /admin/api/jobs/{id}/{steps,logs}, POST /admin/api/jobs/{id}/{pause,resume,stop,restart} Settings GET /admin/api/settings, POST /admin/api/settings/{group}[/{action}], GET /admin/api/settings/export, POST /admin/api/settings/import (export format v3; v1/v2 files still import) Model endpoints GET /admin/api/llm-providers (provider adapter catalog); /admin/api/llm/accounts[/{id}][/models], POST /admin/api/llm/accounts/test, POST /admin/api/llm/models/test, /admin/api/llm/routes[/{id}][/test], PUT /admin/api/llm/roles, POST /admin/api/llm/oauth/chatgpt/{start,complete} MCP tools GET /admin/api/mcp/overview, GET /admin/api/mcp/tools, POST /admin/api/mcp/tools/{name}/invoke Terminology explorer (read-only) GET /admin/api/terminology/icd/{cm,who}/{children,path,search}, GET /admin/api/terminology/icd/pcs/{browse,table,codes,code,search}, GET /admin/api/terminology/snomed/{concept,children,search}, GET /admin/api/terminology/loinc/{facets,facet-values,term,code}, GET /admin/api/terminology/rxnorm/{summary,search,concept}, GET /admin/api/terminology/ig/{codesystems,codesystem,codesystem/children,codesystem/search} Backups GET /admin/api/backups, GET /admin/api/backups/{job_id}/download; docs.title: Service layer (TypeScript)
docs.text:
The domain services live in node-server/src/. Each offers async initialize(); database access goes through the shared pg pool in db.ts (not a constructor argument), and search services take the shared EmbeddingService in their constructor. mcp.ts creates each one as a lazy singleton; a service that fails to initialise only removes its own tools.

Class File Data IcdService icdService.ts icd.* DrugService drugService.ts drug.* DrugAnalysisService drugAnalysisService.ts drug.insert_analysis (including OCR — MinerU / Indra, ocrProviders.ts — and analysis-LLM calls) HealthSupplementsService supplementsService.ts health_supplements.* FoodNutritionService foodService.ts food_nutrition.* LabService labService.ts loinc.* FHIRConditionService fhirConditionService.ts reads icd.* FHIRMedicationService fhirMedicationService.ts reads drug.* FHIRIGService fhirIgService.ts fhir.* (multi-IG) FHIRServerService fhirServerService.ts admin.fhir_servers SnomedService snomedService.ts snomed.* EmbeddingService embeddingService.ts External embedding endpoint — the route assigned to the embedding role (admin.llm_routes / admin.llm_role_routes over provider accounts in admin.llm_providers) MinIO helper minioService.ts MinIO bucket (drug assets)

docs.title: Related documents
docs.text:
• FHIR Services API
  • Module overview
  • For each service's public MCP tools, see the tool reference.

docs.title: FHIR Services API
docs.text: The three FHIR service classes live in node-server/src/; methods return JSON-serialisable objects.

docs.title: class FHIRConditionService (fhirConditionService.ts)
docs.text: Reads icd.diagnoses directly (through the shared pool in db.ts); it does not depend on another service instance.

docs.title: async createCondition(icdCode, patientId, opts = {})
docs.text: Builds a FHIR R4 Condition from an ICD-10-CM code (system http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10-cm); opts covers clinical / verification status, category, severity, dates and notes. Backs Path A of query_fhir_condition.

docs.title: async createConditionFromSearch(keyword, patientId, opts = {})
docs.text: Searches an ICD code by keyword first, then builds the Condition; applies only clinical / verification status and severity. Backs Path B.

docs.title: validateCondition(condition)
docs.text: Basic structural validation, returns {valid, errors, warnings}. Backs validate_fhir_condition.

docs.title: async createMedication(licenseId, resourceType = "Medication")
docs.text: Builds a Medication or MedicationKnowledge from a TFDA license (CodeSystem https://mcp.fda.gov.tw/fhir/CodeSystem/tfda-license-id), using normalised TFDA data only.

docs.title: async createMedicationFromSearch(keyword, resourceType = "Medication")
docs.text: Searches the drug first, then builds the resource.

docs.title: validateMedication(medication)
docs.text: Basic structural validation, returns {valid, resource_type, errors}. Backs validate_fhir_medication.

docs.title: class FHIRIGService (fhirIgService.ts)
docs.text: The multi-IG profile / terminology / validation / authoring service behind every fhir_* tool. Each method returns a JSON string in the shared envelope {ok, data, warnings, provenance, error?}; package-resolution rules (provenance.resolved_by, NO_DEFAULT_IG, |version) and per-tool parameters are in FHIR IG Tools.

docs.title: ICD Service API
docs.text: IcdService (node-server/src/icdService.ts) backs the MCP ICD-10 tool group. Every method returns a JSON-serialisable object (the MCP tool wraps it as a JSON string in content[0].text). Database access always goes through the shared pg pool in db.ts (via pgBouncer); nothing is injected through the constructor.

docs.title: constructor(embeddingSvc: EmbeddingService | null = null)
docs.text: Takes the shared EmbeddingService; with null the diagnosis search is keyword-only. mcp.ts creates a lazy singleton.

docs.title: async initialize(): Promise<void>
docs.text: Checks whether icd.procedures has rows, which decides whether ICD-10-PCS search is available.

docs.title: async searchCodes(keyword, type = "all", limit = 3)
docs.text: type is "diagnosis" | "procedure" | "all"; limit is capped at 10. Diagnoses use score-aware hybrid ranking of full-text and vector candidates (terminologyRanking.ts + hybridRank.ts; exact vector scan, not HNSW); procedures are BM25 only. Returns {diagnoses?, procedures?, procedures_note?}, plus search_mode: "keyword_only" when vectors are unavailable; {error} when nothing matches. Backs search_medical_codes.

docs.title: async inferComplications(code)
docs.text: Pure hierarchy lookup: with children returns {base_code, potential_complications_or_specifics} (up to 15), otherwise codes of the same category as {message, related_codes} (up to 10). Backs infer_complications.

docs.title: async getNearbyCodes(code)
docs.text: Returns the 2 codes before and the 2 after in alphabetical order as {target, nearby_options}. Backs get_nearby_codes.

docs.title: async browseCategory(category = null, limit = 50)
docs.text: Without category lists every category with counts; with one, expands its codes (limit capped at 200). Backs browse_icd_category.

docs.title: async getConflictInfo(diagnosisCode, procedureCode)
docs.text: Returns full data for one diagnosis and one procedure code side by side — facts only, no verdict. Backs check_medical_conflict.

docs.title: Lab Service API
docs.text: LabService (node-server/src/labService.ts) handles LOINC search, category browsing, reference-range lookup and lab-result interpretation, backing the four tools search_loinc, query_loinc, interpret_lab_result and batch_interpret_lab_results. Database access goes through the shared pool in db.ts; methods return JSON-serialisable objects.

docs.title: constructor(embeddingSvc: EmbeddingService | null = null)
docs.text: Takes the shared EmbeddingService; with null searches are keyword-only.

docs.title: async searchLoincCode(keyword, category = null, limit = 3)
docs.text: Searches candidate LOINC codes by test name, abbreviation or analyte (BM25 + semantic hybrid); category narrows to one LOINC class. Carries search_mode: "keyword_only" when vectors are unavailable.

docs.title: async searchBySpecimen(specimenType, limit = 3)
docs.text: Searches LOINC items by specimen type.

docs.title: async findRelatedTests(component, limit = 3)
docs.text: Finds related LOINC tests for the same analyte, grouped by specimen system (by_system).

docs.title: async listCategories()
docs.text: Lists the LOINC classes available in the database.

docs.title: async getPatientFriendlyName(loincNum)
docs.text: Full concept detail and patient-friendly name for one LOINC code (query_loinc detail mode).

docs.title: async getReferenceRange(loincNum, age, gender = "all")
docs.text: Reference range by age and sex ("M" | "F" | "all") (query_loinc reference_range mode).

docs.title: async interpretLabResult(loincNum, value, age, gender = "all")
docs.text: Interprets one value: returns the range, the measured value and a normal / high / low flag.

docs.title: async batchInterpretResults(results, age, gender = "all")
docs.text:
Interprets an array of {loinc_code, value} in one call — suited to a full lab report.

Reference values are general guidance only and do not replace clinical judgement.

docs.title: Deployment Architecture
docs.text:
graph TD
    User[End User] --> Client[MCP Client / Browser]

    subgraph "Docker Compose Stack"
        NGX["nginx (single front door, :8080 = WEB_PORT)"]
        WEB["web-v2 (nginx + static Vite SPA) — /admin pages"]
        Server["app (Node MCP server + admin REST API, internal :8000)"]
        Worker["admin-worker (Node — imports, embeddings, drug pipeline)"]
        PGB["pgbouncer (transaction mode, :5432)"]
        PG["postgres:16 + pgvector"]
        RD["redis:7 (:6379)"]
        MN["minio (object storage, :9000)"]
        PM["Prometheus metrics (:9090, localhost only)"]
    end

    Client -- "HTTP :8080" --> NGX
    NGX -- "/mcp, /openapi.json, /tools/*, /admin/api/*, /admin/ws, /fhir-client/*, /fhir-oauth/*" --> Server
    NGX -- "/admin pages + everything else" --> WEB
    Server --> PGB --> PG
    Server --> RD
    Worker --> RD
    Server --> MN
    Server --> PM
    Worker --> PGB
    Worker --> MN
    Server -. "Embeddings (query vectors)" .-> Ext[External model endpoints]
    Worker -. "OCR (MinerU) / Analysis LM / Embeddings" .-> Ext
    Worker -. "OCR (Indra, internal network ocr)" .-> OcrIndra["ocr-indra (CPU OCR)"]

docs.title: Key considerations
docs.text:
1. Single entry point: nginx is the only service intended for host access (WEB_PORT, 8080 by default). app only has expose, no ports, so :8000 cannot be reached from the host.
  2. Data persistence: PostgreSQL and MinIO data live in Docker volumes, so the data survives container restarts and needs no re-import.
  3. Transport: always streamable-http (through nginx's /mcp). It is the only transport the server offers; there is no stdio mode.
  4. pgBouncer transaction mode: incompatible with LISTEN/NOTIFY and named prepared statements; the Node side uses pg's unnamed statements for compatibility.
  5. Data imports: triggered from the admin console and executed in the background by admin-worker (there is no longer a standalone data-loader container). Source files are uploaded to MinIO through the admin console and fetched back when a job runs.
  6. MinIO: stores drug document assets (inserts / labels / pill images); the tools return time-limited presigned download links.
  7. External model endpoints: embeddings, OCR (MinerU), and the analysis LLM are all external HTTP services (OCR can instead use the bundled CPU OCR container ocr-indra, which sits on an internal-only network). Embedding and analysis-LLM endpoints live in the provider-account / profile tables (admin.llm_providers, llm_routes, llm_route_members, llm_role_routes) and are configured on the console's Model endpoints page; OCR lives in the ocr group of admin.app_settings and is configured under External services. When unavailable, the system degrades (search falls back to keywords and is stamped search_mode: "keyword_only"; analysis jobs pause and retry automatically, without affecting queries).
  8. Legacy front-end: the Next.js web service is kept only in the compose profile legacy-web for rollback and is not started by default.
  9. Images: app (node-server/Dockerfile), admin-worker (Dockerfile.worker) and web-v2 (web-v2/Dockerfile) are three separate images; job / loader code changes must be rebuilt into admin-worker too.

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text:
Every data import is performed in the admin console and executed in the background by admin-worker (there is no longer a CLI data loader): terminologies under Terminology → , FHIR IGs under FHIR → IG packages, drugs and TFDA open data under Data. Each module page's "Data lifecycle" tab handles source uploads, imports and vector backfills. The "import stage" column below gives the actual admin.import_jobs.job_type value — these are the strings a job is created with. Dataset Version / source How to import Import stage Licensing ICD-10-CM CMS 2026-04-01 ("Code Descriptions in Tabular Order", complete code set incl. 7th characters) Upload the zip → import icd_import Public (bring your own zip) ICD-10-PCS CMS 2025 Upload the zip → import (same job as CM) icd_import Public WHO ICD-10 (optional) tx.fhir.org 2019-covid-expanded (FHIR JSON) Upload the JSON → import (same job as CM) icd_import WHO LOINC 2.80 (Regenstrief) Upload the zip → import loinc_import LOINC license required SNOMED CT International RF2 (currently 20250601) Upload the RF2 zip → import snomed_import SNOMED license required RxNorm (concept reference) NLM Upload RxNorm_full_*.zip → import (for IG ValueSet expansion) rxnorm_import UMLS account required FHIR IG (TWCore and others) MoHW / packages.fhir.org Install from the registry or upload package.tgz; dependency IGs download automatically ig_import Public Drugs (Taiwan FDA / TFDA) TFDA 36_2.csv + online crawl Upload the CSV + crawl and analysis drug_index_import → drug_enrichment → drug_analysis Open data Taiwan health supplements TFDA open data API fetch health_supplements_sync Open data Taiwan food nutrition TFDA open data API fetch food_nutrition_sync Open data

CVX (287 codes), ISO 3166 and UCUM need no import: they ship with the code as built-in tables / a library and are used only by the FHIR validator.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Licensed source files (SNOMED, LOINC, the ICD zips, RxNorm, and so on) must be obtained yourself and uploaded on the corresponding module page. The files actually used are listed in Test data files.
  • The drug domain is a three-stage pipeline (index → online enrichment crawl → OCR/LLM analysis). The TFDA address is set under Integrations → External services (the DRUG_* keys in .env only seed it on first boot); OCR (MinerU or Indra) under Integrations → External services → OCR Server; the analysis LM under Integrations → Model endpoints. See Drug Service.
  • FHIR IG uses a multi-IG (package-scoped) design; declared dependency packages (such as hl7.terminology.r4 and hl7.fhir.r4.core) are downloaded automatically from the FHIR registry — upload one by hand only when the registry cannot supply it. See FHIR IG Service.
  • RxNorm is currently loaded as concept-only reference terminology, used for TTY expansion of FHIR IG ValueSets and for the FHIR validator's RxNorm code / display checks (the import keeps every SAB=RXNORM name of each RXCUI and the release, see migration 20261030_rxnorm_display_names). It does not expose a standalone drug tool.
  • Embeddings: the *_embeddings vector tables are backfilled by each module's separate *_embed job (icd_embed, loinc_embed, snomed_embed, health_supplements_embed, food_nutrition_embed), runnable or schedulable from the module page. The embedding endpoint is configured under Integrations → Model endpoints (provider accounts + an embedding route, stored in admin.llm_providers / admin.llm_routes and related tables, never read from env); when the endpoint is unavailable, search falls back to keyword mode automatically.

Per-source details: ICD-10, LOINC.

docs.title: ICD-10-CM / PCS
docs.text:
• CM (Clinical Modification): used for diagnosis coding.
    • Source: the annual release from the US CMS (Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services) (https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coding-billing/icd-10-codes).
    • Recommended file: the "Code Descriptions in Tabular Order" zip (containing icd10cm_order_YYYY.txt) — the complete code set: header codes plus billable codes including 7th characters / placeholder X (98,186 codes in the 2026-04-01 release). Only with this file is icd.editions.complete true, and only then does the FHIR validator treat unknown ICD-10-CM codes as errors.
    • Also accepted: the "Code Tables, Tabular and Index" zip (icd10cm_tabular_YYYY.xml); 7th characters are expanded, but unknown codes stay warnings.
  • PCS (Procedure Coding System): used for procedure and surgical coding.
    • Source: as above (the flat codes TXT inside the ICD-10-PCS zip).

docs.title: WHO ICD-10 (optional)
docs.text:
• Purpose: lets the FHIR validator check codes and displays of http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10; the ICD lookup tools are unaffected.
  • File: a WHO ICD-10 FHIR CodeSystem or expanded ValueSet JSON, e.g. 2019-covid-expanded (13,831 codes) fetched from tx.fhir.org with node-server/scripts/validator-audit/harness/fetch_tx_terms.py. Written to icd.icd10_who.

docs.title: Taiwan Chinese names
docs.text:
• Source: the Ministry of Health and Welfare's bilingual "Chinese edition of ICD-10-CM/PCS" XLSX (source role icd_zh_tw, optional).
  • Chinese names only fill name_zh; the code set itself always follows the CMS release.

docs.title: File format and import
docs.text:
Upload on the Terminology → ICD-10 page of the admin console, "Data lifecycle" tab; the icd_import stage processes every role in one job:

Source role File Required icd10cm CMS ICD-10-CM zip (order file or tabular XML) Yes icd10pcs CMS ICD-10-PCS zip No (procedure features degrade without it) icd_zh_tw MOHW bilingual XLSX (sheets ICD-10-CM and ICD-10-PCS, code in column A, Chinese name in column D) No icd10_who WHO ICD-10 FHIR JSON No

The import writes staging tables first, then swaps icd.* and writes icd.editions in one promote transaction.

docs.title: International standard
docs.text:
• Authority: the Regenstrief Institute (https://loinc.org/downloads/, account required)
  • Version: LOINC 2.80 (Loinc_2.80.zip).
  • Content: about 105k concepts (laboratory tests and clinical observations) from LoincTable/Loinc.csv, written to loinc.concepts.
  • AccessoryFiles: the import also takes the answer (LA), part (LP), answer-list (LL) and group (LG) codes (loinc.other_codes), per-axis part links, answer lists, panel membership and MapTo replacements (loinc.part_links, loinc.answer_list_items / _links, loinc.panel_items, loinc.map_to), and the release version (loinc.editions). The former are used by the FHIR validator, the structure tables by the LOINC browser in the admin console.

docs.title: Taiwan Chinese mapping
docs.text:
• File: data/loinc/taiwan_mapping.csv (source role loinc_taiwan_mapping, optional), columns loinc_code, name_zh, common_name_zh, specimen_type, unit, about 30 tests common in Taiwan.
  • Curated by the project and downloadable nowhere, so it is kept in version control; the import merges it into the Chinese columns of loinc.concepts.

docs.title: Reference range data
docs.text:
• File: data/loinc/lab_reference_ranges.csv (source role loinc_reference_ranges, optional), about 40 rows stratified by age / sex, written to loinc.reference_ranges.
  • Source: compiled from published material of the NTUH Department of Laboratory Medicine and Taiwanese societies (diabetes, lipid, nephrology) — see each row's source column.
  • Caution: reference values vary slightly between laboratories depending on instruments and reagents. The values this system provides are for general reference only. interpret_lab_result can only interpret codes that have a reference range.

docs.title: Test Data Files
docs.text:
This document records the source files actually used when rebuilding the whole system from scratch: where each file comes from, where it goes, and which module it feeds. The full wipe-and-rebuild on 2026-07-14 (docker compose down -v → up -d --build → re-import every module) followed exactly this list.

fhir-code/ is not in version control at all (the files are large, some are license-restricted, and all of them can be obtained again). This list is therefore the only record of that folder — when moving to another machine, use it to restore the files. The two LOINC mapping tables the project compiled itself, which cannot be downloaded anywhere, live in data/loinc/ under version control (see below).

docs.title: File list
docs.text:
These live under fhir-code/ in the repository root. Only the first 16 characters of each sha256 are listed, enough to confirm you have the same file.

File Size sha256 (first 16) Module / source_role icd/10/icd10cm/icd10cm-table-index-2025.zip 20 MB 7e0fa0cae6348fb6 icd / icd10cm icd/10/icd10pcs/icd10pcs_tables_2025.zip 648 KB 728d9b8f5c315548 icd / icd10pcs icd/10/1.2023年中文版ICD-10-CM_PCS_1131118V3(…).xlsx 7 MB 1bf34d1f92930f29 icd / icd_zh_tw loinc/2.80/Loinc_2.80.zip 74 MB 5a6b10dd6ed29704 loinc / loinc snomed/SnomedCT_InternationalRF2_PRODUCTION_20250601T120000Z.zip 540 MB 3d6c189288e375d4 snomed / snomed_ct rxnorm/RxNorm_full_06032024.zip 241 MB fc612ca0abee8955 rxnorm / rxnorm_full twcoreig/v1.0.0/package.tgz 2.8 MB 2fa1419fa48d1545 ig / ig (only after download) 36_2.csv 44 MB — drug / drug_index_csv (recommended since 2026-10) icd/10/icd10cm/april-1-2026-code-descriptions-tabular-order.zip — — icd / icd10cm (optional, generated by a script) icd10who.json — — icd / icd10_who

ICD-10-CM now uses the CMS order file

icd10cm-table-index-2025.zip (tabular XML) in the table above is the file the 2026-07-14 rebuild used. Since 2026-10 the CMS "Code Descriptions in Tabular Order" zip (2026-04-01 release, containing icd10cm_order_2026.txt, 98,186 codes) is recommended instead: only this complete edition (icd.editions.complete = true) makes the FHIR validator report unknown ICD-10-CM codes as errors. The WHO ICD-10 icd10who.json is fetched from tx.fhir.org with node-server/scripts/validator-audit/harness/fetch_tx_terms.py. Neither is in the local fhir-code/ yet, hence no sha256.

The local loader (without an admin upload) looks for the ICD-10-CM zip in fhir-code/icd/10/icd10cm/ in this order: the ICD_CM_ZIP env var → a CMS order-file zip (name contains order / code-descriptions) → a zip whose name contains table-index / tabular (last by name within each kind) → the legacy default icd10cm-table-index-2025.zip. So dropping the order-file zip into that folder is enough; the old table-index zip can stay.

umls/umls-2024AA-metathesaurus-full.zip (4 GB) is also in the folder, but no import flow currently uses it — skip it when rebuilding.

docs.title: The two LOINC mapping tables kept in version control
docs.text: data/loinc/taiwan_mapping.csv (loinc / loinc_taiwan_mapping) and data/loinc/lab_reference_ranges.csv (loinc / loinc_reference_ranges) were compiled by the project itself (Taiwan lab code mappings and reference values collated from several medical centres) and cannot be downloaded anywhere, so they live under data/ and travel with the repo — not under fhir-code/ (that entire folder stays out of version control). Both roles are optional in the source catalogue, but without them there are no Chinese names or reference ranges (interpret_lab_result cannot interpret anything) — remember to upload them alongside the LOINC zip.

docs.title: Where each file comes from
docs.text:
ICD-10-CM / PCS: the official CMS annual release (for CM, the 2026-04-01 "Code Descriptions in Tabular Order" is recommended) (https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coding-billing/icd-10-codes). The Chinese-name XLSX comes from the MoHW Chinese edition of the ICD-10-CM/PCS mapping file.

LOINC 2.80: the Regenstrief Institute (https://loinc.org/downloads/); requires registering an account to download.

SNOMED CT International RF2: requires an active license (obtainable through an NLM / UMLS account); https://www.nlm.nih.gov/healthit/snomedct/. Not redistributable.

RxNorm Full Release: NLM, requires a UMLS account; https://www.nlm.nih.gov/research/umls/rxnorm/. This project uses it only as concept-only reference terminology (for IG ValueSet expansion), not as a standalone drug tool.

TW Core IG package.tgz: obtain tw.gov.mohw.twcore from https://packages.fhir.org. The import fetches dependency packages recursively and automatically (hl7.terminology, hl7.fhir.r4.core, hl7.fhir.r4.examples, and so on, from packages.fhir.org with packages2.fhir.org as fallback); the 2026-07-14 rebuild ended with 9 packages and roughly 21,000 artifacts in the database — so this one tgz is all you need to prepare. Packages fetched as dependencies are marked install_origin = 'dependency'.

TFDA drug licenses 36_2.csv: not in the repo, and there is no need to place it in fhir-code/ by hand. Download it directly:

curl -L "https://data.fda.gov.tw/data/opendata/export/36/csv" -o drug36.zip
# This is a zip containing 36_2.csv (roughly 44 MB, 71,921 rows, UTF-8 with BOM)

The two other plausible-looking URLs (cacheData/36_2.csv and codedata/datadownload/36) both return 404.

Health supplements and food nutrition need no source file: health_supplements_sync / food_nutrition_sync call the TFDA Open Data API directly.

docs.title: Rebuild procedure
docs.text:
Restore settings (OCR / TFDA / registry addresses, model provider accounts and routes, passkeys) from a settings export (admin console System → Backups & settings, or the API below; the export format is currently v3, and v1 / v2 files still import):

curl -X POST localhost:8080/admin/api/settings/import \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     --data-binary @tw-health-settings-YYYY-MM-DD.json

That export contains API keys and passkeys — keep it out of version control. Keep your own backup.

Upload source files on each module page's "Data lifecycle" tab (or through the API; note the Content-Type: application/octet-stream header, without which express's 4 MB parser intercepts the body):

curl -X POST "localhost:8080/admin/api/uploads?module_key=icd&source_role=icd10cm&filename=april-1-2026-code-descriptions-tabular-order.zip&auto_activate=true" \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
     --data-binary @fhir-code/icd/10/icd10cm/april-1-2026-code-descriptions-tabular-order.zip

Then queue the jobs in order: icd_import, loinc_import, snomed_import, rxnorm_import, ig_import (which needs job_options.object_key, the MinIO object key of that source file), health_supplements_sync, food_nutrition_sync, and drug_index_import.

The drug pipeline chains automatically

A successful drug_index_import auto-chains into drug_enrichment, which then chains into drug_analysis. Enrichment crawls the official TFDA site and analysis calls OCR + an LLM — both cost money and time, and there are over twenty thousand licenses pending. Auto-chaining is now capped at 200 per batch (DRUG_AUTOCHAIN_BATCH_LIMIT) and advances gradually; stop it from the Jobs page if you do not want it to run. For a small-scale check, queue a drug_enrichment with {"limit": 30} yourself.

docs.title: The data volumes this list produces
docs.text:
The actual result after the 2026-07-14 wipe-and-rebuild, usable for checking whether an import completed (the ICD diagnosis count is from the tabular XML used then; with the 2026-04-01 order file it is 98,186 codes):

Module Rows ICD 46,498 diagnoses + 78,948 procedures LOINC 104,672 concepts SNOMED CT 373,972 concepts RxNorm 222,199 concepts FHIR IG 9 packages / 20,996 artifacts Drugs 66,395 licenses Health supplements 565 Food nutrition 1,702

Semantic search needs the *_embed jobs run separately (which need a reachable embedding endpoint, configured under Integrations → Model endpoints, e.g. Ollama). Without embeddings, Chinese keyword search finds almost nothing — Postgres's simple tokenizer treats a whole Chinese product name as a single token, so substring matching fails. This is not a bug; the design relies on vector search to cover it.

docs.title: Deployment Guide
docs.text:
This section explains how to deploy the Taiwan Health MCP server to production. The project is container-first; Docker deployment is strongly recommended for environment consistency.

For the full variable reference see Configuration. This page is the ordered deployment procedure.

docs.title: Supported environments
docs.text:
• Operating system: Linux (Ubuntu/CentOS), macOS, Windows (WSL2)
  • Container platform: Docker Engine 24+ with Docker Compose v2 (docker compose, not the legacy docker-compose)
  • Node.js: 20 or newer (for bare-metal deployment or local development). The project has no Python runtime dependency.

docs.title: Resource requirements
docs.text:
Item Minimum Recommended Notes CPU 2 cores 4+ cores Imports and embedding jobs are the dominant load Memory 8 GB 16 GB+ admin-worker alone is configured with --max-old-space-size=8192 (required by FHIR IG imports) Disk 20 GB 100 GB+ PostgreSQL plus MinIO drug assets (inserts / labels / pill images) grow continuously

The embedding service, OCR (MinerU), and the analysis LLM are all external HTTP services. They are not part of this compose stack — provision them separately and configure them in the admin console. The one exception is the optional CPU OCR container ocr-indra (services/ocr-indra/, Indra OCR): it starts with compose, sits only on the internal ocr network (no route out, no host port), and is used only once External services → OCR sets the provider (or the fallback) to indra; see services/ocr-indra/README.md for the model-licence restrictions.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
docker compose up -d starts the following services:

Service Description nginx The front door (:8080 by default, set by WEB_PORT). Routes /mcp, /openapi.json, /tools/*, /admin/api/*, /admin/ws, /fhir-client/*, and /fhir-oauth/* to app, and everything else (the /admin pages) to web-v2. web-v2 Static build of the admin console SPA (web-v2/, Vite + React + Mantine), served by the container's own nginx. app Node MCP server + admin REST API. Only exposes port 8000 on the compose network; never published to the host. admin-worker Background job runner: every import (including the three-stage drug pipeline) and embedding job. postgres PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector. pgbouncer Connection pool (transaction mode). redis Live event broadcast for the admin console and health probes (tool responses are not cached today). minio + minio-init Object storage for source files, drug assets and system backups, plus bucket initialisation.

The old Next.js front-end web is kept only in the compose profile legacy-web (for rollback) and is not started by default; bring it back with docker compose --profile legacy-web up -d web and restore $th_frontend in nginx/nginx.conf at the same time.

Data imports are triggered from the admin console and run inside admin-worker; there is no longer a standalone data-loader container.

Application traffic goes through nginx only

Never use http://<host>:8000 in documentation or client configuration — app does not publish that port to the host. All application traffic (including MCP) must go through http://<host>:8080.

(postgres and minio do publish ports to the host for operational access; for production see Exposed ports and hardening.)

docs.title: Step 1: Get the code
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/healthymind-tech/Taiwan-Health-MCP.git
cd Taiwan-Health-MCP

docs.title: Step 2: Create .env
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env

The defaults in .env.example must not go straight to production. The following must be handled:

docs.title: 2-1. Required / must-change variables
docs.text:
Variable Why it matters Suggested approach POSTGRES_PASSWORD docker compose fails outright when unset (compose enforces it with :?); app refuses to start while the .env.example placeholder is still in place openssl rand -hex 24 ADMIN_ENABLED Defaults to true (/admin is the only way to import data). Set it to false once the data is loaded, to shrink a public deployment's attack surface As needed ADMIN_USERNAME Admin console account Defaults to admin; customisable ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORDor ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH Without a credential you cannot sign in Pick one, see 2-2 ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET Session cookie signing key — holding it is enough to forge a session for any user, no password involved; also the fallback for FHIR_SERVER_SECRET_KEY. app refuses to start while the .env.example placeholder is still in place openssl rand -hex 32 MINIO_ACCESS_KEY / MINIO_SECRET_KEY Default to minioadmin / minioadmin, effectively no password openssl rand -hex 16 each PUBLIC_BASE_URL Public origin, used to build the OAuth2 redirect_uri and to derive the WebAuthn RP ID https://your-domain.example.com PUBLIC_TOOLS_AUTH_MODE / PUBLIC_TOOLS_BEARER_TOKEN Defaults to none, meaning /mcp and /tools/* are completely unauthenticated Set bearer + openssl rand -hex 32 when publicly reachable WEB_PORT Public port Defaults to 8080; adjust per environment

Generate every random value at once:

echo "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 24)"
echo "ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
echo "FHIR_SERVER_SECRET_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
echo "MINIO_ACCESS_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)"
echo "MINIO_SECRET_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)"
echo "PUBLIC_TOOLS_BEARER_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 32)"

docs.title: 2-2. Set the admin console password
docs.text:
Pick one of two approaches:

(a) Plaintext initial password (simpler) — used only on first boot, when the database has no credential row yet, and ignored forever afterwards:

ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD=your-strong-password

(b) A pre-computed hash:

node -e "console.log('sha256\$' + require('crypto').createHash('sha256').update('change-me').digest('hex'))"

ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH=sha256$$1a2b3c...

When both are set, ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD wins. Password hashes support sha256$<hex> and pbkdf2_sha256$<iterations>$<salt>$<hex>.

Every $ in .env must be written as $$

Docker Compose interpolates variables in .env, so a single $ is read as a variable reference. When the hash starts with a letter (for example sha256$abc…), $abc… is treated as an undefined variable and the value is silently truncated to sha256 — login then fails forever with no obvious error message.

Write every $ as $$ (Compose collapses it back to a single $). A pbkdf2_sha256$...$...$... hash contains several $; double each one. The same applies when the password itself or ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET contains a $.

docs.title: 2-3. Keep the encryption key consistent
docs.text: FHIR_SERVER_SECRET_KEY is the pgcrypto symmetric key for external FHIR servers' OAuth tokens and client secrets, falling back to ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET when unset. compose.yaml passes it to both app and admin-worker, and the two must match — otherwise the worker fails to decrypt with Illegal argument to function (empty key) or Wrong key or corrupt data (mismatched key).

docs.title: 2-4. Know which settings are read only once
docs.text:
Seed-only settings (MinIO, the TFDA crawler, the FHIR package registry, worker tuning) are read from .env exactly once, on first boot, and written into admin.app_settings (seedIfEmpty() inserts key by key with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). Editing .env afterwards has no effect. How changeable they remain, however, differs:

Settings group How to change it after first boot TFDA crawler, FHIR package registry Edit directly under External services (/admin/integrations) in the console (applied hot) MinIO (Storage), Worker Tuning Read-only in the console, labelled "Owned by the deployment (.env / compose)". But since the values were already seeded into the database and the code reads the database, editing .env has no effect either — the only way is a direct UPDATE admin.app_settings followed by a restart of the relevant service. Model endpoints (embedding / analysis LLM), OCR Never read from .env: embedding and the analysis LLM are configured under Model endpoints (/admin/models), OCR under External services → OCR

ADMIN_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS is the exception: it never enters admin.app_settings. The worker reads the environment variable on every start, so editing .env and restarting the worker takes effect.

Set the MinIO credentials before the very first boot

MINIO_ACCESS_KEY / MINIO_SECRET_KEY have two consumers that behave differently:

  • The minio container reads .env on every start for its root credentials (MINIO_ROOT_USER / MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD);
  • app / admin-worker use the copy seeded into admin.app_settings on first boot (seedIfEmpty() writes with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and never overwrites).

Changing .env after the first boot leaves the MinIO server's credentials out of sync with the stored application settings, breaking object storage reads and writes.

Worse, the MinIO group under External services is read-only (labelled "Owned by the deployment (.env / compose)"), so it cannot be fixed from the console. If this has already happened, the only route is the database:

sql UPDATE admin.app_settings SET value = '<new-access-key>' WHERE group_key = 'minio' AND key = 'access_key'; UPDATE admin.app_settings SET value = '<new-secret-key>' WHERE group_key = 'minio' AND key = 'secret_key';

Then restart app and admin-worker.

See Configuration for details.

docs.title: 2-5. A minimal working .env
docs.text:
# --- Public ---
WEB_PORT=8080
PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://taiwan-health-mcp.example.com

# --- Database ---
POSTGRES_DB=taiwan_health
POSTGRES_USER=mcp
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=<openssl rand -hex 24>

# --- MCP ---
MCP_PORT=8000
MCP_PATH=/mcp
PUBLIC_TOOLS_AUTH_MODE=bearer
PUBLIC_TOOLS_BEARER_TOKEN=<openssl rand -hex 32>

# --- Admin console ---
ADMIN_ENABLED=true
ADMIN_USERNAME=admin
ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD=<strong password; write any $ as $$>
ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET=<openssl rand -hex 32>
ADMIN_COOKIE_SECURE=true          # set explicitly when TLS terminates at a proxy
FHIR_SERVER_SECRET_KEY=<openssl rand -hex 32>

# --- Object storage (seed-only: read on first boot) ---
MINIO_ENDPOINT=minio:9000
MINIO_ACCESS_KEY=<openssl rand -hex 16>
MINIO_SECRET_KEY=<openssl rand -hex 16>
MINIO_BUCKET=taiwan-health-drug-assets

docs.title: Step 3: Build and start
docs.text:
BUILD_SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) docker compose build   # builds the app / admin-worker / web-v2 images
docker compose up -d

compose.yaml passes the BUILD_SHA environment variable (default dev) as a build arg to app and admin-worker: app reports it in the build field of the health_check response, and admin-worker records it in its startup log (the build field of Admin worker started). web-v2 does not use it.

On first boot the PostgreSQL container applies db/schema.sql automatically, and minio-init creates the bucket and exits (an exited status is normal).

docs.title: Step 4: Verify
docs.text:
Check container status — postgres / redis / minio / pgbouncer should be healthy:

docker compose ps

Check the services and each module's status:

curl http://localhost:8080/openapi.json | head  # currently registered tools
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/tools/health_check -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'

health_check returns DB / cache / per-module status, the server version, build (git sha), tools_version (per-tool versions), the loaded terminology editions (terminology), the installed IG packages and default_ig.

When startup fails, start with the logs:

docker compose logs -f app admin-worker

docs.title: Step 5: Sign in and configure the model endpoints
docs.text:
Open http://<host>:8080/admin and sign in with the credentials from step 2.

Then configure the external model endpoints (these cannot be set from .env):

Page What it configures Consequence if unset Model endpoints (/admin/models) → Embedding Create a provider account, then an embedding profile bound to the embedding role (e.g. Ollama qwen3-embedding) Search falls back to keyword mode; Chinese keyword search finds almost nothing Model endpoints (/admin/models) → Analysis A profile for the LLM used to extract drug inserts The drug analysis stage cannot run External services (/admin/integrations) → OCR Provider (MinerU address, or indra → http://ocr-indra:8000) and an optional fallback Insert PDFs cannot be OCR'd

Settings can be moved between environments with the settings export / import under Backups & settings (/admin/system). See Admin Console.

docs.title: Step 6: Load data
docs.text:
Import module by module from each module page (Terminology, Drug, Health supplements, Food nutrition, IG library). Licensed source files (ICD-10, LOINC, SNOMED CT, RxNorm, FHIR IG) must be uploaded first; drugs, health supplements, and food nutrition are fetched automatically via API.

A manually queued drug_enrichment is not protected by the batch cap

DRUG_AUTOCHAIN_BATCH_LIMIT (default 200) applies only to auto-chained jobs. A manually queued drug_enrichment with no limit crawls the entire pending queue, issuing tens of thousands of requests against the TFDA site.

For the steps and scheduling see Getting Started and Jobs & Scheduling.

docs.title: Updating and redeploying
docs.text:
When only application code changed, there is no need to restart the whole stack:

git pull
BUILD_SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) docker compose build app admin-worker web-v2
docker compose up -d --no-deps app admin-worker web-v2

admin-worker is a separate image

admin-worker is built by Dockerfile.worker from the same node-server/ source. Changing job / loader code (adminJobs.ts, *Service.ts, loaders/*) but rebuilding only app leaves the worker running stale code with no error.

docs.title: Rollback tags
docs.text:
Before redeploying, tag the images currently running so you can switch straight back if something breaks:

LABEL=rollback-pre-$(date +%Y%m%d)
for svc in app admin-worker web-v2; do
  docker tag taiwan-health-mcp-$svc:latest taiwan-health-mcp-$svc:$LABEL
done

(The image-name prefix is the compose project name; check docker images.) To roll back, re-tag the image as :latest and run docker compose up -d --no-deps <service>. Database migrations do not roll back with the images — back up the database before applying one.

After changing nginx/nginx.conf (a single-file bind mount — edit it in place and reload):

docker compose exec nginx nginx -s reload    # or: docker compose restart nginx

Containers only need recreating when a bootstrap variable in .env changed (DB / Redis / MCP / ADMIN_*):

docker compose up -d

(Changing the seed-only block has no effect; see 2-4.)

docs.title: Database migrations
docs.text:
