db/schema.sql is applied automatically on first boot. Existing environments must apply the incremental changes under db/migrations/ themselves, in filename date order:

docker compose exec -T postgres \
  sh -c 'psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1' \
  < db/migrations/20261020_loinc_structure.sql

Migrations added in 2026-10 (apply in order; all are folded into db/schema.sql):

File Contents 20261015_llm_provider_registry.sql Data only: rewrites legacy provider values to registry ids (vllm → openai_compatible, google → gemini, …) 20261016_llm_providers_and_routes.sql Adds admin.llm_providers / llm_routes / llm_route_members / llm_role_routes, migrates the old rows, renames admin.llm_profiles to admin.llm_profiles_legacy 20261017_icd10cm_complete_edition.sql Complete ICD-10-CM edition: short_name_en, is_header columns and icd.editions 20261018_terminology_completeness_v4.sql LOINC LA/LP/LL/LG codes and loinc.editions, SNOMED inactive concepts / descriptions, first_released, snomed.editions, WHO ICD-10 (icd.icd10_who) 20261019_ig_install_origin.sql fhir.ig_packages.install_origin / installed_for 20261020_loinc_structure.sql LOINC axis part links, answer lists, panels and MapTo tables 20261021_embedding_identity.sql admin.embedding_identity / admin.embedding_fingerprints (embedding identity; the code also creates them at runtime, so applying it is idempotent either way) 20261022_ig_concept_search.sql IG concept search: fhir.concept_index_cs / _concepts / _terms, fhir.concept_embeddings, fhir.term_thesaurus, fhir.codesystem_supplements. Afterwards press "補建索引" in admin → IG packages → 術語搜尋索引 (ig_concept_index, followed by ig_embed) 20261023_umls_terms.sql Optional UMLS synonym store fhir.umls_terms / fhir.umls_release (needs a UMLS licence; the engine works without it)

After 20261017, 20261018 and 20261020, re-import the matching modules (ICD, LOINC, SNOMED CT) to fill the new tables.

To apply all of them in order (drop the ones already applied yourself — the project has no built-in migration version tracking):

for f in $(ls db/migrations/*.sql | sort); do
  echo "applying $f"
  docker compose exec -T postgres \
    sh -c 'psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1' < "$f"
done

Credentials are expanded inside the container

The $POSTGRES_USER / $POSTGRES_DB above are expanded inside the container (which is why the whole command is wrapped in a single-quoted sh -c), so nothing needs exporting or substituting on the host.

Connect to postgres directly, not pgbouncer

Run migrations through the postgres container. pgBouncer runs in transaction mode and is unsuitable for DDL batches.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
Two approaches:

(a) Admin console (recommended) — Backups & settings (/admin/system) lets you select settings and credentials, the PostgreSQL database, and MinIO object storage. It queues a system_backup background job; the resulting ZIP is written back to the system-backups/ prefix in MinIO and can be downloaded from the backup history.

(b) Manual:

# PostgreSQL (custom format, for pg_restore)
docker compose exec -T postgres \
  sh -c 'pg_dump -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" -Fc' > backup-$(date +%F).dump

# MinIO objects (volume level)
docker run --rm -v taiwan-health-mcp_minio_data:/data -v "$PWD":/backup \
  alpine tar czf /backup/minio-$(date +%F).tar.gz -C /data .

The volume name is prefixed with the compose project name (the directory name by default); confirm the actual name with docker volume ls.

Backups contain API keys, login credentials, and medical data — treat them as production secrets.

docs.title: Exposed ports and hardening
docs.text:
Ports compose.yaml currently publishes to the host:

Service Port Binding Production recommendation nginx ${WEB_PORT} → 80 All interfaces Put a TLS reverse proxy in front postgres 5432 All interfaces Rebind to 127.0.0.1:5432:5432 or remove minio 9000 All interfaces Rebind to 127.0.0.1:9000:9000 or remove minio console 9001 127.0.0.1 Leave as is redis 6379 127.0.0.1 Leave as is app metrics ${METRICS_PORT} 127.0.0.1 Leave as is

Pre-launch checklist:

  • POSTGRES_PASSWORD, ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET, and FHIR_SERVER_SECRET_KEY are all strong random values
  • MinIO credentials no longer use the minioadmin defaults
  • postgres:5432 / minio:9000 rebound to 127.0.0.1 or blocked by a firewall
  • PUBLIC_TOOLS_AUTH_MODE=bearer with a high-entropy token (if /mcp is publicly reachable)
  • TLS terminates at a front proxy and ADMIN_COOKIE_SECURE=true
  • .env permissions tightened (chmod 600 .env) and kept out of version control

Override the port bindings with docker-compose.override.yml instead of editing compose.yaml:

services:
  postgres:
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
  minio:
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:9000:9000"

The same override file is a good home for resource limits.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Fix docker compose up fails immediately with POSTGRES_PASSWORD is required The variable is unset in .env Set it (compose enforces it with :?) /admin returns 404 ADMIN_ENABLED was set to false Set it back to true and run docker compose up -d /admin returns 503 Enabled, but the auth variables are incomplete Check the missing field in the startup log, fill them in and restart The admin password is correct but login fails $ in .env was not written as $$, truncating the hash See the warning box in 2-2 Changing the password in .env has no effect The credential was written to admin.admin_credentials on first boot, and seeding uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING Change it under Account security (/admin/security) instead The worker raises Illegal argument to function / Wrong key or corrupt data FHIR_SERVER_SECRET_KEY is empty, or differs between app and the worker See 2-3 Changing TFDA / registry settings in .env has no effect That group is seed-only, read only on first boot Change it under External services (/admin/integrations) Changing MinIO / worker tuning in .env has no effect Seed-only, and read-only in the console UPDATE admin.app_settings directly, then restart the service (see 2-4) Chinese search returns almost nothing No embedding endpoint configured, so search fell back to keyword mode Configure an embedding profile under Model endpoints (/admin/models) The worker OOMs during an IG import NODE_OPTIONS was lowered, or the container memory limit is too small Keep --max-old-space-size=8192 and give the container a 10G limit http://<host>:8000 is unreachable By design — app publishes no host port Always use http://<host>:${WEB_PORT} A change to job / loader code has no effect Only app was rebuilt; admin-worker still runs the old image docker compose build admin-worker && docker compose up -d --no-deps admin-worker

docs.title: Isolated staging stack
docs.text:
deploy/staging/compose.yaml is a stack fully isolated from production (compose project twh-staging): its own Postgres, Redis, MinIO, app, admin-worker and web-v2. The web-v2 container is the front door (its nginx proxies the backend via BACKEND_UPSTREAM), published on ${STAGING_PORT:-8090}; the entry point is http://<host>:8090/admin/.

Before starting it, create an untracked deploy/staging/.env containing at least:

Variable Purpose STAGING_DB_PASSWORD Staging Postgres password (compose fails without it) STAGING_MINIO_PASSWORD Staging MinIO root password (compose fails without it) STAGING_RESTORE_DIR Host directory holding the production DB dump, mounted read-only at /restore in Postgres (compose fails without it) STAGING_HOST / STAGING_PORT Optional; used to build PUBLIC_BASE_URL, default port 8090 
BUILD_SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) docker compose -p twh-staging -f deploy/staging/compose.yaml up -d --build

Notes:

  • app / admin-worker also read the root .env (env_file) and then override the DB / Redis / MinIO connections with staging values.
  • Staging runs over http, so it sets ADMIN_COOKIE_SECURE=false and uses its own cookie name, ADMIN_SESSION_COOKIE=tw_health_admin_session_staging — cookies are scoped per host, not per port, so on a shared host production's Secure cookie of the default name would shadow it and loop the staging login.
  • Postgres mounts the host directory ${STAGING_RESTORE_DIR} read-only at /restore for restoring a production dump; after restoring, disable the inherited jobs / schedules and model endpoints so staging does not compete with production for external resources.

docs.title: Architecture & Container Deployment
docs.text: Infrastructure topology, container composition, and the startup sequence.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The full parameter reference, covering bootstrap variables (.env) and seed-only settings (managed under External services in the console after first boot).

docs.title: Performance & Monitoring
docs.text:
Optimisation advice for high-concurrency scenarios, connection pool and cache strategy, and Prometheus monitoring.

The public pages moved out of this repo

The public-facing marketing and legal pages (/, /status, /privacy, /dpa) are now served by a standalone marketing-site project, not by this repo's front-end. /privacy is the URL registered with the Anthropic Connectors Directory, so once the new site is live, add the 301 redirects in nginx/nginx.conf (a TODO block is in place).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The system is configured through two layers: environment variables and database settings (admin.app_settings, plus the model-endpoint tables admin.llm_providers / llm_routes / llm_route_members / llm_role_routes). Copy .env.example to .env and edit it:

cp .env.example .env

docs.title: Settings precedence (important)
docs.text: Category Stored in Notes Bootstrap variables .env only DB / Redis / MCP transport / ADMIN_* auth / WEB_PORT. These must be known before startup and never enter the database. Seed-only settings .env → admin.app_settings MinIO, the TFDA crawler, the FHIR package registry, worker tuning, and so on. Read exactly once, on first boot, for keys that do not yet exist, to seed the database; editing .env has no effect on an already-seeded database. TFDA and registry settings can then be managed under External services (/admin/integrations) in the console (applied hot); MinIO and worker tuning are read-only groups in the console, so changing them later requires a direct UPDATE admin.app_settings and a service restart. Model endpoints Database only Embedding and the analysis LLM live in the provider-account / profile tables (admin.llm_providers etc.) and are configured under Model endpoints (/admin/models); OCR (MinerU / Indra and the fallback) lives in the ocr group of admin.app_settings and is configured under External services → OCR. Never read from environment variables; movable between environments with the settings export / import (v3) under Backups & settings (/admin/system).

docs.title: Public port
docs.text:
Variable Default Description WEB_PORT 8080 The port the nginx front door publishes to the host. This is the system's only public entry point.

The app container only exposes MCP_PORT (8000) on the internal network and never publishes it to the host. Clients always connect to http://<host>:${WEB_PORT}.

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text: Variable Default Description POSTGRES_PASSWORD Required PostgreSQL password (compose fails outright when unset) POSTGRES_DB taiwan_health Database name POSTGRES_USER mcp Database user DATABASE_URL Composed by compose postgresql://<user>:<pass>@pgbouncer:5432/<db>. Only needs setting by hand when running outside Docker.

docs.title: Redis
docs.text: Variable Default Description REDIS_URL redis://redis:6379/0 (set by compose; the program's own default is redis://localhost:6379/0) Redis connection URL

docs.title: MCP transport
docs.text: Variable Default Description MCP_HOST 0.0.0.0 Listen host (HTTP mode) MCP_PORT 8000 Container-internal listen port. Never published to the host. MCP_PATH /mcp HTTP endpoint path PUBLIC_TOOLS_AUTH_MODE none Authentication mode for the public MCP / OpenAPI bridge: none or bearer. bearer is recommended in production. PUBLIC_TOOLS_BEARER_TOKEN empty The token required in bearer mode; use a high-entropy random value. PUBLIC_TOOLS_CORS_ORIGINS empty Permitted browser origins (comma-separated). * is not allowed in bearer mode; empty means no cross-origin browser calls are permitted.

docs.title: Application and monitoring
docs.text: Variable Default Description LOG_LEVEL INFO DEBUG | INFO | WARNING | ERROR METRICS_PORT 9090 Prometheus metrics endpoint (bound to 127.0.0.1 only)

docs.title: Admin console authentication
docs.text:
Variable Default Description ADMIN_ENABLED true Mounts /admin. Accepts true/1/yes/on and false/0/no/off; anything else aborts startup ADMIN_USERNAME admin Operator account ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH empty sha256$<hex> or pbkdf2_sha256$<iterations>$<salt>$<hex> ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD empty A plaintext initial password, used only on first boot while the database has no credential row: it is hashed into admin.admin_credentials once and ignored forever afterwards. Takes precedence over ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH when both are set. The plaintext is never persisted. ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET empty Session cookie signing key ADMIN_SESSION_TTL_MINUTES 240 Session lifetime ADMIN_SESSION_COOKIE tw_health_admin_session Session cookie name (letters, digits, _, -, . only). Isolates several stacks on one host (cookies are scoped per host, not per port); staging uses tw_health_admin_session_staging. ADMIN_COOKIE_SECURE empty (automatic) true / false. When empty, the cookie's Secure attribute is added if PUBLIC_BASE_URL uses HTTPS. Set it explicitly to true when TLS terminates at an external proxy and no public URL is configured. ADMIN_MAX_UPLOAD_MB 512 Source file upload cap FHIR_SERVER_SECRET_KEY empty (falls back to ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET) pgcrypto symmetric key for external FHIR servers' OAuth tokens and client secrets. Must be identical on app and admin-worker, or the worker's decryption raises Illegal argument to function (empty key) or Wrong key or corrupt data (mismatched key).

/admin opens (adminReady()) when ADMIN_ENABLED=true, ADMIN_USERNAME, and ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET all have values, and at least one of ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH / ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD is set.

Generating a password hash (Node):

node -e "console.log('sha256$' + require('crypto').createHash('sha256').update('change-me').digest('hex'))"

Write every $ in .env as $$

Docker Compose interpolates variables in .env, so a single $ is read as a variable reference and the hash value is silently truncated (especially when the digest starts with a letter). Write every $ as $$; Compose collapses it back to a single $.

docs.title: Passkeys / WebAuthn (optional)
docs.text:
Variable Default Description PUBLIC_BASE_URL empty The public origin (scheme://host), used to build the OAuth2 redirect_uri and to derive the WebAuthn RP ID. When empty it is derived from the request's Host header. WEBAUTHN_RP_ID The host of PUBLIC_BASE_URL, falling back to taiwan-health-mcp.gugulu.tw The registrable domain the admin console is served from WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME Taiwan Health MCP — Admin The name shown in the OS passkey prompt WEBAUTHN_ORIGIN https://<WEBAUTHN_RP_ID> Allow-list of expected origins (comma-separated)

compose.yaml passes all four variables to app. A production deployment should at least set PUBLIC_BASE_URL; set WEBAUTHN_* only when the derived values need overriding.

docs.title: Seed-only settings (managed under External services in the console after first boot)
MinIO (drug assets)
docs.text: Variable Default MINIO_ENDPOINT minio:9000 (use localhost:9000 outside Docker) MINIO_ACCESS_KEY minioadmin MINIO_SECRET_KEY minioadmin MINIO_BUCKET taiwan-health-drug-assets MINIO_SECURE false MINIO_PRESIGN_TTL_SECONDS 3600

docs.title: Drug / TFDA crawler
docs.text: Variable Default Description DRUG_TFDA_BASE_URL https://mcp.fda.gov.tw TFDA site base URL DRUG_HTTP_TIMEOUT 30 Per-request HTTP timeout (seconds) DRUG_CRAWLER_CONCURRENCY 4 Crawler concurrency DRUG_AUTOCHAIN_BATCH_LIMIT (env var, not seeded) 200 The licenses each follow-on job processes when auto-chaining (index → enrichment → analysis). Applies only to auto-chained jobs; a manually queued job without a limit processes the entire pending queue. DRUG_ANALYSIS_PROMPT_PATH (env var, not seeded) <repo>/src/prompts/drug/analysis_prompt.txt Path to the analysis LLM's system prompt (lets a container say where the repo is mounted; not meant for swapping the prompt)

docs.title: Background worker tuning
docs.text: Variable Default (program) Description ADMIN_WORKER_NAME admin-worker Worker identifier (used for heartbeats and job claiming) ADMIN_WORKER_POLL_SECONDS 3 Queue poll interval ADMIN_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS 15 Heartbeat interval ADMIN_WORKER_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS 45 No heartbeat for longer than this counts as lost ADMIN_RECLAIM_INTERVAL_SECONDS 60 How often lost jobs are checked for reclaim ADMIN_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS (env var, not seeded) 4 Maximum concurrent jobs (per-module resource slots apply on top). Read from the environment on every worker start — not stored in admin.app_settings. ADMIN_SCHEDULE_SCAN_INTERVAL_SECONDS (env var, not seeded) 60 Schedule scan interval NODE_OPTIONS --max-old-space-size=8192 (set by compose on the worker) IG imports load whole dependency packages — do not lower this.

docs.title: Source file paths for local development
docs.text:
In production, source files are uploaded to MinIO through the admin console; the variables below only specify file locations when running a loader locally.

Variable Default FHIR_CODE_DIR <repo>/fhir-code ICD_CM_ZIP / ICD_PCS_ZIP / ICD_XLSX The matching files under fhir-code/icd/10/... (without ICD_CM_ZIP the CMS order-file zip is preferred; see Test data files) LOINC_ZIP_PATH fhir-code/loinc/2.80/Loinc_2.80.zip LOINC_MAPPING_CSV / LOINC_RANGES_CSV The mapping tables under data/loinc/ SNOMED_ZIP fhir-code/snomed/SnomedCT_InternationalRF2_PRODUCTION_*.zip RXNORM_ZIP fhir-code/rxnorm/RxNorm_full_*.zip IG_TGZ fhir-code/twcoreig/**/package.tgz

docs.title: Image build arguments
docs.text: Argument Applies to Description BUILD_SHA node-server/Dockerfile (app), Dockerfile.worker (admin-worker) Git sha; app reports it in the build field of health_check, admin-worker records it in its startup log. compose.yaml passes it from the environment variable of the same name, dev when unset. Usage: BUILD_SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) docker compose build app admin-worker.

docs.title: streamable-http (production, recommended)
docs.text:
Claude Desktop:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "taiwan-health": {
      "url": "http://<host>:8080/mcp",
      "transport": "streamable-http"
    }
  }
}

With PUBLIC_TOOLS_AUTH_MODE=bearer, clients must send an Authorization: Bearer <PUBLIC_TOOLS_BEARER_TOKEN> header. The console's MCP tools page (/admin/mcp) offers copy-ready client configs.

docs.title: Recommended resource limits (production)
docs.text:
Add resource limits in docker-compose.override.yml:

services:
  app:
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2G
  admin-worker:
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 10G     # needed by IG imports, matching NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192
  postgres:
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4G
  redis:
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512M

docs.title: Advanced pgBouncer settings
docs.text:
pgBouncer is configured through the edoburu/pgbouncer image's environment variables. The important ones (see compose.yaml):

Parameter Value Description POOL_MODE transaction Release the connection after each transaction MAX_CLIENT_CONN 500 Up to 500 client connections DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE 30 Up to 30 PostgreSQL connections MIN_POOL_SIZE 5 Pre-warmed connections AUTH_TYPE scram-sha-256 Authentication method IGNORE_STARTUP_PARAMETERS extra_float_digits Driver compatibility setting

docs.title: Startup speed
docs.text:
The system connects to PostgreSQL directly at server startup; the data is pre-loaded, so no ETL runs on each boot.

  • First deployment: terminology data must first be imported from the admin console's module pages (Terminology etc.) — roughly 1 minute for ICD, 5–15 minutes for SNOMED CT.
  • Subsequent starts: the service connects straight to PostgreSQL and starts within seconds.
  • Initialisation model: the Node server creates the connection pool, Redis, and each service exactly once at process start (main() in node-server/src/server.ts); each MCP session holds its own transport but shares these process-level singletons. (The old Python mcp SDK's lifespan-per-session problem no longer exists.)

Recommendation: make sure the PostgreSQL data volume is persistent (compose.yaml sets this up by default) so the loaded terminology data survives.

docs.title: Query performance
docs.text:
• pgBouncer connection pool: transaction mode, 500 client connections mapped onto 30 PG connections, for high concurrency.
  • Redis cache (not in use today): node-server/src/cache.ts provides cached(ttl, prefix) — a Redis-backed, fail-open memoizer (on a cache error the function simply runs) — but no service or tool calls it yet, so every tool call hits PostgreSQL. Wrapping a hot read path in cached() is the intended way to add caching.
  • FTS indexes: every major search column has a PostgreSQL Full-Text Search index.
  • Vector search: the *_embeddings tables use pgvector. ICD semantic search deliberately bypasses the HNSW index with an exact scan (ORDER BY (embedding <=> …) + 0): the ~50k near-duplicate 7th-character codes make HNSW recall collapse, and the exact scan over ~98k rows takes about 0.35 s.
  • pg driver: uses unnamed prepared statements to stay compatible with pgBouncer transaction mode.

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text:
The MCP server is implemented in Node.js (Express + @modelcontextprotocol/sdk). To handle heavy request volumes:

  1. Tune pgBouncer's MAX_CLIENT_CONN (default 500) and DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE (default 30).
  2. Watch pool usage through Prometheus (mcp_db_pool_size / mcp_db_pool_checked_out).
  3. Multiple container instances can share one PostgreSQL and one Redis.

docs.title: Background jobs
docs.text:
• ADMIN_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS bounds how many jobs admin-worker runs at once (4 by default in compose); per-module resource slots additionally prevent parallel imports of the same module.
  • The worker's NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 is necessary: IG imports load whole dependency packages (such as hl7.fhir.r4.examples) into memory. Do not lower it.
  • On a memory-constrained host, avoid running several large imports at once (e.g. SNOMED CT and an IG); an idle worker may also retain gigabytes of heap, so restarting it before a large import can help.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
The Prometheus metrics endpoint is /metrics on METRICS_PORT (9090 by default, bound to 127.0.0.1 only). node-server/src/metrics.ts defines:

Metric Type Status mcp_db_pool_size / mcp_db_pool_checked_out Gauge Updated periodically by the DB stats collector mcp_tool_requests_total{tool,status} / mcp_tool_duration_seconds{tool} Counter / Histogram Recorded on every tool call (MCP, POST /tools/<name> and the admin playground share one dispatch point, withToolMetrics in mcp.ts). Labels are only the tool name and status (success / error; a throw or an isError result counts as error) — arguments are never recorded; calls rejected by argument validation before reaching the handler are not counted mcp_cache_operations_total{prefix,result} Counter Increments only when cached() is used; it currently has no call site

docs.title: Development
docs.text: Thank you for your interest in contributing to Taiwan Health MCP. This section helps new developers get familiar with the project structure and development workflow quickly.

docs.title: Project structure at a glance
docs.text:
Path Contents node-server/ The entire backend (Node.js / TypeScript): MCP server, admin REST API, background worker, and all data loaders. node-server/src/*Service.ts The domain services (icdService.ts, drugService.ts, labService.ts, snomedService.ts, fhirIgService.ts, …). node-server/src/mcp.ts MCP tool registration (tool groups and input schemas). node-server/src/server.ts Entry point: the HTTP surface (/mcp, /openapi.json, /tools/*) and process initialisation. node-server/src/admin/ Admin console backend (adminApp.ts routing, adminJobs.ts jobs, adminWorker.ts background worker, adminSettings.ts settings, …). node-server/src/loaders/ Per-module loaders (icd.ts, loinc.ts, snomed.ts, rxnorm.ts, ig.ts, drug*.ts, embeddings.ts, …). node-server/src/admin/termViz/ Read-only API behind the admin terminology browser (/admin/api/terminology/*: ICD tree, PCS axes, SNOMED graph, LOINC axes, RxNorm, IG CodeSystem tree). node-server/src/providers/ Model provider adapters (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible servers, ChatGPT sign-in … 24 in all), used by the embedding and analysis-LLM routes. node-server/src/grounding/ Deterministic record-faithfulness engines (fhir_check_grounding, fhir_check_completeness). node-server/scripts/validator-audit/ Tools and audit report (REPORT.md) comparing the built-in FHIR validator with HL7 validator_cli 7.0.1. web-v2/ The production admin console: a static Vite + React + Mantine SPA served by its own nginx container (compose service web-v2), mounted at /admin/. web/ The old Next.js admin console (web/admin-app/), replaced by web-v2/; the compose service web only starts under the legacy-web profile and is kept for rollback only. db/ schema.sql and migrations/. src/prompts/ LLM prompts read at runtime (drug analysis). This is the only thing left under src/. data/loinc/ Hand-curated LOINC mapping tables that cannot be re-downloaded from anywhere. docs/ The MkDocs documentation source (this site).

The project has no Python runtime dependency; there is no backend code outside node-server/.

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
# Backend
cd node-server
npm install
npm run build          # tsc -> dist/
npm run dev            # tsx watch src/server.ts
npm run typecheck
npm test

# Admin console front-end (web-v2)
cd web-v2
npm install
npm run dev            # vite, http://localhost:5173/admin/, API proxied to ADMIN_BACKEND (default http://127.0.0.1:8090)
npm run typecheck      # tsc -b --noEmit
npm run build          # outputs dist/

For the full stack use Docker: docker compose up -d (see Getting Started). To redeploy after code changes: docker compose build app web-v2 && docker compose up -d --no-deps app web-v2. admin-worker is a separate image (Dockerfile.worker); rebuild it too whenever job / loader code changes: docker compose build admin-worker && docker compose up -d --no-deps admin-worker.

docs.title: Code Style
docs.text: Naming, comments, and coding conventions (code and comments are written in English).

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: How to run the tests (npm test) and perform end-to-end verification.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Pull request conventions and code review standards.

docs.title: Adding a new service
docs.text:
1. Create node-server/src/<name>Service.ts (a class whose constructor takes a pg.Pool and which offers async initialize()).
  2. Instantiate it in the startup sequence in server.ts (a failing service must degrade gracefully without affecting the others).
  3. Add a tool registration function in mcp.ts (input schemas defined with zod) and register it in the appropriate tool group.
  4. For availability driven by data-load status, add the table and minimum row count to REQUIREMENTS in moduleStatus.ts (exported as MODULE_REQUIREMENTS), and wrap the group's registration in mcp.ts in if (status.<key>).
  5. If the tool's output is pinned by fixtures, register its version in TOOLS_VERSION in toolVersions.ts, and bump it whenever its output for the same input changes.

docs.title: Code Style
docs.text: Code and comments in this project are always written in English; user-facing documentation is bilingual, in Traditional Chinese and English (see Docs Site Maintenance).

docs.title: TypeScript (node-server/, web-v2/)
docs.text:
• Format: ESM ("type": "module"). In node-server/ (TypeScript 5.7+, compiled by tsc) relative imports must carry the .js extension (matching the compiled output); web-v2/ (TypeScript 5.9, bundled by Vite) imports through the @/ path alias, without extensions.
  • Naming: files in camelCase (drugService.ts, adminJobs.ts); types and classes in PascalCase; functions and variables in camelCase.
  • Types: annotate parameter and return types on public functions. Avoid any; when unavoidable, note why.
  • Validation: MCP tool input schemas are defined with zod.
  • Logging: always go through logger.ts (logInfo / logWarning / logError), which writes structured JSON to stderr. Never write to stdout — that channel belongs to the MCP stdio transport.
  • Database: loaders take a pg.Pool and follow the existing batchInsert pattern in that file.

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
Comments explain why, or record constraints the code itself cannot express; they should not restate what the next line does.

Quirks deliberately preserved during the Python → Node migration for value-for-value behavioural parity all carry a comment explaining which behaviour they replicate and what breaks if it changes (for example pick() / dictGet() in drugRecordBuilder.ts, whose output is persisted as normalized_records.normalized_json). Do not "tidy these up" in passing.

docs.title: Import rules (important)
docs.text:
Bulk imports follow "fetch everything first, then write atomically":

  1. Complete the entire network phase first (fetch all the data back).
  2. Then write inside a single transaction (TRUNCATE / UPSERT).
  3. Deduplicate the source data before inserting (TFDA Open Data occasionally has duplicate primary keys).

Never interleave HTTP fetches with database writes inside a transaction.

docs.title: Commits
docs.text: Follow Conventional Commits: feat:, fix:, refactor:, docs:, chore:. Keep subjects short and specific; describe in the PR what changed, the related issue, any data or schema impact, and the testing evidence.

docs.title: Pull request process
docs.text:
1. Fork the project to your GitHub account.
  2. Create a new branch: git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
  3. Commit your changes: git commit -m "feat: Add new drug search filter"
  4. Push the branch: git push origin feature/your-feature-name
  5. Open a Pull Request on GitHub.

docs.title: Commit message convention
docs.text: Please follow Conventional Commits: - feat: a new feature - fix: a bug fix - docs: documentation changes - refactor: code refactoring (no behavioural change)

docs.title: Documentation changes
docs.text: The docs site is bilingual. Every page exists as both <page>.md (Traditional Chinese) and <page>.en.md (English), and both must be updated in the same commit. See Docs Site Maintenance.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Backend tests use Node's built-in test runner (node --test), executing TypeScript directly through tsx.

The old pytest suite (tests/test_*.py) was removed along with the Python backend; there are no Python tests left in the repository.

docs.title: Running the tests
docs.text:
cd node-server
npm install
npm test          # node --import tsx --test 'src/**/*.test.ts' (node expands the glob: any depth)

Type checking (worth running before every commit):

cd node-server
npm run typecheck # tsc -p tsconfig.dev.json --noEmit

cd ../web-v2
npm run typecheck # tsc -b --noEmit

web-v2/ has no test suite — only typecheck.

CI does not run tests

The only GitHub Actions workflow is deploy-docs.yml (builds and publishes MkDocs when docs/ or mkdocs.yml changes on main). Nothing blocks a merge on a failing npm test / npm run typecheck — run both locally in node-server/ and web-v2/ before committing.

docs.title: Current test coverage
docs.text:
Test files sit beside the code they cover (node-server/src/**/*.test.ts). There are currently 61 test files with 721 test cases (2026-10-17; npm test takes about 40 s), by area:

Area Test files (under node-server/src/) FHIR validator / IG / terminology fhirValidator.test.ts, fhirValidatorV2.test.ts, fhirValidator.v6.test.ts, fhirIg.test.ts, fhirCodeSystem.test.ts, fhirExternalTerminology.test.ts, fhirPath.test.ts, fhirRequiredElements.test.ts, fhirTestKit.test.ts Grounding groundingTools.test.ts, grounding/*.test.ts Model providers and routing providers/*.test.ts, admin/llmRouting*.test.ts, admin/llmErrorCodes.test.ts, admin/embeddingIdentity*.test.ts, admin/chatgptOAuth.qa.test.ts, embeddingService*.test.ts, analysisLlmClient*.test.ts, drugAnalysisService*.test.ts, rateLimiter.qa.test.ts Loaders loaders/icd.test.ts, loaders/loinc.test.ts, loaders/ig.test.ts, loaders/igRegistry.test.ts, loaders/embeddings.test.ts, loaders/batchPool.test.ts, loaders/drugRecordBuilder.test.ts, loaders/drugImageVariant.test.ts Admin backend admin/adminAuth.test.ts, admin/adminJobs.test.ts, admin/adminMcp.test.ts, admin/mcpToolExamples.test.ts, admin/igDependencies.test.ts, admin/igOrigin.test.ts, admin/igRemoval.test.ts, admin/termViz/termViz.test.ts, admin/fhirServerService.test.ts, admin/publicToolsSecurity.test.ts, admin/draftTarget.test.ts, admin/drugAssetResponse.test.ts Other clinicalCalculators.test.ts, config.test.ts

*.qa.test.ts files are QA regression tests; npm test runs them with the rest.

Some parity tests (fhirRequiredElements.test.ts, grounding/completeness.test.ts, and others) read a fixture directory that is not in version control; when it is absent those cases are reported as skipped, not failed.

The item-by-item comparison of the FHIR validator with the official HL7 validator_cli 7.0.1 is not part of npm test: it is a separate harness in node-server/scripts/validator-audit/ (it needs a database with the IG packages loaded); results are in that directory's REPORT.md.

The tests remain pure unit tests: no Postgres, Redis or MinIO is started, so write new tests against injected / faked collaborators. During the Python → Node migration most behaviour was verified by differential runs (feeding the same input to both implementations and comparing the output field by field); please add tests alongside new functionality.

docs.title: Writing a new test
docs.text:
Create <name>.test.ts next to the module under test, using Node's built-in node:test and node:assert:

import { test } from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";

test("parses a LOINC row", () => {
  assert.equal(actual, expected);
});

docs.title: End-to-end verification
docs.text:
Against a running environment, you can issue requests to the tool surface directly (through the nginx front door, :8080 by default):

# Currently registered tools (varies with each module's data-load status)
curl http://localhost:8080/openapi.json

# Invoke a single tool
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/tools/search_medical_codes \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"keyword": "diabetes", "limit": 3}'

# Server version, build (git sha), per-tool versions and loaded terminology editions
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/tools/health_check -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'

The admin console's Integrations → MCP tools page also offers a tool catalogue and a playground, which invokes tools exactly like POST /tools/<name>.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: The questions users most commonly hit while using Taiwan Health MCP.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Missing data, keyword search techniques, and so on.

docs.title: LOINC
docs.text: Questions about LOINC code mapping and reference values.

docs.title: Q: Why are some tools missing?
docs.text: A: Module-backed tools are enabled and disabled automatically according to data-load status. If the corresponding module has not been imported (or has not reached the row-count threshold), its tools are not registered. Check each module's status with health_check first (services), or import the module from its page in the admin console. The tool catalogue under Integrations → MCP tools in the admin console also shows whether each tool is currently registered, and why not.

docs.title: Q: Why do search results look keyword-only rather than semantic?
docs.text: A: Semantic / hybrid search needs a reachable embedding endpoint (for example Ollama). The endpoint is configured in the admin console under Integrations → Model endpoints (provider accounts + an embedding route, stored in admin.llm_providers / admin.llm_routes and related tables) — not through environment variables. When it is unset or unreachable, search falls back to keyword mode and the response carries a keyword_only signal. Note also that each module's vectors must be backfilled by its *_embed job first; otherwise you get keyword-only results even with a working endpoint.

docs.title: Q: A FHIR IG tool returns NO_DEFAULT_IG?
docs.text: A: The call passed no package_id, no canonical argument identified an owning package, and no default IG is set (with more than one manually installed IG). Set a default IG under FHIR → IG packages in the admin console, or pass package_id. The package actually used is reported in the response's provenance.resolved_by.

docs.title: Q: Installation and deployment questions?
docs.text: A: See Getting Started and the Deployment Guide.

docs.title: Q: FHIR format and validation questions?
docs.text: A: For basic Condition / Medication conversion see FHIR Tools; for profile- and terminology-level authoring and validation see FHIR IG Service.

docs.title: Q: Why does one test (glucose, say) have several LOINC codes?
docs.text: A: LOINC distinguishes very precisely between specimen (serum vs whole blood), timing (fasting vs post-prandial vs random), and method. Always pick the most precise code for your institution's actual testing workflow. Using a generic code (such as "glucose, timing unspecified") can lead to misinterpretation during exchange.

docs.title: Q: What if I cannot find a particular LOINC code?
docs.text: A: 1. Try searching by the English scientific name. 2. The test may be an emerging one that LOINC has not yet coded. 3. The item may be part of a panel — try searching for the panel name.

docs.title: Q: Why can't I find some newly launched drugs?
docs.text: A: The system's drug data depends on the Taiwan FDA's open dataset. If the FDA has not yet updated the dataset, the system cannot return the drug. We synchronise the latest data periodically.

docs.title: Q: Why can't I find foreign products when searching health supplements?
docs.text: A: The system only includes health supplements certified with the "Little Green Man" mark issued by Taiwan's Ministry of Health and Welfare. Detailed lookup is not currently offered for products bought overseas or supplements without Taiwanese registration.

docs.title: Q: Can I look up traditional Chinese medicine diagnosis codes?
docs.text: A: The system currently focuses on ICD-10-CM (Western medicine) coding. ICD-10-CM extension codes used in traditional Chinese medicine, and traditional TCM coding schemes, are not yet supported.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text: Welcome to the Taiwan Health MCP guides. This section offers task-oriented tutorials that help you combine tools to solve real medical or health problems.

docs.title: Lab Result Interpretation
docs.text: How to use the system to interpret biochemistry lab reports and understand the clinical meaning of abnormal values.

docs.title: LOINC Integration Guide
docs.text: For healthcare IT staff: how to use the system to standardise in-house codes to LOINC.

docs.title: Lab Result Interpretation Guide
docs.text: This guide helps users understand how to use the lab module to interpret laboratory data.

docs.title: Foundation: LOINC codes
docs.text: Before interpreting anything, the most precise approach is to work from LOINC codes, because the same test (glucose, say) can have different specimen sources (whole blood, plasma, urine) or measurement methods. This system supports LOINC first and foremost.

docs.title: Example: interpreting a health check-up report
docs.text:
Suppose you receive a check-up report with several flagged values: 1. Fasting glucose: 110 mg/dL 2. Triglyceride: 180 mg/dL 3. Total cholesterol: 240 mg/dL

The patient is a 55-year-old man.

docs.title: Step 1: Determine the LOINC codes (if the report does not supply them)
docs.text:
Tool call:

search_loinc(mode="code", keyword="空腹血糖")
# Returns: 1558-6 (Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --Fasting)

search_loinc(mode="code", keyword="三酸甘油酯")
# Returns: 2571-8 (Triglyceride [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma)

docs.title: Step 2: Interpret a single value
docs.text:
Analyse each of these values.

Tool call:

interpret_lab_result(loinc_code="1558-6", value=110, age=55, gender="M")

Result: The tool picks the reference interval that applies to the age / sex (fasting glucose is 70–100 mg/dL in data/loinc/lab_reference_ranges.csv) and returns result.flag = "H", status = "偏高 (High)", the interval and its source, and a generic sentence ("above the normal reference value; further evaluation advised"). The tool does not diagnose: a clinical reading such as impaired fasting glucose (pre-diabetes) is for the caller (the LLM) or a clinician to make from the result.

docs.title: Step 3: Batch interpretation
docs.text:
To analyse the whole report at once.

Tool call:

batch_interpret_lab_results(
    results_json='[
        {"loinc_code": "1558-6", "value": 110},
        {"loinc_code": "2571-8", "value": 180},
        {"loinc_code": "2093-3", "value": 240}
    ]',
    age=55,
    gender="M"
)

Result: The tool returns total_tests, abnormal_count, normal_count and the per-item interpretations (all three are H). Tests without a reference range are skipped and not counted. An overall risk assessment (for example a metabolic-syndrome concern) is likewise left to the caller or a clinician.

docs.title: LOINC Integration Guide (for IT / developers)
docs.text: This guide is written for hospital information system (HIS) developers and data engineers, explaining how to map in-house lab codes to standard LOINC codes.

docs.title: Why LOINC?
docs.text: Hospitals commonly use their own codes (such as GLU-AC), but exchanging data between institutions or uploading to a health passbook requires a common language. LOINC is that standard.

docs.title: 1. Build a mapping table
docs.text:
Use the search_loinc(mode="code", ...) tool to find the standard code that best matches each in-house item.

Comparing the key attributes: When choosing a LOINC code, confirm that these six axes agree: 1. Component: the analyte (such as glucose) 2. Property: the measured property (such as mass concentration) 3. Time aspect: the timing (such as Pt = point in time, or 24H) 4. System: the specimen type (such as serum/plasma or urine) 5. Scale: the measurement scale (such as quantitative) 6. Method: the measurement method (a method-less code is acceptable when it does not affect interpretation)

Using the tool:

# Search for "urine protein"
search_loinc(mode="code", keyword="Urine Protein")
# The results distinguish qualitative from quantitative

Operators can also use the "Data preview" tab on Terminology → LOINC in the admin console to filter by the six axes and inspect a single term's parts, answer lists, panels and MapTo (the LOINC structure tables behind it are loaded by loinc_import).

docs.title: 2. Verify the reference ranges
docs.text: Once mapped, use query_loinc(mode="reference_range", ...) to confirm that the standard reference values for that LOINC code are close to the in-house laboratory's. A large discrepancy may mean the wrong code was chosen (for example a code with different units or a different measurement method).

docs.title: 3. Automate the conversion
docs.text: In the exporter module: 1. Read the in-house lab result. 2. Convert it to LOINC via the mapping table. 3. Call or consult query_loinc(mode="reference_range", ...) to fill in standard reference range information (where in-house data is missing). 4. Package it as a FHIR Observation resource.

docs.title: Common issues
docs.text: • Unit conversion: LOINC usually has a default unit (such as mg/dL). If the hospital uses mmol/L, convert the numeric value during the transformation.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The drug service integrates Taiwan FDA (TFDA) western-medicine license data, providing drug search, pill appearance identification, drug details, and download links for official document assets (package inserts / carton labels / pill images). The data is built around TFDA's standard license index and progressively enriched by a multi-stage pipeline.

docs.title: 1. Drug search (search_drug)
docs.text:
Four search modes are supported:

  • drug_name: search by Chinese or English drug name (for example「普拿疼」or "acetaminophen").
  • ingredient: search by ingredient text.
  • license_id: exact lookup by license number (for example「衛署藥製字第000480號」or the numeric ID).
  • atc_code: search by ATC classification code (for example "N02BE01").

include_cancelled optionally includes revoked licenses; limit defaults to 3 with a maximum of 10.

docs.title: 2. Pill identification (identify_unknown_pill)
docs.text: Matches space-separated appearance keywords (colour, shape, score line, imprint, size, engraving) by intersection to help identify an unknown tablet. English colour and shape terms are expanded through a built-in synonym table — for example "white round" or "白 圓形".

docs.title: 3. Drug details (get_drug_details)
docs.text: Returns the normalized drug record for a single license, assembled from normalized JSON stored in PostgreSQL, along with the current availability and document counts for each stage.

docs.title: 4. Document asset links (get_drug_asset_links)
docs.text: Returns persisted asset metadata and generates presigned MinIO download links on the fly. The asset_group values are insert (electronic package insert), label (carton label), shape (pill image), and analysis (analysis output).

docs.title: Data pipeline (three stages)
docs.text:
Drug data is built by three import stages, triggered and monitored from the drug page of the admin console (executed in the background by admin-worker):

  1. drug_index_import — loads the license index from TFDA's standard 36_2.csv, creating drug.licenses and the other base tables.
  2. drug_enrichment — crawls TFDA for electronic inserts, document assets, and pill appearance records, storing the files in MinIO.
  3. drug_analysis — runs OCR (MinerU or Indra, see OCR providers below) and the analysis LM over the insert documents, extracting structured content into drug.insert_analysis. OCR is configured in the admin console under Integrations → External services → OCR Server (stored in the ocr group of admin.app_settings); the analysis LM under Integrations → Model endpoints (provider accounts + routes: admin.llm_providers / admin.llm_routes / admin.llm_route_members / admin.llm_role_routes). Neither is ever read from environment variables.

A drug_pipeline job type also exists: one job that runs all three stages per license. The three stages auto-chain as well: each auto-chained job is capped at DRUG_AUTOCHAIN_BATCH_LIMIT (200 by default); a manually queued drug_enrichment with no limit is not capped and will crawl the entire backlog.

docs.title: OCR providers
docs.text:
drug_analysis sends each insert PDF to OCR for Markdown and hands that to the analysis LLM; the LLM stage does not depend on which OCR provider ran. Choose under External services → OCR:

Provider Runs where Notes mineru (default) External HTTP service (POST {base_url}/file_parse), usually on a GPU box Most robust on complex tables and layouts. Settings: base URL, backend, effort, parse method, language, timeout. indra The bundled ocr-indra compose container (POST http://ocr-indra:8000/ocr), CPU only Indra OCR (indra-ocr 0.3.2, ONNX Runtime, ~18 MB of models baked into the image — no internet needed at runtime). Reads a digital PDF's text layer directly and OCRs only scanned pages. Settings: Indra base URL, timeout, DPI (72–400), mode (auto / ocr / text).
  • Fallback provider (fallback_provider: none / mineru / indra): tried once when the primary is unreachable, returns an HTTP error, times out or produces empty output; not tried when the file itself is unreadable (encrypted, corrupt, not a PDF). drug.insert_analysis.ocr_provider records the provider that actually produced the Markdown.
  • Service health: with a fallback configured both are probed; one side down is degraded (does not block jobs), only both down is error.
  • Test connection: for Indra it also OCRs the built-in sample PDF, proving Markdown really comes back.
  • Indra limitations: occasional misreads of rare Traditional Chinese characters on scanned pages; merged cells and ruling-less key/value tables can land in the wrong columns.
  • Indra model licence: the code is Apache-2.0, the weights are under a modified OpenRAIL-M licence — not usable by an entity with more than US$20M gross revenue in the prior year or more than US$20M total funding (except personal / research use), or one offering a product that competes with Datalab; the restrictions extend to the OCR output. Read the licence section of services/ocr-indra/README.md before enabling it.

docs.title: Technical architecture
docs.text:
• Data source: Taiwan FDA western-medicine licenses (mcp.fda.gov.tw), configured via DRUG_TFDA_BASE_URL.
  • Database: the drug schema, with tables including licenses, ingredients, atc, electronic_inserts, appearance_records, assets, asset_variants, insert_analysis, and normalized_records, plus import-state tracking tables (import_runs, import_license_state, enrichment_queue, and so on).
  • Object storage: insert / label / pill-image files are stored in MinIO, and the tools generate time-limited presigned links at response time.
  • Search: drug search is keyword matching (ILIKE substring + simple full-text search); there is no vector / semantic search and no drug_embed job.
  • Admin UI: the admin console's Data → Drugs page shows the pipeline overview, takes 36_2.csv uploads, and schedules and runs jobs; the drug explorer (/admin/drug/explorer) shows a single license's inserts, appearance, files, history and LLM calls.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: • FHIR Medication Service: generates FHIR Medication / MedicationKnowledge resources from this module's drug data.

docs.title: Key limitations
docs.text:
• Insert OCR + LLM analysis is machine-generated and must be reviewed by a clinician.
  • drug_enrichment and drug_analysis require reachable TFDA / OCR (MinerU or ocr-indra) / analysis-LM endpoints.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This module converts local ICD-10 diagnosis data into Condition resources conforming to the HL7 FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) R4 standard. It is a key component for healthcare interoperability, ensuring Taiwan's diagnosis records can connect with international health information systems.

docs.title: 1. ICD-10 to FHIR Condition
docs.text: Automatically wraps structured ICD-10 data into a FHIR JSON object: - Code conversion: maps ICD-10-CM codes correctly into the Condition.code.coding field. - System identification: fills in the standard system URI (http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10-cm) automatically. - Text description: carries over the standard ICD-10 disease name.

docs.title: 2. Attribute configuration
docs.text: Supports setting the full range of Condition resource attributes: - Clinical status: set the clinical status (such as active, resolved, remission). - Verification status: set the verification status (such as confirmed, provisional). - Category: distinguish an encounter diagnosis from a problem list entry. - Severity: annotate severity (mild, moderate, severe). - Patient link: associate the resource with a specific Patient resource (subject).

docs.title: 3. Dates and notes
docs.text:
• Onset date: record when the condition began.
  • Recorded date: record when the data was entered.
  • Notes: supports adding unstructured clinical notes.

docs.title: Example resource structure (JSON)
docs.text:
{
  "resourceType": "Condition",
  "clinicalStatus": {
    "coding": [
      {
        "system": "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/condition-clinical",
        "code": "active"
      }
    ]
  },
  "code": {
    "coding": [
      {
        "system": "http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10-cm",
        "code": "E11.9",
        "display": "Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications"
      }
    ]
  },
  "subject": {
    "reference": "Patient/example"
  }
}

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
1. EMR exchange: exchanging patient diagnosis records between hospitals.
  2. Health passbook integration: formatting clinical data for upload to a personal health management platform.
  3. Insurance claim automation: insurers receiving standardised diagnosis data for adjudication.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The FHIR IG service is a general, IG-scoped toolset built on top of the multi-IG fhir.* data store. It lets an LLM explore installed Implementation Guides, read profiles (StructureDefinition) and terminology (ValueSet / CodeSystem), perform terminology validation, and produce and validate profile-conformant FHIR R4 resources through a "skeleton-fill" approach. The default IG is TWCore v1.0.0, but multiple IGs can be installed and switched between.

Every tool accepts an optional package_id + version, and responses use a shared envelope: {ok, data, warnings, provenance, error?}.

docs.title: How the target package is resolved
docs.text:
When not stated explicitly, a tool picks the IG package in this order and records the outcome in provenance.resolved_by:

  1. explicit_version: a canonical argument (or meta.profile) carries |version and an installed package holds that version — there is no silent fallback to another version;
  2. package_arg: the caller passed package_id (+ version); latest: package_id without a version → that package's highest release;
  3. meta_profile: no package_id — the package owning the resource's meta.profile (validation tools);
  4. canonical_owner: no package_id — the package owning a canonical argument (profile / ValueSet / system);
  5. default_ig: the default IG;
  6. sole_manual_ig: no default IG is set and exactly one IG was installed manually.

If none applies the error code is NO_DEFAULT_IG (no arbitrary package is picked). Versions compare by SemVer 2.0 precedence (FHIR labels such as -ballot, -snapshot1, -cibuild are pre-releases); |version matches by the HL7 rule (exact, else the highest of the same major.minor, else a wildcard). Declared dependencies that are not installed are listed in data.deps_missing; when one package appears at several versions in a closure, provenance.closure_versions shows which one canonical lookup uses.

docs.title: 1. IG discovery
docs.text:
• fhir_list_igs: lists installed IG packages with packageId, version, title, canonical, fhirVersion, status, isDefault, and declared dependencies. Use this first to pick an IG when several coexist.
  • fhir_get_ig: details for a single IG, including identity, dependencies, and artifact counts per resource type.
  • fhir_list_artifacts: lists an IG's conformance artifacts in summary form (StructureDefinition / ValueSet / CodeSystem / examples…), filterable by resource_type or grouping_id.
  • fhir_search_artifacts: full-text search over artifacts by id, canonical URL, name, title, or description.

docs.title: 2. Profile selection and reading
docs.text:
• fhir_list_resource_profiles: lists the IG's selectable resource profiles (constraint StructureDefinitions), grouped by the base resource type they constrain (for example Patient → Patient-twcore).
  • fhir_rank_resource_profiles: ranks candidate profiles by how well the source field keys you intend to populate match each profile's element paths. This tool is advisory only — the response carries selectionRequired:true, and you must still make the final choice; it never maps automatically.
  • fhir_get_profile: summary of a single profile / StructureDefinition (identity, base definition, derivation, element count). Resolvable by artifact id, canonical URL, or artifact_key; canonicals defined by dependency IGs resolve transitively.
  • fhir_get_profile_required_elements: every element the profile effectively requires (min≥1 under required ancestors, required slices, choice types, invariant-implied value-or-dataAbsentReason, plus target-implied primary content), each row classified by where its value comes from (auto / coding / source_fact / workflow_default) with a fill hint. verbosity=compact (default) or full; an optional instance (draft) makes the min≥1 children of optional parents it populates required too. Call it before writing a resource so every required field is filled.
  • fhir_get_profile_elements: reads the structural truth of a profile snapshot (cardinality, types, bindings, slicing, choice[x], constraints). One tool offers several view values: elements, element, slices, choices, binding, examples.

docs.title: 3. Terminology / ValueSet
docs.text:
• fhir_get_valueset: retrieve a ValueSet definition summary.
  • fhir_expand_valueset: expand a ValueSet and list the actual member codes.
  • fhir_lookup_code: look up a single code's display name and properties in a given CodeSystem.
  • fhir_validate_code: validate whether a system+code belongs to a given ValueSet.
  • fhir_normalize_code: match free text (for example「流行性感冒」/ influenza) against a ValueSet or code system and return ranked candidate codes. For CodeSystems of installed IGs (e.g. the NHI payment codes) it uses the IG Concept Search engine.

docs.title: 4. Authoring, assembly, and validation
docs.text:
• fhir_get_resource_skeleton: generate a "skeleton" resource from a profile — an empty draft containing only required / mustSupport structure, for filling in step by step.
  • fhir_finalize_resource: finalise a draft against its profile, completing the structure and returning the full resource.
  • fhir_resolve_reference: resolve resource references by temporary key, so resources can link to each other inside a Bundle.
  • fhir_build_bundle: assemble several resources into a Bundle of type transaction, collection, and so on.
  • fhir_validate_resource: validate a single resource against the profile named in meta.profile (structure + terminology bindings).
  • fhir_validate_bundle: validate a whole Bundle (each entry against its meta.profile, plus reference integrity inside the Bundle).
  • Both validation tools report how complete the check was: checked_fully, profiles_unchecked, valuesets_unchecked (valid keeps the HL7 meaning; a profile or ValueSet that could not be checked is flagged rather than silently passed). The optional source_text / site_config / evidence_map parameters add grounding issues; without them the output is identical to the output before grounding existed.

docs.title: 5. Record faithfulness (grounding — deterministic, no LLM)
docs.text:
• fhir_check_grounding: checks a Bundle against the source clinical record text — every populated clinical fact and code must be supported by the record (evidence map or auto-locate), with date / number / unit / identifier / dose / frequency normalisation and section, negation and history rules; issues come back in the fhir_validate_bundle shape.
  • fhir_check_completeness: a gap report — compares the facts the conversion targets require (profile-required plus target-implied elements) with what the record states, and returns the missing items, the record lines that state absence, a template clarification question and a ready insufficient_information object.

source_text is clinical data: the server never logs its content (only its SHA-256). Per-tool versions live in node-server/src/toolVersions.ts and are reported by health_check under tools_version.

docs.title: Technical architecture
docs.text:
• Data source: FHIR IG packages (package.tgz), installed from the package registry or uploaded as a tgz on the FHIR → IG packages page of the admin console (import stage ig_import). Declared dependency IGs (such as hl7.terminology.r4 and hl7.fhir.r4.core) are downloaded automatically from the FHIR registry (default https://packages.fhir.org, falling back to https://packages2.fhir.org; the registry address is set under Integrations → External services) and each is indexed as a package-scoped IG, so cross-system ValueSet bindings expand to real codes. Upload a dependency by hand only when the registry cannot supply it.
  • Install origin: fhir.ig_packages.install_origin records whether a package was installed by an operator (manual) or fetched to satisfy another IG's dependencies (dependency), and installed_for records which IG pulled it in (migration 20261019_ig_install_origin.sql); manual is sticky on re-import. The IG page lists missing dependencies and dependencies nothing uses any more.
  • Deletion protection: removing a package that another installed IG depends on (directly or transitively), or removing the default IG, is refused by default; the operator must name a new default (new_default) or pass force explicitly (recorded in the audit log).
  • Database: the fhir schema — ig_packages, codesystems, concepts, and artifacts (all package-scoped, supporting multiple IGs). The IG detail view in the admin console can browse the concept tree of a CodeSystem inside an IG (/admin/api/terminology/ig/*).
  • Validation engine: fhirValidator.ts / fhirTerminology.ts / fhirSnapshot.ts / fhirReference.ts / fhirAuthoring.ts perform snapshot generation, terminology binding checks, reference resolution, and skeleton-fill authoring in process. The rules are benchmarked against HL7 validator_cli 7.0.1 + tx.fhir.org, compared item by item over a corpus (audit record: node-server/scripts/validator-audit/REPORT.md). Offline terminology: ICD-10-CM / WHO ICD-10 (icd.*), LOINC (including LA/LP/LL/LG), SNOMED CT (including inactive content), RxNorm, CVX (built in, 287 codes, version 20250715), ISO 3166 (built in, version 2018), and UCUM (grammar check with @lhncbc/ucum-lhc; if the library cannot load, the code is reported unchecked, never invalid).

docs.title: Suggested authoring workflow
docs.text:
1. fhir_list_igs → select the target IG (when necessary).
  2. fhir_list_resource_profiles / fhir_rank_resource_profiles → pick a profile.
  3. fhir_get_profile_elements (choices / binding / slices) → understand the structure and terminology constraints.
  4. fhir_get_profile_required_elements → confirm the required elements; fhir_get_resource_skeleton → get the skeleton and fill fields in step by step (use fhir_normalize_code / fhir_validate_code for coding as needed).
  5. fhir_finalize_resource → finalise; assemble multiple resources with fhir_resolve_reference + fhir_build_bundle.
  6. fhir_validate_resource / fhir_validate_bundle → validate (pass source_text when the source record is available, or call fhir_check_grounding / fhir_check_completeness).

docs.title: Key limitations
docs.text:
• In-process validation is based on profile snapshots and terminology bindings. Although it is benchmarked against HL7 validator_cli 7.0.1, it is not equivalent to conformance certification by the official HL7 FHIR Validator.
  • The tools offer suggestions and structural assistance only; profile selection and final content remain the caller's responsibility.

For an in-depth walkthrough see FHIR Authoring Walkthrough.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The FHIR Medication service converts Taiwan FDA drug data from the drug service module into FHIR R4 Medication and MedicationKnowledge resources, with basic validation. It lets drug data be exchanged between systems in the standard FHIR format.

docs.title: 1. Generate FHIR Medication / MedicationKnowledge (query_fhir_medication)
docs.text:
• Query by drug keyword (keyword) or license number (license_id).
  • Use resource_type to select Medication or MedicationKnowledge output.
  • Coding uses the TFDA license number CodeSystem (https://mcp.fda.gov.tw/fhir/CodeSystem/tfda-license-id) and carries ingredient information.

docs.title: 2. Validate FHIR Medication (validate_fhir_medication)
docs.text: Performs basic structural validation of the supplied Medication JSON (required fields, coding systems) and returns {"valid", "resource_type", "errors"}.

docs.title: Technical architecture
docs.text:
• Data source: reads normalized drug data from the drug service module (drug_service).
  • Availability: derived from the drug domain — the tools degrade automatically when drug data is not loaded.
  • Validation scope: basic structure and required fields only. For full IG conformance, use the FHIR IG module's validation tools or the official HL7 FHIR Validator.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• Drug Service: supplies the source drug data.
  • Complementary to the FHIR IG module, which provides advanced profile- and terminology-level validation and authoring.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The food nutrition service provides comprehensive Taiwan food composition data and food ingredient regulatory information. It supports precise diet planning, nutritional analysis, and food compliance checking, for dietitians, food developers, and anyone paying attention to dietary health.

docs.title: Public tools (4)
docs.text: Tool Description query_food_nutrition Food nutrition lookup; detailed=true returns the full categorised panel query_food_ingredient Food ingredient compliance search; optional category filter on the top-level class search_foods_by_nutrient Rank foods from highest to lowest by a nutrient analyze_meal_nutrition Total nutrition analysis for a combination of foods

docs.title: 1. Food name resolution (hybrid search)
docs.text:
Every tool accepting food_name uses BM25 + semantic embedding Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF): - BM25 (FTS): plainto_tsquery('simple', ...) against sample_name, common_name, and english_name - Vector search: the food_embeddings table stores a halfvec embedding, with embedding <=> $2::halfvec computing cosine distance - RRF merge: the two rankings are summed as 1/(60+rank), and the highest score wins

This lets「白米飯」find「白飯」in the database despite the literal difference.

docs.title: 2. Nutrient lookup
docs.text:
• General search (detailed=false): returns a flat [{food, category, nutrients}] list, with an optional nutrient filter.
  • Detailed panel (detailed=true): returns all 100+ nutrients grouped by category, covering energy, macronutrients, vitamins, minerals, and fatty acids.

docs.title: 3. Food ingredient regulatory lookup
docs.text: Check the regulatory status of a food ingredient to confirm whether it may be used in food processing: - Top-level categories: "可供食品使用之原料" (approved) and "未確認安全性尚不得使用之原料" (prohibited) - Hybrid search: supports approximate Chinese and English matching, so a near-miss name still finds the closest ingredient

docs.title: 4. Meal analysis
docs.text: Overall nutritional assessment of a meal composed of several foods: - Hybrid per-item resolution: each food name goes through BM25 + embedding RRF independently; anything not found is marked "found": false - Totals: sums the calories and nutrients of every food in the meal (100 g per item by default) - pgBouncer compatible: the embedding HTTP call completes before a DB connection is acquired, satisfying transaction-mode constraints

docs.title: Data sources
docs.text:
• Food composition: the Taiwan Food Composition Database (FDA).
  • Approved food ingredients: the integrated food ingredient query platform.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
1. Dietary control: helps patients with diabetes or kidney disease, and people managing their weight, calculate intake.
  2. Menu design: lets caterers and institutional food services calculate nutrition labelling for meals.
  3. Product development: lets R&D staff confirm ingredient legality and assess a product's nutritional value.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The health supplements service focuses on data for health supplements certified with Taiwan's "Little Green Man" (小綠人) mark. It follows the Health Food Control Act strictly, providing information on government-approved health products to help users find safe, scientifically substantiated complementary options alongside conventional medical care.

docs.title: Key disclaimer
docs.text: Note: health supplements are not drugs and have no disease-treating efficacy. All information is for wellness reference only; treatment of disease must still follow a physician's instructions.

docs.title: 1. Health supplement lookup
docs.text: Lets users look up legally approved health supplement information: - Product search: search by product name (for example「靈芝」/ reishi or「魚油」/ fish oil). - Efficacy search: search by health claim (for example「調節血脂」/ blood lipid regulation,「護肝」/ liver protection, or「免疫調節」/ immune modulation). - License search: look up a specific 衛部健食字 license number.

docs.title: 2. Detailed product information
docs.text: Provides the complete approved record for a product: - Approved efficacy: the officially permitted health claims. - Functional ingredients: the content of the specific ingredients responsible for the health function. - Warnings and precautions: intake limits and contraindications for particular groups (such as pregnant women or infants). - Health claim statements: a detailed summary of the scientific substantiation.

docs.title: 3. Disease-oriented complementary analysis
docs.text: Combines ICD diagnoses with health supplement data to offer suggestions for a specific condition: - Association analysis: analyses the link between a disease (such as diabetes) and a health claim (such as blood glucose regulation). - Product recommendation: lists legal products certified for the relevant claim. - Safety reminders: automatically attaches the relevant medical warnings.

docs.title: Health claim categories
docs.text: The module covers the main claim categories approved under Taiwan regulation, including but not limited to: - Gastrointestinal function improvement - Blood lipid regulation - Liver protection - Bone health - Immune modulation - Support for adjusting allergic constitution - Resistance to body-fat formation - Blood glucose regulation - Anti-fatigue - Support for blood pressure regulation

docs.title: Technical architecture
docs.text:
• Data source: the Taiwan FDA health supplements dataset.
  • Integration: this module works together with the Nutrition Service, distinguishing certified "health supplements" (bearing the Little Green Man mark) from ordinary "nutritional supplements".

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
1. Nutrition consulting: a reference for dietitians planning a wellness programme.
  2. Chronic disease management: a lifestyle-adjustment reference for patients alongside conventional treatment.
  3. Consumer guidance: helps the public identify legal, government-certified products.

docs.title: Key limitation
docs.text: The disease mappings are developer-curated and have not been medically validated — they are not suitable for patient-facing use without expert review.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The ICD service is one of the system's core components, responsible for International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10) data. It integrates the Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) and Procedure Coding System (ICD-10-PCS), providing precise medical code lookup, hierarchical inference, and compatibility checking.

docs.title: 1. Medical code lookup
docs.text: Several query modes let users find the ICD-10 code they need quickly: - Keyword search: search by Chinese or English keyword (for example「糖尿病」, "Diabetes", or "E11"). - Type filter: restrict the search to diagnosis codes or procedure codes. - Hybrid search: diagnosis codes are ranked by BM25 full-text search plus vector similarity (merged with RRF). Vectors must first be backfilled by the icd_embed job; when the embedding endpoint is unavailable the search falls back to keywords and is marked search_mode: "keyword_only".

docs.title: 2. Complication inference
docs.text: Uses the ICD-10 hierarchy to infer complications or finer subcategories that may accompany a principal diagnosis. - Hierarchical analysis: expands from a parent code (for example E11) to child codes (for example E11.2, with kidney complications). - Clinical assistance: helps clinicians avoid missing potentially relevant conditions in the record.

docs.title: 3. Contextual analysis (nearby codes)
docs.text: Returns the codes immediately before and after a target code in the code list, which helps with: - Differential diagnosis: comparing descriptions of similar conditions. - Severity assessment: seeing codes of differing severity within the same category.

docs.title: 4. Category browsing
docs.text: Browse all diagnosis codes by ICD category: - Category list: grouped by the first three characters (for example E11.x, I10.x) - Code enumeration: returns every diagnosis code and name under a given category

docs.title: 5. Diagnosis / procedure conflict detection
docs.text: check_medical_conflict helps judge the logical compatibility of a diagnosis and a procedure (for example a male-specific diagnosis code paired with uterine surgery). - Structured data: returns the full rows for both the diagnosis code and the procedure code, with an instruction asking the caller (the LLM) to analyse contraindications. - The caller decides: the tool has no built-in indication / contraindication rule base; the conflict judgement is left to the caller, reasoning over the returned data. - When PCS is not loaded: the procedure side returns an "ICD-10-PCS data not loaded" notice.

docs.title: Technical architecture
docs.text:
• Data sources: ICD-10-CM and ICD-10-PCS (CMS), uploaded and imported on the Terminology → ICD-10 page of the admin console, "Data lifecycle" tab (import stage icd_import). Source roles:
    • icd10cm (required): upload the CMS "Code Descriptions in Tabular Order" zip (it holds icd10cm_order_YYYY.txt, e.g. april-1-2026-code-descriptions-tabular-order.zip). It is the complete code set (header codes plus billable codes including 7th characters / placeholder X — 98,186 codes in the 2026-04-01 release) and keeps the CMS short title and the header flag. The "Code Tables, Tabular and Index" zip (tabular XML) is also accepted — 7th characters are expanded — but it does not count as a complete edition.
    • icd10pcs: the ICD-10-PCS zip (CMS flat codes TXT).
    • icd_zh_tw (optional): the MOHW bilingual XLSX, for Chinese names.
    • icd10_who (optional): "WHO ICD-10 (FHIR JSON)" — a WHO ICD-10 FHIR CodeSystem or expanded ValueSet (e.g. the tx.fhir.org edition 2019-covid-expanded, 13,831 codes, fetched with node-server/scripts/validator-audit/harness/fetch_tx_terms.py), imported into icd.icd10_who so the FHIR validator can check codes and displays of http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10.
  • Edition record and strict judgement: every import writes icd.editions (edition, source_format = cms-order / tabular-xml, complete, code_count) in the same promote transaction. Only when the local table is a complete CMS order-file edition does the FHIR validator report unknown ICD-10-CM codes as errors (as tx.fhir.org does); with tabular XML, or no recorded edition, they stay warnings. WHO ICD-10 works the same way: strict only when the complete 2019-covid-expanded edition is loaded.
  • Database: PostgreSQL 16 — icd.diagnoses (diagnosis codes, with short_name_en and is_header), icd.procedures (procedure codes), icd.editions, icd.icd10_who, and the vector table icd.diagnosis_embeddings.
  • PCS degradation: the pcsAvailable flag in icdService.ts — when icd.procedures is empty, the procedure features degrade automatically and return an informational message rather than an error.
  • Vector search uses an exact scan on purpose: the diagnosis vector query orders by (embedding <=> $v) + 0 so the planner stays off the HNSW index — the ~50k near-duplicate 7th-character codes make HNSW recall collapse (diabetes queries returned fracture codes). An exact scan of ~98k rows takes about 0.35 s.
  • Terminology browsing: the "Data preview" tab of the same module page offers an ICD-10-CM chapter tree, a WHO ICD-10 tree and an ICD-10-PCS seven-axis table browser, backed by /admin/api/terminology/icd/* (cm/children, cm/path, cm/search, who/*, pcs/browse, pcs/table, pcs/codes, pcs/code, pcs/search).
  • Local development: without an admin upload the loader falls back to fhir-code/icd/10/ (overridable with ICD_CM_ZIP, ICD_PCS_ZIP and similar env vars); see Test data files.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: This is a self-contained foundational module, but the following advanced services depend on it: - FHIR Condition Service: converts ICD codes to the FHIR standard format. - Health Supplements Service: its condition mode resolves a diagnosis keyword through ICD search. - FHIR IG validator: judges ICD-10-CM / WHO ICD-10 codes and displays against icd.*.

docs.title: IG Concept Search
docs.text: Maps Chinese or English free text, abbreviations and chart wording to codes of any CodeSystem of an installed IG — for example TW Core medical-service-payment-tw (Taiwan NHI medical service payment codes), occupation, department or medication-frequency codes, or the PAS CodeSystems. The code lives in node-server/src/conceptSearch/ and is used by fhir_normalize_code (when the target is an IG CodeSystem) and search_medical_codes(system=…); SNOMED CT / LOINC / ICD-10 keep their own tables.

docs.title: What is searched
docs.text:
Every IG CodeSystem is indexed by ig_import (automatically after an IG is installed) or ig_concept_index (backfill / rebuild):

Source Notes The CodeSystem JSON display, designations in every language (e.g. the English names TW Core already ships), nested concept.concept, string properties (e.g. ingredients), short definitions (≤ 120 characters, low weight) CodeSystem supplements FHIR R4 content = supplement, merged by supplements (optionally |version): designations and properties. Supplements shipped in IG packages, uploaded in the admin console, or bundled with the code (see "Bundled data" below) all apply. A numeric usage property (code or description mentions claim-volume / usage / popularity / 申報量 / 使用量, e.g. a claim-volume built from the NHI open dataset 診療項目醫令申報量(年)) is not a name: it becomes a usage prior for ranking (see "Usage" below) Linked names Coding properties (e.g. a supplement's loinc) and the targets of IG ConceptMaps whose group.source is the CodeSystem: the shared LOINC COMPONENT, SNOMED descriptions, otherwise the coding display UMLS (optional) When a concept's English name is a string of a UMLS concept (CUI), that CUI's other synonyms / abbreviations become match-only terms (at most 12 per concept)

CodeSystems served by the ICD / LOINC / SNOMED tables (icd-10-cm-*-tw …) are not indexed. A signature decides whether a CodeSystem needs rebuilding; unchanged ones are skipped.

docs.title: Query processing
docs.text:
• Normalisation: NFKC (full-width → half-width), case, Unicode dashes, variant characters (臺/台, 脢/酶 …), Chinese numerals before measure words (小於五公分 → 小於5公分), cm → 公分, < → 小於, dotted abbreviations (C.R.P → crp), w/o.
  • Chart noise removed: laterality, x1, 5針, suture specs (4-0 Nylon), r/o, f/u, s/p, dosing / sampling frequencies (q6h, q3m, bid, prn), measured values and doses with a unit (7.8%, 0.5mg, 25 cmH2O, 28Fr, 2.4 ATA) and decimal lab values (Hb 9.1). Sizes (公分), durations and ages are kept.
  • Shorthand: short shorthand joined by & / / (I&D, U/A, B/C) is one word; its parts remain words of their own (Na/K → na, k).
