  • Tokens: English words (-s / -ing / -ed folded), Chinese character bigrams plus low-weight unigrams; an English word absent from the index matches as a prefix (abd → abdominal, vanco → vancomycin); an English word of 7+ letters that a name lacks also matches, at a discount, another form sharing its first 6 letters (recurrent ↔ recurrence, laparoscopic ↔ laparoscopy).
  • Query variants (each scored, the best kept, agreement between variants adds a little): the text, its clinical core, without brackets, abbreviation expansions, zh ↔ en bridges, UMLS synonyms. Every expansion comes from data: SNOMED CT "ACR - expansion" descriptions, LOINC shortname ↔ component, abbreviations defined inside IG names ("… lithotripsy (ESWL)", Schwartz–Hearst validated), English ↔ Chinese word pairs mined from ICD-10 / IG bilingual names (Dice + mutual best match), the abbrev / zhEn tables of grounding/twLexiconData.ts, and optionally UMLS — stored in fhir.term_thesaurus / fhir.umls_terms.
  • General abbreviation lexicon fills gaps (fhir.abbreviation_lexicon, the SPECIALIST Lexicon's LRABR; a copy is bundled with the code and loaded while the table is empty, a UMLS file carrying LRABR replaces it): an abbreviation in the query's first clause is looked up there only when the CodeSystem does not use it as a word itself (e.g. "Procalcitonin (PCT)" already contains PCT) and no thesaurus expansion is supported by the CodeSystem (support < 0.45). A general lexicon gives an abbreviation dozens of senses (LP → lipoprotein, lumbar puncture …); each sense is scored by how well the CodeSystem's own names name it — the best lexical score of the sense on its own (capped at 1) + 0.3 × usage of that concept — kept at support ≥ 0.45, one reading per concept, best first (the best one is also embedded). Upper-case acronyms (PLEX, BMA) apply only to words written like abbreviations, lower-case clippings (chole, trach) only to words the CodeSystem does not know; abbreviations of fewer than 3 letters / digits are too ambiguous to expand from it; a one-word expansion must be a clipping (trach → tracheostomy) — ABO → antibody, where the letters merely occur, is dropped. Abbreviations in later clauses (indication, notes) are not expanded, so a wrong sense there adds no noise.
  • Scoring: BM25-like with query / name coverage; only the text as typed matching a name exactly is exact and always ranks first (official Chinese names typed verbatim: top-1 ≥ 98%).
  • Semantic: the same embedding model and identity as ICD (ig_embed job; vectors keyed by sha256(name), so a name shared by package versions is embedded once). The core text, the abbreviation-expanded text and the first clause are embedded in one call and scanned exactly against that CodeSystem's vectors (no HNSW). CodeSystems with more than 20,000 concepts are indexed lexically only. Without a usable embedding endpoint, or before the CodeSystem has vectors, responses carry search_mode: "keyword_only".
  • Fusion: 0.55 × lexical + 0.45 × semantic (similarities rescaled within the query's own similarity distribution — best = 1, rank 40 = 0 — and weighted by a confidence of (best − rank-40 value) ÷ 0.12; no absolute 0.7 floor any more: absolute similarity levels are model-specific, and Qwen3-Embedding-4B with a query instruction puts the best match at ~0.6–0.75. The query vector carries the ig_concept task instruction).
  • Usage (only when the CodeSystem carries a usage property; otherwise ranking is unchanged):
  • prior: + 0.3 × usage (log-scaled to 0–1 relative to the CodeSystem's most used code);
  • sibling ordering: among codes of one group (same name stem, differing only by a method / setting / size qualifier — 白蛋白 vs 白蛋白(免疫比濁法), 血液透析(一次)-住院 vs -門診), the members the query cannot tell apart — same exact-match status and the same share of the query's words covered (within 0.05), or, when no word of the query matched, a similarity within 0.02 — are ordered by usage instead of by vector noise. The group keeps its place among the candidates; only its representative changes. A query that names the qualifier ("住院 洗腎", "recurrent") covers more words with that sibling, so usage never overrides it.
  • Multi-item text ("Na/K/Cl", "CBC/DC, Hb …"): the response carries clauses (each clause's best code, in text order) and the first clause's concept gets a small boost.

docs.title: Response fields
docs.text: IG candidates of fhir_normalize_code: code, display, source (lexical / semantic / hybrid), score, matched_term / matched_language (the IG name that matched — always the IG's own display or designation, never a UMLS string), exact, category (from a categorical property or the hierarchy), group + siblings (near-duplicate codes with the same name stem, e.g. the same test by another method), linked (codes of other systems reached through Coding properties, at most 3 + linked_more, e.g. an NHI drug's ATC code). When the resolved IG holds only an excerpt of a CodeSystem and another installed package holds a full copy of the same canonical (≥ 10× the concepts and ≥ 1,000 more, e.g. TW Core 1.0.0 vs 0.3.2 medication-nhi-tw), the full copy is searched unless package_id / version is given, noted in warnings and data.codesystem_copies. system may be a canonical, a CodeSystem id or alias words (e.g. nhi_payment). fhir_lookup_code adds hint and near_codes when a code is not found.

docs.title: Admin console (IG packages → 術語搜尋索引)
docs.text:
• Index / vector / thesaurus / abbreviation-lexicon status (the lexicon shows its source: bundled or an uploaded UMLS file); "補建索引" (skips unchanged CodeSystems) and "全部重建" (force). While an index job runs the panel shows its step and "CodeSystems checked / total"; when it ends it shows the result — "索引已是最新（N 個 CodeSystem 未變更）" (index up to date, N unchanged) when nothing was rebuilt.
  • "N 個套件尚未建立索引" (N packages not indexed yet) counts only packages that have indexable CodeSystems; packages with profiles only, or whose CodeSystems are served by the ICD / LOINC / SNOMED tables or are content = not-present, are listed as a neutral note ("no indexable CodeSystem") and need no action.
  • Upload a CodeSystem supplement JSON (application/fhir+json, up to 64 MB); the list shows the package versions it applies to; uploads and deletions rebuild the affected index. Bundled supplements carry a 「內建」 badge; deleting one is remembered (it is not re-applied by the next import) and "還原" / "還原內建 supplement" restores it (queues ig_concept_index, which applies it). API: GET/POST/DELETE /admin/api/igs/supplements, POST /admin/api/igs/supplements/bundled/restore ({url?}, all when omitted), GET /admin/api/igs/concept-index, POST /admin/api/igs/concept-index/rebuild.

docs.title: Bundled data (no manual upload)
docs.text:
The code ships openly licensed reference data (node-server/data/, copied into both images; sources, versions, licences and how to regenerate them: node-server/data/README.md, generators in node-server/scripts/supplements/). On a fresh install the operator imports an IG (e.g. TW Core) through the normal admin flow — no file uploads, no direct DB writes:

File Supplements Content nhi-payment-en-supplement TW Core medical-service-payment-tw NHI English item names of the payment codes nhi-payment-loinc-supplement same LOINC links of the TWPAS ConceptMap nhi-loinc (with LOINC names) nhi-payment-usage-supplement same NHI annual claim volume — a usage prior for ranking nhi-medication-supplement TW Core medication-nhi-tw Chinese / English names, ingredients and ATC of NHI drug codes lrabr-2024AA.tsv.gz — SPECIALIST Lexicon LRABR abbreviation lexicon (filtered like the loader keeps it, 115,233 rows)
  • When: before every index build — ig_import (including dependency installs) and ig_concept_index ("補建索引") — each bundled supplement whose supplements canonical names an installed CodeSystem is written to fhir.codesystem_supplements (uploaded_by = 'system:bundled', the same write path as uploads); the same job then builds the index, including the packages a newly applied supplement touches — no second rebuild. A supplement whose target is not installed yet is applied when it is.
  • Idempotent, never overwrites: a row with the same url + version (whoever stored it) is left alone; when an operator-uploaded different version of the url exists the bundled version is not written; only an older bundled version is replaced by a newer bundled one.
  • Deletion is respected: deleting a bundled supplement records an opt-out (admin.app_settings, group bundled_supplements, key = url); it does not come back until restored.
  • Abbreviation lexicon: the bundled LRABR is loaded only while fhir.abbreviation_lexicon is empty (source = 'bundled:LRABR-2024AA'; parsed fully first, written in one transaction); uploading a UMLS file that carries LRABR (umls_import) still replaces it. The lexicon is not part of the index signature, so loading it triggers no rebuild.
  • Installs that already hold them (e.g. production, where the same 4 supplements were uploaded by hand with the same url + version and the lexicon came from a UMLS file): nothing is written, nothing re-indexed or re-embedded; the list marks those rows 「內建」.

docs.title: UMLS (optional, requires a UMLS licence)
docs.text:
Without UMLS the engine works as described, just without UMLS synonyms. To enable it:

  1. Write the compact subset (same parser, ~36 MB): node dist/loaders/umls.js --subset umls-2024AA-metathesaurus-full.zip umls-subset-2024AA.rrf.gz (the Metathesaurus zip, or a zip holding only META/MRCONSO.RRF + META/MRSAB.RRF, is accepted as well and is streamed member by member, but uploading the full 4 GB zip through the browser is impractical.)
  2. Upload it in the admin console as source ig / umls_metathesaurus and run the umls_import job; the index is rebuilt afterwards.

Source vocabularies (SAB): MRSAB rows with CURVER = Y and SRL = 0, plus SNOMEDCT_US (covered by this deployment's SNOMED CT licence), minus non-clinical sources: HGNC, OMIM, GO, NCBI, LCH, LCH_NW, SRC, MTHMST, UWDA, FMA, MTHSPL, USP, USPMG, HL7V2.5, HL7V3.0, CDCREC, MVX, CVX, TKMT, SPN, MCM, QMR, RAM, CCS, CCSR_, DXP, ICPC. Only LAT = ENG, SUPPRESS = N strings of ≤ 80 characters, and only concepts with at least 2 distinct strings, are kept (2024AA: ~2.53 M strings / 0.76 M concepts, fhir.umls_terms ≈ 610 MB). The SAB is recorded internally only (fhir.concept_index_terms.source); no UMLS string is ever returned by a tool.

Abbreviation lexicon (a copy is bundled — see "Bundled data"; this is how to load it from a UMLS file): LRABR of the SPECIALIST Lexicon (NLM Lexical Systems Group; LEX/LRABR inside LEX.tgz, ~20 MB; open source and freely available — no UMLS licence needed). Only acronym / abbreviation rows with a 2–10 character abbreviation and a 3–80 character ASCII expansion are kept, spelling variants (plasma exchange / plasma-exchange) collapse (2024 release: ~115 k rows / 34 k abbreviations). Add it as a third argument when writing the subset: node dist/loaders/umls.js --subset <umls.zip> umls-subset-2024AA-lrabr.rrf.gz LEX/LRABR; an LRABR member of an uploaded UMLS zip is read as well. umls_import replaces fhir.abbreviation_lexicon only when the file carries it (apply migration 20261027_abbreviation_lexicon.sql first; without the table it logs a warning and skips). Lexicon strings likewise only steer matching and never appear in tool output.

docs.title: Jobs and tables
docs.text:
Job Description ig_import Applies the bundled data (supplements / lexicon), indexes the packages it installed (plus those a newly applied supplement touches), then queues ig_embed ig_concept_index Applies the bundled data, then backfill / rebuild; progress counts CodeSystems (options: packages, force, embed_max_concepts, thesaurus, queue_embed); then rebuilds the thesaurus and queues ig_embed when vectors are missing ig_embed Embeds the embeddable names (incremental, content-addressed) umls_import Loads UMLS (optional; also the abbreviation lexicon when the file carries LRABR), then queues ig_concept_index

Tables: fhir.concept_index_cs / _concepts / _terms, fhir.concept_embeddings, fhir.term_thesaurus, fhir.codesystem_supplements (migration 20261022_ig_concept_search.sql), fhir.umls_terms / fhir.umls_release (20261023_umls_terms.sql), fhir.abbreviation_lexicon (20261027_abbreviation_lexicon.sql).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Taiwan-specific chart abbreviations (NSD, Foley, OB, "echo" for ultrasound …) are mostly absent from SNOMED / LOINC / UMLS / LRABR and may still not be found; two-letter abbreviations (PD, LP, VF) are not expanded from the general lexicon and rely on the CodeSystem itself, the thesaurus and the embedding.
  • CodeSystems with Chinese names only and no English designation (e.g. occupations) rely on the embedding for English queries.
  • A very large CodeSystem (tens of thousands of concepts) takes a few seconds to load on its first query; it is cached in memory afterwards.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The lab service integrates reference data and standard coding for laboratory tests, with particular emphasis on mapping Taiwan NHI lab codes to the international lab standard (LOINC). The module aims to improve the interoperability of lab data and the consistency of its interpretation.

docs.title: 1. Test lookup and LOINC mapping
docs.text:
• Code mapping: cross-reference lookup between local lab codes and LOINC (Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes).
  • Standardised names: standard Chinese and English names for each test, reducing confusion when one test has several names.

docs.title: 2. Reference ranges
docs.text: Standard reference intervals for each category of test, to assist interpretation: - Numeric ranges: upper and lower bounds of the normal range (for example haemoglobin Hb 13.5–17.5 g/dL). - Unit conversion: recognises common units. - Sex and age differences: some tests provide different reference standards by sex or age band.

docs.title: 3. Abnormality interpretation (interpret_lab_result)
docs.text: Picks the reference interval that applies to the patient's age / sex, flags the value H (high), L (low) or N (normal), and returns the interval, its source note and a generic sentence (for example "above the normal reference value; further evaluation advised"). It does not infer causes — clinical meaning is for the caller or a clinician to judge. A value can only be interpreted when loinc.reference_ranges holds a range for that code.

docs.title: 4. Search by specimen type
docs.text: Filter LOINC tests by specimen type such as blood, urine, or stool.

docs.title: 5. Related test lookup
docs.text: Find all related LOINC tests for the same analyte, helping select the most appropriate method.

docs.title: 6. Full LOINC concept details
docs.text: Retrieve complete information for a single LOINC code, including a patient-friendly Chinese name, units, specimen, and method.

docs.title: 7. Batch result interpretation (batch_interpret_lab_results)
docs.text: Submit many values at once (results_json, each item with loinc_code and value) and get back total_tests, abnormal_count, normal_count and the per-item interpretations; items without a reference range are skipped.

docs.title: Technical architecture
docs.text:
• Data sources: LOINC 2.80 (Loinc_2.80.zip, about 105k concepts), uploaded and imported on the Terminology → LOINC page of the admin console (import stage loinc_import). Two optional, project-curated sources: loinc_taiwan_mapping (Chinese names of tests common in Taiwan, data/loinc/taiwan_mapping.csv, about 30 rows) and loinc_reference_ranges (age/sex-stratified reference ranges, data/loinc/lab_reference_ranges.csv, about 40 rows).
  • Extra content for the FHIR validator: the import also keeps the answer (LA), part (LP), answer-list (LL) and group (LG) codes of the LOINC zip AccessoryFiles (loinc.other_codes) and the release version (loinc.editions), so the FHIR validator can check those codes and displays; unknown LOINC codes are errors only when the local release is at least the version tx.fhir.org uses (currently 2.82), warnings otherwise (2.80 < 2.82, so warnings today).
  • LOINC structure tables (migration 20261020_loinc_structure.sql): loinc.part_links (per-axis parts: COMPONENT / PROPERTY / TIME / SYSTEM / SCALE / METHOD), loinc.answer_list_items / loinc.answer_list_links (answer lists), loinc.panel_items (panel membership) and loinc.map_to (MapTo replacements), written in the same promote transaction as loinc.concepts and read by the admin terminology browser.
  • Database: PostgreSQL 16 — loinc.concepts (LOINC codes), loinc.reference_ranges (reference values), the extra tables above, and the vector table loinc.concept_embeddings (backfilled by loinc_embed).
  • Terminology browsing: the module page's "Data preview" tab offers six-axis facet filtering, a single-term view (parts, answer lists, panels, MapTo) and LA/LP/LL/LG code lookup, backed by /admin/api/terminology/loinc/* (facets, facet-values, term, code).
  • Structured output: the returned data can be used directly to generate FHIR Observation resources.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
1. Health check-up report systems: automatically flag abnormal values and attach explanations.
  2. EMR integration: standardise in-house lab codes to LOINC for cross-hospital exchange.
  3. Personal health management: help the public understand the terminology and values in their check-up reports.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The SNOMED CT service integrates the SNOMED CT International edition terminology, providing concept search, concept details, relationship (hierarchy and attribute) queries, and SNOMED ↔ ICD-10 mapping. SNOMED CT is the broadest clinical terminology in use today; this module lets the system express clinical semantics as standard concepts and interoperate with ICD-10.

docs.title: 1. Concept search (search_snomed_concept)
docs.text: Search SNOMED CT concepts by Chinese or English keyword, returning the concept ID, FSN (Fully Specified Name), and preferred term. Semantic / hybrid search is supported (requires a working embedding endpoint, configured in the admin console under Integrations → Model endpoints, and vectors backfilled by snomed_embed); without embeddings it falls back to keyword search.

docs.title: 2. Concept details (query_snomed_concept)
docs.text: Retrieve full information for a single concept by concept ID, including: - FSN and preferred term - Ancestors: concepts up the is-a hierarchy, with depth. - Children: direct child concepts.

docs.title: 3. Relationship queries (get_snomed_relationships)
docs.text: Retrieve all relationships for a concept, grouped by relationship type, listing the target concept of each attribute — for example finding site or associated morphology.

docs.title: 4. SNOMED ↔ ICD-10 mapping (query_snomed_mapping)
docs.text: Bidirectional mapping: - mode="icd": given an ICD-10 code (for example E11.9), return the corresponding SNOMED concepts. - mode="snomed": given a SNOMED concept ID (for example 44054006), return the corresponding ICD-10 mapping.

docs.title: Technical architecture
docs.text:
• Data source: SNOMED CT International RF2 (SnomedCT_InternationalRF2_PRODUCTION_*.zip), uploaded and imported on the Terminology → SNOMED CT page of the admin console (source role snomed_ct, import stage snomed_import). The dataset is large — expect roughly 5–15 minutes. The import also keeps inactive concepts and the English descriptions of inactive concepts / inactive descriptions (snomed.inactive_concepts, snomed.inactive_descriptions), each component's first release date (from the RF2 Full files) and the edition (snomed.editions), so the FHIR validator answers as the edition tx.fhir.org serves: an inactive concept is a warning, an unknown code or an inactive description used as display is an error. The SNOMED search tools are unaffected (they still use active concepts only). Historical associations (SAME AS / REPLACED BY …, snomed.historical_associations) let an inactive concept point at live content.
  • Database: the snomed schema, with concepts, descriptions, relationships, icd10_map, historical_associations, and concept_embeddings.
  • Terminology browsing: the module page's "Data preview" tab shows a concept graph (is-a parents and children, attribute relationships, ICD-10 maps; for an inactive concept also its historical associations), backed by /admin/api/terminology/snomed/* (concept, children, search).
  • Availability gate: snomed.concepts must reach the threshold (100,000 rows) before the corresponding tools are registered; otherwise they degrade automatically.

docs.title: Key limitations
docs.text: • Using SNOMED CT requires an active SNOMED International license (free for most uses). The related tools are not enabled while the data is unloaded.

docs.title: Clinical Calculator Tools
docs.text:
This group provides validated clinical scores and calculations used across Taiwan clinical practice. Every calculator is a pure, stateless function — no database, no external service — and is always registered (never gated by module data load state).

Every result returns a consistent envelope:

{
  "calculator": "bmi",
  "score": 27.55,
  "category": "肥胖",
  "interpretation": "BMI 27.55，肥胖",
  "inputs": { "weight_kg": 75, "height_cm": 165 },
  "notes": [
    "台灣（亞洲）標準：<18.5 過輕、18.5–23.9 正常、24–26.9 過重、≥27 肥胖。",
    "WHO 國際標準為 ≥25 過重、≥30 肥胖，與台灣標準不同。"
  ],
  "disclaimer": "僅供臨床決策支援，不取代專業醫療判斷。"
}

Besides the common fields, each calculator adds its own tier field (e.g. category, risk_category, ckd_stage, disease_activity). interpretation is a full sentence, not a bare tier label — read the tier field when parsing programmatically. Continuous scores are rounded to two decimals, and the tier is always derived from the rounded value, so the reported score and tier never contradict each other.

Input validation: every parameter has a plausible range (see the tables below). Out-of-range values and obvious unit mix-ups (e.g. height in metres, creatinine in µmol/L) are rejected with a validation error instead of producing a score. The ranges are also published in the JSON Schema of tools/list and /openapi.json.

All results are decision support only and do not replace professional medical judgment. Cutoffs and tiers follow each score's original literature and current Taiwan guidance; interpretation / notes are Traditional Chinese.

docs.title: calculate_chads2_vasc
docs.text: CHA₂DS₂-VASc stroke-risk score for non-valvular atrial fibrillation (0–9), plus the 2024 ESC CHA₂DS₂-VA adjusted score (sex removed).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description age integer Yes Age in years (0–130); 65–74 / ≥75 brackets computed internally sex string Yes "M" / "F" congestive_heart_failure boolean No Congestive heart failure hypertension boolean No Hypertension diabetes boolean No Diabetes stroke_or_tia boolean No Prior stroke / TIA vascular_disease boolean No Vascular disease

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Score 0–9; also returns adjusted_score (sex removed). Risk tiering uses CHA₂DS₂-VA: 0 no anticoagulation, 1 consider, ≥2 oral anticoagulation recommended.

docs.title: calculate_wells_pe
docs.text: Wells criteria for pulmonary embolism (two-tier + three-tier risk).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description clinical_signs_dvt boolean No Clinical signs of DVT (+3) alternative_diagnosis_less_likely boolean No Alternative diagnosis less likely (+3) heart_rate_bpm number No Heart rate (0–350); >100 auto +1.5 immobilization_or_recent_surgery boolean No Immobilization / surgery ≤4 weeks (+1.5) previous_dvt_or_pe boolean No Prior DVT/PE (+1.5) hemoptysis boolean No Hemoptysis (+1) active_malignancy boolean No Active malignancy (+1)

docs.title: calculate_wells_dvt
docs.text: Wells criteria for deep-vein thrombosis (two-tier + three-tier risk).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description active_cancer boolean No Active cancer (+1) paralysis_paresis_or_immobilization boolean No Paralysis / paresis / immobilization (+1) bedridden_or_recent_surgery boolean No Bedridden / surgery ≤4 weeks (+1) calf_swelling_gt_3cm boolean No Calf swelling >3 cm (+1) collateral_superficial_veins boolean No Collateral superficial veins (+1) entire_leg_swollen boolean No Entire leg swollen (+1) localized_tenderness boolean No Localized tenderness (+1) pitting_edema boolean No Pitting edema (+1) previous_dvt boolean No Prior DVT (+1) alternative_diagnosis_as_likely boolean No Alternative diagnosis as likely (−2)

docs.title: calculate_das28
docs.text: DAS28 rheumatoid arthritis disease activity (ESR or CRP variant).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description tender_count integer Yes Tender joint count (28-joint assessment, 0–28) swollen_count integer Yes Swollen joint count (28-joint assessment, 0–28) global_health number Yes Patient global assessment VAS (0–100 mm; not the 0–10 scale CDAI uses) formula string Yes "esr" or "crp" esr number per formula Required when formula="esr", mm/h (>0, max 200) crp number per formula Required when formula="crp", mg/L (0–500; not mg/dL)

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text: ≤2.6 remission, ≤3.2 low, ≤5.1 moderate, >5.1 high disease activity.

docs.title: calculate_cdai
docs.text: CDAI (lab-free) rheumatoid arthritis disease activity.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description tender_count integer Yes Tender joint count (28-joint assessment, 0–28) swollen_count integer Yes Swollen joint count (28-joint assessment, 0–28) patient_global number Yes Patient global assessment (0–10) provider_global number Yes Provider global assessment (0–10)

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text: Total 0–76; ≤2.8 remission, ≤10 low, ≤22 moderate, >22 high disease activity.

docs.title: calculate_bmi
docs.text: Body mass index with Taiwan (Asian) cutoffs.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description weight_kg number Yes Weight in kg (>0, max 700) height_cm number Yes Height in cm (50–280; height in metres is rejected)

docs.title: Tiers (Taiwan/Asian)
docs.text: <18.5 underweight, 18.5–23.9 normal, 24–26.9 overweight, ≥27 obese. WHO international cutoffs are ≥25 overweight, ≥30 obese.

docs.title: calculate_egfr
docs.text: Estimated glomerular filtration rate (CKD-EPI 2021, race-free).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description age integer Yes Age in years (18–130; CKD-EPI 2021 is adults-only) sex string Yes "M" / "F" serum_creatinine_mgdl number Yes Serum creatinine (mg/dL, >0, max 30; µmol/L ÷ 88.4)

docs.title: Tiers (KDIGO)
docs.text: G1 ≥90, G2 60–89, G3a 45–59, G3b 30–44, G4 15–29, G5 <15. Not applicable in acute kidney injury or unstable states.

docs.title: calculate_has_bled
docs.text: HAS-BLED bleeding risk on oral anticoagulation (0–9).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description age integer Yes Age in years (0–130); >65 auto +1 systolic_bp_mmhg number No Systolic BP (mmHg, 0–300); >160 auto counts as uncontrolled hypertension +1 abnormal_renal_function boolean No Abnormal renal function abnormal_liver_function boolean No Abnormal liver function stroke_history boolean No Stroke history bleeding_history boolean No Bleeding history / predisposition labile_inr boolean No Labile INR drugs_antiplatelet_or_nsaid boolean No Antiplatelet / NSAID alcohol boolean No Alcohol ≥8 drinks/week

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text: ≥3 high bleeding risk — use caution and monitor regularly.

docs.title: calculate_curb65
docs.text: CURB-65 community-acquired pneumonia severity (0–5).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description age integer Yes Age in years (0–130); ≥65 auto +1 confusion boolean No Confusion bun_mgdl number No BUN (mg/dL, 0–300); >19 +1 respiratory_rate number No Respiratory rate; ≥30 +1 sbp_mmhg number No Systolic BP (<90, or DBP≤60, counts as hypotension +1) dbp_mmhg number No Diastolic BP

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text: 0–1 low, 2 moderate, ≥3 high (consider ICU). BUN >19 mg/dL ≈ urea >7 mmol/L.

docs.title: calculate_qsofa
docs.text: qSOFA sepsis screening (0–3).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description respiratory_rate number No Respiratory rate; ≥22 +1 gcs integer No Glasgow Coma Scale (3–15); <15 auto counts as altered mentation +1 sbp_mmhg number No Systolic BP; ≤100 +1

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text: ≥2 suggests sepsis and further evaluation; qSOFA is a screening tool, not a diagnostic criterion.

docs.title: calculate_gcs
docs.text: Glasgow Coma Scale (3–15).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description eye_response integer Yes Eye E (1–4) verbal_response integer Yes Verbal V (1–5) motor_response integer Yes Motor M (1–6)

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text:
13–15 mild, 9–12 moderate, ≤8 severe (coma / consider intubation).

All tools return JSON (a JSON string inside MCP content[0].text); there is no plain-text output format.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
Weights, formulas and cutoffs follow the original literature / authoritative sources below and were re-verified on 2026-10-05:

Score Source CHA₂DS₂-VASc / CHA₂DS₂-VA 2024 ESC AF guideline (CHA₂DS₂-VA, sex removed) Wells PE / DVT Wells et al. (PE / DVT clinical probability) DAS28 / CDAI Prevoo (DAS28), Aletaha (CDAI) BMI Taiwan MOHW Health Promotion Administration (24 overweight, 27 obese) eGFR CKD-EPI 2021 (Inker et al., NEJM 2021; kidney.org) HAS-BLED Pisters et al., 2010 CURB-65 Lim et al., 2003 qSOFA Singer et al., 2016 (Sepsis-3) GCS Teasdale & Jennett, 1974

HAS-BLED and qSOFA accept raw values for their narrower source definitions ("uncontrolled hypertension = SBP >160 mmHg", "altered mentation = GCS <15") and compute them internally.

docs.title: Drug Tools
docs.text:
This group integrates Taiwan FDA (TFDA) western-medicine license data, providing drug search, pill identification, drug details, and official document asset download links.

Maintenance mode: while the admin console has the drug module in maintenance mode, this group's (and the FHIR Medication tools') calls return an isError result immediately with error code MODULE_MAINTENANCE (error.message in English, error.message_zh in Traditional Chinese, error.module the module key), effective within about 5 seconds; the tools stay in tools/list. See the API reference.

docs.title: search_drug
docs.text: A single entry point with four search modes.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example mode string No drug_name / ingredient / license_id / atc_code, drug_name by default "ingredient" keyword string Yes The search term, interpreted according to mode "普拿疼", "acetaminophen", "000029", "N02BE01" limit integer No Result cap, 3 by default, maximum 10 5 include_cancelled boolean No Whether to include revoked licenses, false by default true

docs.title: Choosing a mode
docs.text: Mode When to use it What it searches drug_name The Chinese or English drug name is known Drug name ingredient Looking for drugs containing an ingredient Ingredient text license_id The license number or its trailing digits is known License number atc_code Looking up drugs by ATC classification ATC code

docs.title: Response format
docs.text: { "mode": "drug_name", "keyword": "普拿疼", "include_cancelled": false, "results": [...] }

docs.title: identify_unknown_pill
docs.text: Identify an unknown drug from tablet appearance keywords.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example features string Yes Space-separated appearance keywords (colour / shape / score line / marking / size / engraving) "white round", "白 圓形"

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Each keyword is matched conjunctively against the appearance description, colour, shape, symbol, score line, size, and engraving fields. English colour and shape terms are expanded through a built-in synonym table. Returns up to 5 results. Appearance data must be loaded first by a drug_enrichment job (admin console → Drug).

docs.title: get_drug_details
docs.text: Return the normalized drug record for a single license.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example license_id string Yes License number "衛署藥製字第000480號" include_cancelled boolean No Whether to include revoked licenses, false by default true

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The detail counterpart to search_drug. The response is assembled from normalized JSON in PostgreSQL, along with the current availability and document counts for each stage.

docs.title: get_drug_asset_links
docs.text: Return drug document asset metadata plus freshly generated MinIO download links.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example license_id string No License number (supply this or asset_id) "衛署藥製字第000480號" asset_id string No A specific asset ID — asset_group string No insert (electronic package insert) / label (carton label) / shape (pill image) / analysis (analysis output) "insert" latest_insert_only boolean No Return only the newest insert, false by default true

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The returned download links are time-limited presigned URLs. The corresponding data must be loaded first by drug_enrichment (assets) and drug_analysis (analysis output) jobs.

docs.title: FHIR IG Tools
docs.text:
A general, IG-scoped toolset built on the multi-IG fhir.* store, used to explore Implementation Guides, read profiles and terminology, perform terminology validation, and produce and validate FHIR R4 resources through skeleton-fill authoring.

Maintenance mode: while the admin console has the ig module in maintenance mode, all 22 tools of this group (including fhir_check_grounding / fhir_check_completeness) calls return an isError result immediately with error code MODULE_MAINTENANCE (error.message in English, error.message_zh in Traditional Chinese, error.module the module key), effective within about 5 seconds; the tools stay in tools/list. See the API reference.

docs.title: Shared conventions
docs.text:
• Every tool accepts an optional package_id + version. When package_id is omitted, the target package is chosen by this precedence, and provenance.resolved_by says which rule applied:
    1. explicit_version — a canonical argument or meta.profile pinned as url|version → the package holding that version;
    2. package_arg / latest — package_id was given (with version, that version; without it, the default IG's version, else the highest release — pre-releases only when no release exists);
    3. meta_profile / canonical_owner — the package that owns the meta.profile or the canonical argument (profile / ValueSet / system), manually-installed IGs first;
    4. default_ig — the default IG (isDefault);
    5. sole_manual_ig — no default IG and exactly one manually-installed IG. If none applies the call fails with NO_DEFAULT_IG (no arbitrary package is picked).
  • A |version is always honoured: a version that is not installed returns ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND (the message lists the installed versions) — never a silent fallback to another version.
  • Responses use a shared envelope: {ok, data, warnings, provenance, error?}. provenance carries packageId / version / fhirVersion / source plus resolved_by; when the dependency closure holds several versions of one package it also carries closure_versions (which version canonical lookups use).
  • When declared dependencies of the target IG are not installed, data.deps_missing lists them as {package_id, version, required_by} (incomplete closure — results may be missing content).
  • List / search tools (fhir_list_artifacts, fhir_search_artifacts, fhir_list_resource_profiles) query only the default IG when package_id is omitted; all_packages=true queries every installed package instead (rows carry package_id / package_version; package_id is then ignored). Zero hits come with data.hint naming the other packages that match.
  • Compact output compact=true (fhir_list_igs, fhir_list_artifacts, fhir_search_artifacts, fhir_list_resource_profiles; default false, and the default output is unchanged) is for LLMs with a tight tool-output budget. Each type becomes an {id: title} map, the common canonical prefix is written once (canonical_base; canonical = canonical_base/<ResourceType>/<id>), and only canonicals that break that rule are listed in canonicals; profiles also list non-active ones in status; data.compact is a one-line reading guide. With all_packages=true the groups sit under packages (packageId#version → that package's group). fhir_list_igs returns default plus manual / dependency maps by install origin (packageId#version → title). Measured on TW Core: fhir_list_resource_profiles 12.9k → 4.8k characters, fhir_list_artifacts (50 rows) 19.9k → 2.8k, fhir_search_artifacts (20 rows) 8.6k → 1.5k, fhir_list_igs (58 packages) 19.6k → 3.7k.
  • For the module concepts and the suggested workflow, see FHIR IG Service.

docs.title: IG discovery
docs.text: Tool Description Key parameters fhir_list_igs List installed IG packages (packageId / version / title / canonical / fhirVersion / status / isDefault / installOrigin (manual = installed by an operator, dependency = fetched for another IG's dependencies) / dependencies) compact fhir_get_ig Details for a single IG: dependencies and artifact counts per resource type; data.deps_missing lists uninstalled dependencies package_id, version fhir_list_artifacts List a summary of the IG's conformance artifacts resource_type, grouping_id, all_packages, limit (50 by default, 200 maximum), compact fhir_search_artifacts Full-text search over artifacts by id / canonical / name / title / description keyword, resource_type, all_packages, limit (20 by default, 100 maximum), compact

docs.title: Profile selection and reading
docs.text: Tool Description Key parameters fhir_list_resource_profiles List selectable resource profiles, grouped by the base resource type they constrain base_type, all_packages, compact fhir_rank_resource_profiles Rank by how well source field keys match profile element paths (advisory only, selectionRequired:true) keys, base_type, limit (5 by default, 20 maximum) fhir_get_profile Summary of a single profile (identity / base / derivation / element count), resolvable by id, canonical, or key; a canonical may be pinned as url|version (an uninstalled version is ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND) identifier fhir_get_profile_elements Read the profile snapshot; view = elements / element / slices / choices / binding / examples profile, view, path, slice_name, limit fhir_get_profile_required_elements List the elements a profile effectively requires: required only when the whole parent chain is required, required slices, choice types, invariant-implied value[x]-or-dataAbsentReason (vs-2 / vs-3 / tw-core-4 style, detected from the expression), and target-implied primary content; each row carries grounding_class (auto / coding / source_fact / workflow_default …), required_by, allowedCodes for small required bindings and a fill hint; derived rows (e.g. Condition.category) also carry the binding's allowedCodes (extensible / preferred too, up to 20 codes) and a derivation rule (see "Derived elements and Must Support" below). Profiled extensions are expanded from their definitions (url, value[x] via ext-1, required sub-extensions), base-datatype children of populated elements are added (Narrative.div, Extension.url …), and profile-specific error invariants are listed under invariants. With instance, slices are matched by their discriminators, so absent slices add nothing profile, instance (draft: populated optional parents add their required children), include_target_implied (true by default), include_mustsupport (false by default; "defaults" = only the mustSupport elements with a fixed / default / derivable value; true = every mustSupport element; added rows carry optional: true), verbosity (compact by default: id / required_by / grounding_class / fixed·pattern·value / choices / allowedCodes / hint, profile-pinned subtrees folded into one copyable value; full adds min / max / types / binding / mustSupport)

docs.title: Derived elements and Must Support
docs.text:
Elements with grounding_class: "derived" are not copied from the record but follow from other filled values. For well-known derived elements, hint starts with derive: and states the rule (each rule paraphrases the published definitions of the codes it names; the citation is derivation_source in verbosity="full"). A rule applies only when the element's binding is the ValueSet the rule describes:

Element Rule (summary) Source Condition.category diagnosed or assessed in this visit (outpatient, admission, discharge) → encounter-diagnosis (and point Condition.encounter at that encounter); an entry of the longitudinal problem list kept across visits → problem-list-item; a diagnosis written in a visit note is encounter-diagnosis even when the disease is chronic FHIR R4 condition-category; US Core Condition Encounter Diagnosis / Problems and Health Concerns Observation.category by what was measured: lab test → laboratory, BP / heart rate / temperature / height / weight … → vital-signs, imaging, exam, survey, social history … FHIR R4 observation-category; R4 Vital Signs profile Encounter.diagnosis.use / .rank admission AD, discharge DD, chief complaint CC, comorbidity CM …; principal diagnosis rank 1, the rest in record order FHIR R4 diagnosis-role; Encounter.diagnosis.rank MedicationRequest.category / MedicationStatement.category / courseOfTherapyType by the setting of the order (inpatient / outpatient / community / discharge); long-term continuous, short course acute FHIR R4 code systems AllergyIntolerance.category / .type / .criticality, Observation.interpretation by the substance; immune vs non-immune reaction; life-threatening → high; against the reference range N / H / L / HH / LL FHIR R4 code systems

Derived elements without a rule get the CodeSystem definitions of the binding's codes in hint (pick the code whose meaning fits the record: …).

mustSupport is not required. include_mustsupport="defaults" adds only the mustSupport elements that need no source fact (a profile fixed value / pattern, a conventional default such as verificationStatus, a derivable value from the table above) and whose parents are all listed; true adds every mustSupport element. Rows added either way carry optional: true and a "may be left out, never refuse over it" hint, and guide says the same. The default (false) output is unchanged except for the derived rows.

docs.title: Terminology / ValueSet
docs.text: Tool Description Key parameters fhir_get_valueset ValueSet definition summary identifier fhir_expand_valueset Expand a ValueSet and list its member codes (resolved locally where possible; whole large external code systems are not enumerated — TOO_BROAD) identifier, limit (500 by default, 2000 maximum) fhir_lookup_code Look up a single code's display name and properties in a CodeSystem (RxNorm from the local rxnorm.concepts); when the code is not found, hint (use fhir_normalize_code) and near_codes (similar codes of an IG CodeSystem) system, code fhir_validate_code Validate whether a system+code belongs to a given ValueSet; returns valid / invalid / unverifiable; value_set may be pinned as url|version system, code, value_set fhir_normalize_code Free text (Chinese or English, abbreviations, chart wording) → candidate codes: SNOMED CT / LOINC / ICD-10 and any CodeSystem of an installed IG (e.g. the NHI payment codes medical-service-payment-tw, see IG Concept Search). IG candidates carry matched_term, matched_language, group/siblings and linked (codes of other systems the concept links to, e.g. a drug's ATC code); system may be a canonical, id or alias (nhi_payment). Drugs: Taiwan NHI drug codes are supported — system="medication-nhi-tw" (TW Core) or "nhi-medication" (TWPAS), text = brand or generic name in English or Chinese (Glucophage 500mg, 脈優錠 5mg); when the default IG ships only an excerpt of a CodeSystem (TW Core 1.0.0 medication-nhi-tw: 35 codes) and another installed package holds the full list (TW Core 0.3.2: 44,709 codes), the full copy is searched unless package_id / version is given (noted in warnings and data.codesystem_copies). ATC: no searchable WHO ATC is held (TW Core medcation-atc-tw has only 27 Taiwan-specific codes) — look up the NHI drug; its candidate's linked is its ATC code (from the bundled NHI medication supplement) text, value_set, system, limit (10 by default)

docs.title: Authoring, assembly, and validation
docs.text:
Tool Description Key parameters fhir_get_resource_skeleton Generate an empty draft from a profile containing only required / mustSupport structure; required is the element's own min≥1, effectiveRequired also requires every ancestor to be required profile, candidate_limit (20 by default, capped at 100), include_examples (true by default) fhir_finalize_resource Finalise a draft already written as FHIR JSON against its profile and validate it: pins fixed / pattern values only where the draft has the parent node (slice members and _slice tags at any depth included), never adds clinical content; repair="content" (default) first applies the same content repairs as fhir_finalize_bundle (see "Content repair") and returns changes / repair_issues; with field values use fhir_author_resources (see "Authoring from field values") profile, draft, context_id, key, generate_narrative (true by default), repair (content / ids), timezone, site_config fhir_resolve_reference Resolve resource references by temporary key (for linking inside a Bundle) key, resource_type, context_id, display fhir_build_bundle Assemble several resources into a Bundle: a key becomes a deterministic UUID v5 fullUrl (the same input always yields the same Bundle), references written inside resources as key, urn:uuid:<key> or <Type>/<key> are rewired to the generated fullUrl, and an invalid fullUrl is normalised by the fhir_finalize_bundle rules. data.changes lists every rewrite, data.unresolved the references no entry matches (1.2.0) entries, bundle_type (transaction by default), context_id fhir_finalize_bundle Call before emitting the final Bundle: it normalises fullUrl, reference and id (see "Bundle finalisation" below) and, with repair="content" (default), corrects content errors whose fix is uniquely determined — never guessing, undecidable ones reported with candidates (see "Content repair"; repair="ids" = ids only); numbers keep the caller's spelling (10.0 stays 10.0). Returns the finalised bundle, every change as changes[{path, from, to, rule}], the references it could not decide as unresolved[{path, reference, candidates}], notes and id_map. bundle_type sets Bundle.type (a profile-fixed type is never overridden) bundle, package_id, version, bundle_profile (canonical or id of the target Bundle profile; defaults to meta.profile), bundle_type (R4 bundle-type code), repair (content default / ids), timezone (the site timezone: a UTC offset or an IANA name), site_config (facility settings text; a timezone: line gives the timezone) fhir_validate_resource Validate a single resource (structure + terminology bindings); falls back to meta.profile when profile is omitted. An optional source_text adds a grounding check (see below) resource, profile, source_text, site_config, evidence_map, grounding, grounding_verbosity fhir_validate_bundle Validate an entire Bundle (each entry against its meta.profile, plus reference integrity inside the Bundle). ID-class errors (UUIDs must be valid…, unresolved references, missing fullUrl, bdl-7, invalid id) carry suggestions and a Bundle-level id_map / id_changes; with normalize_ids=true the Bundle is finalised first and validated as normalized_bundle (see "Bundle finalisation" below). An optional source_text adds a grounding check and merges the results (see further below) bundle, normalize_ids (false by default), repair (ids default / content, with normalize_ids), source_text, site_config, evidence_map, grounding, grounding_verbosity

fhir_validate_resource / fhir_validate_bundle also report whether validation was complete: checked_fully (true when every profile and ValueSet was checked and the dependency closure is complete), profiles_unchecked, valuesets_unchecked. valid keeps HL7 semantics (an unresolvable profile is only a warning), so valid: true with checked_fully: false means part of the content was not checked. When definition / terminology lookups failed during the run because of database trouble, lookups_failed (the count) is added; such a run always carries an error issue with code: "exception" and valid is false (1.6.1). |version canonicals (meta.profile, binding, targetProfile, type profile, extension url) are resolved like HL7 validator_cli 7.0.1.

The builtin validator also checks, like HL7 validator_cli 7.0.1 (same release, 1.6.0):

  • Where an extension may be used: the extension definition's context (element / extension types; contexts restricted to other FHIR versions by version-specific-use are skipped) and contextInvariant. A violation is an error at the host element: The extension <url> v<version> is not allowed to be used at this point (this element is [...]; allowed for this version = e:...) or ... (based on context invariant '...'). fhirpath contexts are not evaluated locally (never an error).
  • An unversioned StructureDefinition resolves to the highest-version copy in the closure (e.g. the hl7.fhir.uv.extensions.r4 extension over the R4 core one with the same URL), so the extension's own invariants (e.g. var-1 of variable) are checked too.
  • Unrecognized property is judged against the core definitions for the whole resource (as the HL7 JSON parser does), including below a choice type the profile does not allow and inside the value of an unknown extension; like HL7, nothing is checked below an element with the wrong JSON shape (an array for a single element).
  • RxNorm: code and display are checked against rxnorm.concepts (tx.fhir.org accepts every SAB=RXNORM name of the RXCUI, case-insensitively): Wrong Display Name '...' for http://www.nlm.nih.gov/research/umls/rxnorm#<code>. Valid display is '...'. An unknown code is an error only when the local RxNorm release is not older than tx.fhir.org's (03022026), otherwise a warning; when only the preferred name is held (imported before migration 20261030) a display mismatch is a warning; without RxNorm loaded: warning Display not checked (RxNorm).
  • Unknown code in an IG CodeSystem with content = complete stays an error; when another installed package has a fuller copy of the same CodeSystem containing the code (e.g. TW Core 0.3.2 medication-nhi-tw), an information issue names that package and version.
  • A Coding element bound directly to a ValueSet (e.g. Encounter.class) whose system is a ValueSet URL only gets the binding warning, no The Coding references a value set error (as HL7).

1.7.0 (validator v13, evaluation report v13) adds:

  • A ValueSet canonical written as Coding.system: an IG ValueSet (e.g. https://twcore.mohw.gov.tw/ig/twcore/ValueSet/laboratory-code-tw) written as the system of a coding inside a CodeableConcept (or of a Coding that is not directly bound), when the same resource / Bundle has an element bound to that ValueSet (or to a ValueSet that includes it — laboratory-code-tw includes loinc-observation-code), gets the error The Coding references a value set, not a code system ('<url>') at …coding[i].system (HL7 Terminology_TX_System_ValueSet2), replacing the warning A definition for CodeSystem … could not be found. 1.6.x reported it for HL7 core / THO ValueSets only (those still error in any context). Basis (confirmed item by item with validator_cli 7.0.1 and 7.0.3): the CLI recognises an IG ValueSet as such only once its run has loaded it — after it checked an element bound to it, the coding is an error (a previous coding of the same CodeableConcept, another element of the resource, an earlier Bundle entry, an earlier file of a batch); the same resource is only a warning the first time it appears in a JVM; a ValueSet never checked as a binding (medication-path-tw; medication-nhi-tw / medication-fda-tw, bound only on medication[x].coding slices) stays a warning even in a batch. We apply the order-independent version: an error whenever the validated resource / Bundle checks a binding to that ValueSet anywhere, otherwise the warning. A directly bound Coding element (Encounter.class, ImagingStudy.series.modality) keeps only the binding warning. These errors carry suggestions: candidates from normalising the code / display within that ValueSet and the CodeSystems it includes (replace_coding), and the CodeSystems it includes (replace_system, the one holding the code first).
  • LOINC property filters decide membership: = / in filters of a ValueSet compose on http://loinc.org (CLASSTYPE (number or a name such as Laboratory class), CLASS, STATUS, COMPONENT, PROPERTY, TIME_ASPCT, SYSTEM, SCALE_TYP, METHOD_TYP, concept in) are evaluated from the local loinc.concepts; codes not held locally and other operators (regex, is-a …) stay undecidable. Binding checks of ValueSets such as laboratory-code-tw against LOINC codes are therefore no longer just "could not be confirmed".

New in 1.6.1 (validator v8, evaluation report v6):

  • An unresolvable CodeSystem URL is an error on every element: a Coding.system / Quantity.system in the HL7 spaces (http://hl7.org/fhir…, http://terminology.hl7.org/…) that no installed package defines gets No definition could be found for URL value '…' at the system element (Coding, CodeableConcept, Encounter.class, Identifier.type, Meta.tag, extension values, contained resources and nested Bundles alike). Under http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/… only the HL7 validator's SIDUtilities list is known (ndc, icpc-2, icd-9, icd-10, cvx, srt, icd-10-cm, icd-9-cm, dsm5 …); icd-10-pcs, us-mbi etc. are not, so they get this URL error on any element (1.6.0 treated them as known and missed them). The code itself keeps the warning A definition for CodeSystem '…' could not be found (HL7 UNKNOWN_CODESYSTEM); an unknown system outside the HL7 spaces (an IG's own URLs …) also only gets that warning, as in validator_cli.
  • Whitespace in a reference (Patient/ 123, a trailing blank): error The reference '…' is not a valid reference (HL7 REFERENCE_REF_INVALID_REF).
  • An RxNorm display naming another drug: when the display shares no drug-name word with any known name of the RXCUI (preferred name + alt_names; strengths, units, dose forms, routes, salts and function words are stripped first, a ≥5-letter common prefix counts as the same word), or contains no Latin letters at all (a Chinese brand name), it is an error even when only the preferred name is held locally: Wrong Display Name '…' for …#<code>. Valid display is '…'; the display denotes a different concept: …. Another wording of the same drug (synonym, salt, form) stays a warning until rxnorm_import has loaded alt_names, after which it is an error as at tx.fhir.org. SNOMED / LOINC / ICD / CVX displays were already errors (validator_cli too) and are unchanged.
  • Failed lookups are never a pass: when any definition / terminology lookup fails during a validation because of database trouble (connection lost, recovery mode, timeouts; missing tables / columns excepted), the result carries an extra error issue (code: "exception", Validation incomplete: N … lookups failed …), valid: false, checked_fully: false and lookups_failed; an exception inside the validator itself now returns a normal result with a fatal exception issue instead of a failed tool call.
  • fhir_validate_bundle: an entry without a usable resource (written as an array, no resourceType) has no entries row; its issues (e.g. must be a simple value, not an Array) are now listed in the Bundle-level issues instead of being lost.

docs.title: Bundle finalisation (fhir_finalize_bundle / normalize_ids)
docs.text:
Models — weaker ones especially — write readable but malformed identities: fullUrl: "urn:uuid:patient-1", references as Patient/patient-1 or a bare id, Bundle.id as a urn. None of this is clinical content, yet the official validator rejects the whole Bundle. fhir_finalize_bundle hands that numbering-and-wiring work to the tool. Every rule comes from the FHIR R4 core specification or from the package's StructureDefinitions — nothing is special-cased per IG:

Rule What it does fullUrl-uuid (mandatory) Valid values are kept (lowercase urn:uuid:<UUID>, urn:oid:, absolute http(s)://); an uppercase UUID is lowercased; anything else (a label, missing, empty) gets a deterministic UUID v5: fixed namespace, seeded by (resourceType, original fullUrl, resource.id, entry position) plus a Bundle-level salt (SHA-256 of the Bundle with the rewritable fields stripped), so the same input always yields the same output and different Bundles never collide reference-rewire (mandatory) Every Reference-typed element is located through the resource's StructureDefinition snapshot (the profile when meta.profile resolves, else the core definition) — including extension valueReference (definition resolved by url / slice), Composition.section.entry, Provenance.target, datatype children such as Identifier.assigner, backbone elements and contained resources. The original fullUrl, a case-different UUID, Type/id (matching resource.id) and a bare id all map to the same entry and are rewritten to its final fullUrl. A bare id / type-less form that matches several entries is disambiguated by the element's targetProfile types; still ambiguous or missing → listed in unresolved with same-type entries as candidates, never guessed. #contained, absolute URLs outside the Bundle and identifier-only logical references are left alone; …/_history/v is resolved with the version kept resource-id (mandatory) A resource.id / Bundle.id outside [A-Za-z0-9\-.]{1,64} takes its last segment (urn:uuid:… → the UUID); if still invalid, resource.id becomes the entry's UUID and Bundle.id a generated value bdl-7 Duplicate fullUrls are only reported (notes), never merged or dropped; references to a duplicated label become unresolved with both candidates bundle-type / document-order (profile-driven, or requested by the caller) When the StructureDefinition of bundle_profile (or meta.profile) fixes Bundle.type (fixed / pattern) it is set; a caller-supplied bundle_type (R4 bundle-type code) is applied as rule bundle-type with reason: "requested by caller (bundle_type)", but a profile-fixed type always wins (the conflict is only noted); for type=document the Composition is moved to the first entry. A document with no Composition at all is never retyped on its own: notes names both ways out — bundle_type=<the type the entries' shape supports> or adding a Composition. Elements the profile requires with real values (Bundle.identifier, Bundle.timestamp …) are only reported in notes, never generated

Apart from those fields the output Bundle is identical to the input (deep copy, key order preserved), numbers included: the HTTP layer parses the request with JSON.parse, which turns 10.0 into 10, 1e3 into 1000 and rounds integers beyond 2^53, while a FHIR decimal's precision is part of its value. So fhir_finalize_bundle, the normalized_bundle of fhir_validate_bundle(normalize_ids=true), the entry resources of fhir_build_bundle and the resource of fhir_finalize_resource re-read the bundle / entries / draft argument losslessly from the raw request text; the finalisation still runs on the ordinary tree (UUIDs, changes and validation are unchanged) and only at the end is each number swapped back to the caller's spelling (10.0, 1.50, 0.50, -0.0, 12345678901234567890, inside extensions and nested arrays too; only where the value is the same). All three entry points (/mcp, POST /tools/<name>, the admin console playground) return the same bytes. An already valid Bundle is returned unchanged with changes: [], and finalising a finalised Bundle changes nothing. Without package_id the package is resolved from bundle_profile / meta.profile; when no IG resolves, hl7.fhir.r4.core is used.

fhir_validate_bundle shares the engine: by default (normalize_ids=false) ID-class errors carry suggestions (replace_fullurl / replace_reference / replace_id / move_entry / replace_bundle_type) and data gains the full map id_map (old → new), id_changes (every path that must change together) and id_unresolved; a Bundle without ID-class issues is byte-identical to 1.6.1. With normalize_ids=true the Bundle is finalised first, the normalised Bundle is validated and returned as normalized_bundle with id_changes, and each fixed problem is noted as an information issue. fhir_get_profile_required_elements on a Bundle profile additionally returns bundle_rules (fullUrl format, references = the target's fullUrl, id format, a profile-fixed Bundle.type — or the hint that fhir_finalize_bundle's bundle_type sets a free one —, document / message ordering, required elements and entry slices), likewise generated from the core specification and the StructureDefinition.

docs.title: Content repair (repair="content")
docs.text:
fhir_finalize_bundle / fhir_finalize_resource take repair, default "content": besides the id normalisation above they correct content errors whose fix is uniquely determined; repair="ids" is exactly 1.1.0 / 1.5.0 (ids only). fhir_validate_bundle accepts repair="content" with normalize_ids=true. fhir_author_resources / fhir_assemble_bundle always apply the same rules (node-server/src/fhirRepair/ — one input, one verdict, one repair in every tool). Every correction is listed in changes[{path, from, to, rule, reason}]; a value that cannot be decided uniquely is left as written and listed in repair_issues[{path, rule, message, candidates}], the validator's error stays (and carries repair).

rule Corrects Left as written and reported display the code exists and the display is the same concept written differently → the official display; the original wording moves to an empty CodeableConcept.text. Method: (a) equal to one of the valid displays / designations the validator lists (other languages, LOINC long / short names) after normalisation — NFKC, case, punctuation, word order, plural, roman numerals (Type II ↔ Type 2), SNOMED semantic tag, initialism; (b) otherwise the display is searched in the code's own system (fhir_normalize_code): this code ranks first, exactly or sharing at least half its words with a valid display another code ranks first (SNOMED 428921007 with "Pneumonia" → 233604007), the code ranks only lower, no search available — a different meaning: not changed, the candidates are the codes the display denotes; ancestors / descendants count as different ucum a Quantity (any Quantity-typed element, component[].valueQuantity included) with no code, a code that is not valid UCUM, or a LOINC code (8310-5) as code gets the UCUM code its unit / code text determines, plus system: UCUM names / synonyms / symbols (mmHg → mm[Hg], °C/℃/degC → Cel), the <count word>/<time unit> grammar (次/分 → /min, mg/天 → mg/d), the micro sign / Greek mu for the UCUM prefix u and bracketed units written without brackets (μIU/mL → u[IU]/mL), a factor glued to a unit in a divisor (a decimal one as an annotation: mL/min/1.73m2 → mL/min/{1.73_m2}; an integer one: mg/24h → mg/(24.h)); it must fit the profile's fixed code or required UCUM ValueSet (min where /min is fixed is read as /min; a spelling equal to exactly one allowed code at conversion factor 1 becomes that code: 1/min → /min). A LOINC code as code with no unit, or a value with neither code nor unit: when the profile allows exactly one unit (fixed / pattern, or a required ValueSet of one code) it is set directly (reason in changes: "the profile allows only "; the unit text too when the profile requires one), otherwise — for the LOINC case — error quantity-code-not-ucum ("valueQuantity.code holds a LOINC code, not a UCUM unit; give the unit") the evidence disagrees (code g, unit kg), the derived code is not allowed (K for a body temperature), nothing derivable; a system naming another real CodeSystem is never touched roc-date ROC (民國) dates in date / dateTime / instant: marked (民國 / ROC) or three-digit years (115-10-03, 115/10/03, 115-10-03T16:05:00, 民國115年10月3日) → +1911, precision kept; a time keeps its own offset, else takes the site timezone (see timezone below) one- or two-digit years (99-10-03) are ambiguous; a time without offset while the site timezone is unknown (error, code: timezone-required); four-digit years are not this rule's business timezone a Gregorian dateTime / instant with a time but no UTC offset ("If a date has a time, it must have a timezone") → the site timezone is added (seconds completed). The site timezone comes from, in order: the timezone argument (+08:00 or an IANA name such as Asia/Taipei, resolved at that local time, DST aware) → a timezone line of site_config (- 時區：+08:00, timezone: Asia/Taipei; label 時區 / timezone / time zone / tz / UTC offset) → the same line in the 【院所設定】 section of source_text the site timezone is unknown (error timezone-required, saying how to give it); site_config names several timezones; the wall time does not exist or is ambiguous in the IANA zone (a DST change) system a Coding.system that is not absolute (ICD-10-CM, LOINC, SNOMED CT, loinc.org, an OID), a ValueSet URL (the HL7 core URL without /ValueSet/, http://hl7.org/fhir/condition-code, included), or a URL that resolves to nothing (…/ns/fhir/CodeSystem#icd-10-cm, …/CodeSystem/_ActMedicalServiceCode, …/CodeSystem/v3-ActEncounterCode) → the one CodeSystem holding the code among those it names: installed CodeSystems' name / title / id / URL tail / identifier, the FHIR R4 external code system list, the URL's fragment / last segment, a THO abstract _ code, a THO / core ValueSet named by the URL's last segment (the CodeSystem the code has in it), the element's bound ValueSets; failing all of these, the installed CodeSystems with a similar name (equal after dropping v2- / v3- and punctuation, one a prefix of the other, or ≥ 80% Levenshtein similarity) — renamed / retired names (v3-AdmitSource → admit-source, v3-GTS → v3-GTSAbbreviation) — only when exactly one holds the code and the element's required / extensible binding (when decidable) accepts it several match, or the code is not in the system named shape lossless reshapes: a Coding given as {coding: [one]} or wrapped in another property (Encounter.class: {type: {...}}), a Coding nested in a Coding's code, a CodeableConcept given as a bare Coding, a required-bound code element given as a CodeableConcept with one coding / a Coding (reaction.severity → "moderate"; the code must be in the ValueSet and no display / text is lost), a one-item array for a single element, a single value for a repeating one, a property misplaced where exactly one neighbour defines it (Dosage.doseQuantity → doseAndRate[0].doseQuantity, entry.meta → entry.resource.meta, Timing.route → Dosage.route, doseAndRate.unit → doseAndRate.doseQuantity.unit, doseAndRate[0].timing → Dosage.timing, a request written in the resource → entry.request), a missing resourceType when meta.profile names one resource type. The Bundle itself: no resourceType but a proper entry array → "Bundle" (before the INVALID_ARGUMENT check; with repair="ids" the error names the location); keys such as "entry[1]", "entry2" → the entry array rebuilt in key-number order; duplicate fullUrls (bdl-7) with deep-equal resources → the later copies dropped several codings, a text that differs from the display, several possible places, duplicate numbers or numbers inside an existing entry array, different resources under one fullUrl; the message shows the correct shape with an example empty empty elements (ele-1): a value {}, [], "" or null is removed (a parent left empty goes in the next pass) a null carrying _x extensions is kept fixed-slice a required (min ≥ 1) Coding / CodeableConcept slice whose content the profile fully fixes (fixed / pattern) and that is absent → added (a pulse-oximetry profile requiring two fixed codings in code.coding, vital-signs category:VSCat); the new value must belong to the slice by its discriminators a required child of the slice is not fixed, an item of the slice is already there, the element's max would be exceeded code a required-bound code written as one code's display or in another case (periodUnit: "hour" → h), complete local expansions of ≤ 200 codes only several or none match

Never adds an error: each resource is validated before and after; when the repaired resource has an error it did not have (a display error revealed by a corrected system, profile rules that apply once meta.profile is moved in), the responsible changes are withdrawn and explained in repair_issues (warning, not applied: …). Exception (evaluator decision): when the only new error after a system correction is the display check of that same Coding (Wrong Display Name … for <new system>#<code>), the error existed semantically before — the system correction is kept and listed in changes, and the display error stays reported by the display rule with the candidates the model's display denotes; any other new error still withdraws the change. Since v14.1 the whole Bundle is validated before and after as well: an error only the Bundle context shows (reference targets, entry slices, document rules) also withdraws the change behind it (traced by the error's path and the entries / fullUrls its message names; when it cannot be traced, nothing is applied). The Bundle envelope repairs (resourceType, the rebuilt entry array) make the Bundle readable by the validator at all and are the baseline of that comparison. The same input always gives the same output, a repaired Bundle repaired again yields changes: [], and numbers keep their spelling.

docs.title: Fix suggestions (suggestions / caused_by)
docs.text:
Besides saying what is wrong, validation issues carry, where possible, "what to change it to": suggestions is a list of candidates ordered by confidence (at most 5 per issue; up to 12 for a binding error on a small ValueSet), and reference-chain errors get caused_by. Both are additive — the set of issues, their severity and message, and valid are unchanged; the field is absent when there is no suggestion.

{"severity": "error", "path": "MedicationRequest.dosageInstruction[0].timing.repeat", "message": "Unrecognized property 'periodUnits'",
 "suggestions": [{"value": "periodUnit", "kind": "rename_property", "confidence": 0.82, "reason": "closest element name at this level: 'periodUnit'",
                  "patch": {"op": "move", "from": "MedicationRequest.dosageInstruction[0].timing.repeat.periodUnits", "path": "MedicationRequest.dosageInstruction[0].timing.repeat.periodUnit"}}]}
Error kind Suggestion Unknown code 'X' in the CodeSystem 'http://unitsofmeasure.org' replace_code The closest valid UCUM: case (UCUM is case-sensitive), square brackets ([U] → U, [UI]/mL → [iU]/mL), prefix + unit from the UCUM table, common clinical spellings (mcg → ug, mmHg → mm[Hg]), and an annotation for dose-form words that are not units (tab → {tablet}); every candidate is checked with the same UCUM parser the validator uses No definition could be found for URL value 'U', A definition for CodeSystem 'S' could not be found, The Coding references a value set, not a code system replace_system The CodeSystem(s) the misused ValueSet (or the ValueSet of that name) draws from (…/CodeSystem/v3-ActEncounterCode → …/CodeSystem/v3-ActCode), and the closest canonical in the package closure; when the Coding has a code, systems that hold it rank first Unrecognized property 'p' rename_property / move_property / remove_property In order: the closest element name at the same level (case, spelling; datatype children and typed names of choice elements included, e.g. value → valueQuantity); the level of this resource where an element of that name actually lives (ancestors, descendants up to three levels including datatype children, sibling backbones / datatypes of an ancestor; timing.periodUnit → timing.repeat.periodUnit, dosageInstruction[0].note → MedicationRequest.note, Patient.city → Patient.address[0].city); a sibling that means the same and whose type fits the value (lower confidence; evidence from the FHIR element's alias / short and a small table of FHIR-generic synonyms: every: 8 next to periodUnit → period, upperLimit in a Range → high, zip → postalCode, comment → note); only when none of these exists, removal (patch.op = remove), with a reason that lists the level's element names (capped at 14) and the other resource types that carry the name (reasonCode on an Observation → "an element of Encounter, Procedure …") The type 'date' is not allowed for Condition.onset[x] rename_property The typed name of an allowed type that fits the value (onsetDate → onsetDateTime) Value not in a required / extensible ValueSet choose_code Codes of the expanded ValueSet: a ValueSet of ≤ 50 codes is always listed whole (the expansion takes no lookup budget), ranked by string similarity; a small one (≤ 12) whose codes resemble nothing is ranked by meaning instead (embedding endpoint; string order when unavailable); for a large one the closest to the given code / display (incl. fhir_normalize_code) Value not in the element's ValueSet, but a valid code of another bound element of the same resource (criticality: "severe" → reaction[0].severity) move_value The instance path of the element the value belongs to (patch.op = move): elements with a required / extensible binding and a compatible type (code → code, CodeableConcept → CodeableConcept) are read from the snapshots of the resource's profiles (meta.profile / the validation's profile) and base definition, membership confirmed with the validator's own check; lower confidence when the target already has a value Unknown code in other CodeSystems replace_code / replace_system Spelling repairs the validator accepts (case, ICD dot, LOINC hyphen), codes whose name matches the display / text (fhir_normalize_code), near codes of an IG CodeSystem, and another terminology whose code shape fits (a LOINC code under the SNOMED system); when the code exists in another CodeSystem included by the element's bound ValueSet (slice bindings included — an IG-local CodeSystem/v2-0203 next to the HL7 CodeSystem of that name in identifier-type-tw) or in the CodeSystem of the same name under another base → replace_system (0.9; 0.6 when the ValueSet enumerates only some codes of that CodeSystem and not this one) No definition could be found for URL value 'U' where U is a Coding.system and the Coding has a code / display replace_coding / replace_system The element's bound ValueSets are read from the profile / base snapshots (slices, the .coding child, maxValueSet / additional bindings) and the Coding's display / code is normalised within them (fhir_normalize_code) → a whole {system, code, display} (oral in dosageInstruction.route → SNOMED 26643006 Oral route, TW medication-path-tw PO 口服), value = the code with system / display alongside; plus the CodeSystems those ValueSets draw from (0.9 for one that holds the code, 0.35 otherwise) Wrong Display Name replace_display (+ replace_code) The valid display(s) the validator names (uniform across terminologies); if the written display is the name of another code, also a code change Unable to find a profile match for urn:uuid:X caused_by The referenced resource's own errors (fullUrl, entry, path, message); when it has none, its errors against the profile the reference requires (with profile); when X is a label-style reference, also a replace_reference UUIDs must be valid and lowercase, missing fullUrl, URN reference is not locally contained, Entry N matches … by type and id, Relative Reference … missing a fullUrl, Invalid Resource id, bdl-7 / bdl-11 replace_fullurl / replace_reference / replace_id / move_entry / replace_bundle_type The deterministic value fhir_finalize_bundle would apply (always the same for the same input); an unresolvable reference lists the fullUrls of same-type entries as lower-confidence candidates; the whole map is in data.id_map / id_changes (see "Bundle finalisation") Constraint failed: bdl-11 (a document with no Composition at all; bdl-12 for message / MessageHeader likewise; the consequent bdl-9 / bdl-10 get only the first kind) replace_value / add_resource 1. Bundle.type → a type the entries' shape supports: no request → collection (0.8); every entry carries request → transaction (0.7), plus batch (0.4) when no entry references another; some carry a request → transaction / collection; every entry carries search → searchset. Never suggested when the profile fixes Bundle.type. 2. Add a Composition (or MessageHeader) as the first entry (patch.op = add, Bundle.entry[0]); reason lists the elements the core StructureDefinition requires (status, type, date, author, title …). A Composition that exists but is not first is handled by move_entry in the row above

patch uses the validator's dotted paths (op: replace / move / remove; move also has from; a move into a repeating element that does not exist yet carries [0]). confidence is a heuristic score, not a probability, but the bands per kind are fixed: exact / case rename > move > semantic rename > remove; suggestions are an aid — validate again after applying one. Suggestions are deterministic for the same input; if computing one fails, that issue simply has none and the validation result is unaffected. Evaluation method and figures: node-server/scripts/suggestions-eval/.

In-process validation is based on profile snapshots and terminology bindings, benchmarked against HL7 validator_cli 7.0.1 (method and results in node-server/scripts/validator-audit/). It is not equivalent to conformance certification by the official HL7 FHIR Validator.

docs.title: Authoring from field values
docs.text:
The model no longer writes FHIR JSON: it gives field values, the MCP composes the resource for the profile, validates it, keeps it in a per-task context and assembles the Bundle from a list of keys. Every rule comes from the resolved package's StructureDefinitions / ValueSets and FHIR R4 core — no IG-specific special cases (TW Core, TWPAS or any other installed IG alike).

Tool Description Key parameters fhir_get_authoring_fields The profile's "writing form": fields (required / expected / commonly used in the IG's own examples, reason in why), more (the remaining mustSupport fields and record links) and omitted (dropped for size, never silent). Record links: an optional backbone the IG neither marks mustSupport nor uses in its examples, but whose required Reference child targets a profile of the same IG (same canonical base) of a non-entity type (not a person / organisation master-data type such as Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location), e.g. Encounter.diagnosis, is listed in fields with all its children (condition, use, rank) and the example {condition: {ref: "condition"}}; a direct reference to such a profile (Encounter.reasonReference, Condition.encounter, Procedure.reasonReference, Observation.hasMember / derivedFrom) is in more with targets. The whole response (envelope, warnings, provenance; non-ASCII counted as \uXXXX) stays within 6,000 characters (150 kept as a margin); its length is data.response_chars. Each field has kind + format (how to write the value), source (record / facility / code / fixed / default / derived), small binding.codes, targets and children; fields with auto: true are filled by the MCP (value shows what), pins shows what the profile fixes inside a field you still fill (identifier system, component code, unit).
