A conventional default is auto only on a required element; an optional one (Patient.active …) is listed as a plain optional field whose format / example only hint at the conventional value profile, package_id, version, include_more (true by default) fhir_author_resources Author several resources in one call (8 or more is fine): {key, profile, fields}; the MCP adds meta.profile, fixed / pattern values, slices, workflow defaults of required elements, derivable values (e.g. Condition.category when an encounter is given), displays, UCUM units, ROC → ISO dates and applies the corrections below, then validates and stores each in the context. Returns {context_id, storage, results[{key, status, resource, provenance, missing, refs, issues, notes}], summary, settings} context_id (omit on the first call), resources, timezone, apply_defaults (required / none), site_config fhir_context Inspect or trim a context: list (status and references per key), get (one key's full result), delete (one key or the whole context) context_id, action, key fhir_assemble_bundle Build the Bundle from a list of keys: each entry's fullUrl is the key's deterministic urn:uuid; the Bundle is finalised by the fhir_finalize_bundle rules and validated like fhir_validate_bundle (grounding too with source_text); every issue carries the key and the model's field name context_id, keys, bundle_type, bundle_profile, identifier, timestamp, source_text, site_config, allow_invalid

Flow

  1. Plan one key per resource (patient-1, enc-1, cond-1, obs-wbc …).
  2. Call fhir_get_authoring_fields(profile) once per profile.
  3. Call fhir_author_resources without context_id for the first batch and keep data.context_id; cross references are {ref: "<key>"} and may point at a key not authored yet (status refs_pending, resolved at assembly); cycles (Encounter.diagnosis ↔ Condition.encounter) are fine.
  4. Fix a status: invalid resource by resending the same key with merge: true and only the changed fields (null removes a field); issues carry key, field (your field name), path (FHIR path) and suggestions.
  5. fhir_assemble_bundle(context_id, keys, bundle_type); for a document Bundle, author the Composition first (section.entry as {ref}) and pass identifier / timestamp from the record (bdl-9 / bdl-10).

Value grammar

Kind Accepted forms string / code / boolean / integer / decimal the JSON scalar; numbers keep their spelling (12.50 stays 12.50, 1e2 stays 1e2) coding / codeableConcept {system, code, display?}; several codes as an array; {text} or a plain string when there is no required binding quantity {value, unit} (unit text or UCUM; the MCP adds the UCUM system / code) or the string "95 mg/dL" date / dateTime / instant ISO 2026-06-15, 2026-06-15T06:00, or ROC 115/06/15, 115/06/15 06:00 (precision kept). A time without an offset needs timezone (e.g. "+08:00", remembered on the context), otherwise it is an error — an offset is never guessed period {start, end?} with the date forms above identifier {value, system?, type?}; a slice as identifier:medicalRecord reference {ref: "<key>"} (a resource in the same context) or {reference: "Patient/123"} (external) choice value[x] give value; its shape picks the type (quantity → valueQuantity, {system, code} → valueCodeableConcept …), or name it (valueQuantity) component [{code, value}] or component:<slice> {value} extension slice extension:<slice> with {value: …} or the bare value ({ref}, {system, code} …); the MCP writes {url, value[x]} from the extension's definition; FHIR JSON that already carries url is kept as written dosage {text?, route?, dose?, frequency?/timing?, period?, asNeeded?}

Rules: model values win (only fixed / pattern values override, a conflict is reported as an error; a display the terminology rejects is replaced as described under "Corrections"); values only the record or the facility knows (dates, numbers, identifiers, names, doses, the time zone, Bundle.identifier / timestamp) are never invented — they are listed in missing; values the MCP supplies are marked fixed / default / derived / lookup in provenance.

Corrections (listed in results[].notes)

  • The display follows the code: a display the model wrote that the terminology rule (the same check fhir_validate_resource runs) rejects for a resolvable code is replaced by the code's display (provenance lookup, note display replaced for <field> (was '<old>')); when that CodeableConcept has no text, the model's wording moves into .text (provenance model) so nothing is lost. A case-only difference is valid; a whitespace-only one takes the valid spelling without a note. This rule never changes the code; when the code does not resolve the model's display is kept (validation reports the unknown code). Example: LOINC 1988-5 with display CRP → display C reactive protein [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma, text CRP.
  • System correction (1.2.0): the model's Coding.system is changed only in the two cases below and only when the answer is unique (provenance lookup, note system corrected for <field>: …); everything else is left as written for validation to report (with the v10 suggestions) — never guessed:
  • the system is a ValueSet URL (a ValueSet of any installed package, or the /CodeSystem/ ↔ /ValueSet/ twin of one): when the code belongs to exactly one CodeSystem within that ValueSet (expansion / valueSetContains), that CodeSystem is used — e.g. Composition.type written as {system: "https://twcore.mohw.gov.tw/ig/twcore/ValueSet/loinc-type-doc-code", code: "11488-4"} → system: "http://loinc.org" (note '<ValueSet URL>' is a ValueSet; code '11488-4' belongs to http://loinc.org). (1.3.0) When the ValueSet has a filter-defined include (e.g. laboratory-code-tw = a LOINC CLASSTYPE filter + an enumeration of NHI payment codes), its local expansion is only partial and never disproves membership: the code exists in a CodeSystem the ValueSet includes and the filter is decidable and satisfied → corrected, note … belongs to http://loinc.org (membership confirmed); the filter cannot be decided but the code exists in exactly one of the ValueSet's CodeSystems → corrected, note (membership unverifiable; the code exists only in <CS> among the ValueSet's systems). code: {system, code} and the raw form code: {coding: [{system, code}]} behave the same. The code under several CodeSystems of the ValueSet → an error with candidates; the code not in the ValueSet (values that are not codes, such as laboratory, WBC, hs-Troponin I) → not corrected; validation reports the error The Coding references a value set, not a code system (with candidates, see validator 1.7.0), status is invalid, and fhir_assemble_bundle and fhir_validate_bundle give the same verdict.
  • the system URL resolves to no definition (the validator's URL rules: an HL7-space URL only when the HL7 validator reports "No definition could be found for URL value"; not a CodeSystem, a ValueSet or a known external terminology): when exactly one CodeSystem of the element's bound ValueSets (slices and additional bindings included — the fhirSuggestions/bindings.ts binding walk) holds the code, that one is used — exact code first, then case-insensitive (the code then takes the correct spelling), then an exact and unique display (the code becomes that display's code). E.g. MedicationRequest.dosageInstruction.route written as {system: "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/route", code: "PO"} → https://twcore.mohw.gov.tw/ig/twcore/CodeSystem/medication-path-tw (display 口服 per the display rule). Several CodeSystems hold it, or none (e.g. oral) → unchanged; the validation error's suggestions offer replace_coding / replace_system.
  • After a correction the display follows the rule above.
  • A single value is wrapped into an array: a repeating element (max > 1) given one object / scalar gets a one-item array, at any depth, including FHIR shapes the model passes through (code: {coding: {system, code}}, identifier: {…} / telecom: {…} inside a nested object, extension inside an extension written with its url, doseAndRate); note wrapped <path> into an array. One value for a top-level field is the documented grammar and gets no note.

Defaults policy (apply_defaults): "required" (the default) fills a workflow default (Observation.status → final, Encounter.status → finished …) or the profile's defaultValue[x] only on elements the profile requires (min ≥ 1, required slices included) that the model left empty; optional elements (Patient.active, Practitioner.active, Organization.active, Immunization.primarySource, MedicationRequest.dispenseRequest.numberOfRepeatsAllowed, a 0..1 Condition.clinicalStatus …) are never auto-filled — give them when the record states them. "none" fills no default at all; required elements without a value then appear in missing. Remembered on the context (like timezone). Derived values (Condition.category …) are unaffected.

Facility settings (site_config): free text in the format fhir_check_grounding's site_config takes — every http(s) URL in it is an accepted facility identifier system, and its lines ground Organization values and Practitioner identifiers. fhir_author_resources stores it on the context (passing it again only adds lines not stored yet); fhir_assemble_bundle's site_config is merged with the context's; with source_text it goes to the grounding engine, so facility identifier systems and organisation data are grounded as site_config instead of being flagged (G-SYSTEM-NOT-SITE). Never logged and never echoed (settings.site_config_lines reports the line count only). Example:

{"site_config": "MRN system: https://hospital.example.tw/mrn\nOrganization: Example Hospital, facility code 0123456789", "resources": [
  {"key": "patient-1", "profile": "Patient-twcore", "fields": {"identifier:medicalRecord": {"value": "MR-00012345", "system": "https://hospital.example.tw/mrn"}}}
]}

Contexts: a context id is 128 random bits (32 hex), stored in Redis under authoring:ctx:<id>, dropped after 60 minutes idle and refreshed by every call; without Redis an in-process memory store is used (storage: "memory", lost on restart). {ref: key} maps to urn:uuid:<UUID v5(context id, key)> — the same value in single-resource validation and in the final Bundle, so the same context + the same keys always give a byte-identical Bundle. Clinical content is never logged (ids, counts and byte sizes only).

Error codes ({ok: false, data: null, error: {code, message, message_zh, hint, hint_zh, retryable}})

code When Next step CONTEXT_EXPIRED the context id does not exist or expired (never partial results) start over without context_id and re-author every resource with the same keys and fields KEY_NOT_FOUND a key passed to assembly / get is not in the context fhir_context action=list, then author or drop it UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE a resource references a key not in keys or not in the context; error.refused lists key / field / ref_key add ref_key to keys, author it, or change the field with merge INVALID_RESOURCE a stored resource still has validation errors; error.refused lists key / field / error fix with merge and assemble again (allow_invalid=true only if the user explicitly accepts it) MISSING_COMPOSITION a document Bundle without an authored Composition; error.missing.fields lists what it needs author the Composition from the record and put its key first CONTEXT_CONFLICT the same context kept being written from several places at once retry once INVALID_ARGUMENT bad arguments (duplicate key, missing profile, unknown bundle_type, timestamp not an instant …) fix as the message says

Example

{"timezone": "+08:00", "resources": [
  {"key": "patient-1", "profile": "Patient-twcore", "fields": {"identifier:idCardNumber": {"value": "A123456789"}, "name:official": {"text": "王小明"}, "gender": "male", "birthDate": "80/03/15"}},
  {"key": "enc-1", "profile": "Encounter-twcore", "fields": {"class": {"system": "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/v3-ActCode", "code": "IMP"}, "subject": {"ref": "patient-1"}, "period": {"start": "115/06/10 14:30", "end": "2026-06-15T10:00"}, "diagnosis": [{"condition": {"ref": "cond-1"}, "rank": 1}]}},
  {"key": "cond-1", "profile": "Condition-twcore", "fields": {"code": {"system": "http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10-cm", "code": "J18.9"}, "subject": {"ref": "patient-1"}, "encounter": {"ref": "enc-1"}}},
  {"key": "obs-wbc", "profile": "Observation-laboratoryResult-twcore", "fields": {"code": [{"system": "http://loinc.org", "code": "6690-2"}, {"system": "https://twcore.mohw.gov.tw/ig/twcore/CodeSystem/medical-service-payment-tw", "code": "08011C"}], "subject": {"ref": "patient-1"}, "effectiveDateTime": "2026-06-11T06:00", "value": {"value": 12.50, "unit": "10*3/uL"}}}
]}

Fix: {"context_id": "<id>", "resources": [{"key": "obs-wbc", "merge": true, "fields": {"value": "11.8 10*3/uL"}}]}; assemble: {"context_id": "<id>", "keys": ["patient-1", "enc-1", "cond-1", "obs-wbc"], "bundle_type": "collection", "bundle_profile": "Bundle-twcore"}.

fhir_finalize_resource (1.4.0) remains for a draft already written as FHIR JSON: it pins fixed / pattern values only where the draft has the parent node (slice members identified by the slicing discriminators and _slice tags at any depth included; tags are always removed), fills a single-system coding.system, rewrites {reference: <key>} to the context's urn, generates the narrative and validates — it never adds clinical content; with field values use fhir_author_resources instead.

docs.title: Checking against the source record (grounding / completeness)
docs.text:
Conformance-valid is not the same as faithful: a model can fill in a diagnosis code, date or dose the record never states, and the validator still passes. These tools compare a Bundle with the clinical record using deterministic rules (no LLM, no embeddings, no randomness). Code names are looked up in the local database only (ICD-10-CM / PCS, LOINC, SNOMED CT, RxNorm, CVX, IG CodeSystems); no external terminology server is called.

Tool Description Key parameters fhir_check_grounding Check that every clinical fact and code in a Bundle is supported by record text (evidence map or auto-locate), with date / number / unit / ID number / dose / frequency normalisation and section, negation and history rules. The output has the fhir_validate_bundle shape (entries[].issues, issues) plus a grounding summary (units_checked, coverage …) bundle, source_text (required), site_config, evidence_map, mode, verbosity (warnings by default), policy, instruction_markers fhir_check_completeness Gap report: for caller-supplied structured targets (resourceType, item, aliases, codes, date rule), decide whether the record states each required fact; returns found / missing / stated_absent / unknown, the missing list, a template follow-up question and a ready abstention object (insufficient_information) targets, source_text (required), site_config, extracted_facts (facts the model claims; verified, not trusted), instruction_markers

Modes (fhir_check_grounding.mode; grounding on fhir_validate_*)

Mode Elements with evidence Elements without evidence strict The quote is verified (must occur verbatim in the record, value matches, section and context are right) error G-UNGROUNDED auto Same The tool locates supporting record text itself: information G-AUTO-LOCATED when found, an error when not found or found only in the wrong context

Default: strict when an evidence_map is given, otherwise auto. evidence_map is [{path, quote}] or {path: quote}; a path may be Bundle.entry[2].resource.code, entry[2].code, <fullUrl>|code, omit list indices, or use value[x]. Every issue carries rule and source:"grounding", and its message starts with [grounding:<RULE>]. Instruction lines such as 【轉換目標】 (instruction_markers) never count as evidence; site_config can only support identifier.system.

Grounding parameters of fhir_validate_bundle / fhir_validate_resource (backward compatible)

  • No source_text, or grounding="off": the output is byte-identical to the pre-extension version.
  • With source_text: the conformance check runs first, then grounding, and the results are merged: data.conformanceValid (the original valid), data.groundingValid, data.valid = conformanceValid ∧ groundingValid, grounding issues appended per entry to entries[i].issues (Bundle-level ones to issues), entries[i].valid updated, the data.grounding summary, data.source = "builtin+grounding" and provenance.groundingVersion.
  • Callers should check for data.groundingValid in the response; if it is absent the server does not support grounding and the result must not be treated as checked.
  • fhir_validate_resource checks the resource as the only entry of a Bundle and reports issue paths rooted at the resource (e.g. Condition.code); references cannot be followed, so rules that need other resources see no context.

Versions and privacy

  • provenance carries tool, toolVersion, lexiconVersion / lexiconSha256, terminologyVersion and sourceSha256 (first 16 hex chars of the record's SHA-256). health_check reports tools_version, lexicon_version and lexicon_sha256.
  • The record text (source_text) and the site configuration are never written to logs, metric labels or provenance — only sourceSha256; malformed JSON request bodies are not logged either.

The rules and the lexicon (tw-lexicon) follow Taiwanese clinical writing; fhir_check_completeness needs the caller to read the conversion target and pass targets — it does not parse natural-language targets. Results support review; they do not replace a clinician.

docs.title: Does the record actually provide it? (record checks)
docs.text:
When a record deliberately lacks a piece of information, models still tend to "fill something in": "number not yet assigned" as the MRN, a month-only date as Encounter.period.start, a "to be ruled out" diagnosis as an established Condition. Such values can be well-formed — the string may even appear in the record — so both the validator and grounding pass them. Record checks are a post-validation layer (node-server/src/recordChecks/; like the fix suggestions it runs after the validator and never touches InstanceValidator, so the validator parity audit is unaffected) that reports "the record does not actually provide this information".

Report only: no value is ever rewritten or removed; whether to answer insufficient_information instead is the model's decision.

Rule code Needs source_text Severity What it checks R1 information-absent no error The whole value of a field that needs a structured value (Identifier.value, Coding.code, dates, Quantity.value, Reference, names, contact values, Observation.valueString, lot numbers, the text of a CodeableConcept without a code) describes that the information is absent / unknown / pending / not yet available / not established — e.g. 尚未取號, 建檔失敗, 尚在申請, 不詳, 待確認, unknown, pending, not yet assigned. Message: "the record does not provide this information" R2 identifier-format no error (see below) Format by Identifier.system: ROC national ID (http://www.moi.gov.tw) shape and check digit; resident certificate / UI number (http://www.immigration.gov.tw) new and old formats with check digits; no identifier may be a sentence; site_config can set formats for facility systems (MRN, NHI card …) R3 insufficient-precision yes error An event time (Encounter.period, Observation.effective[x] / issued, MedicationRequest.authoredOn, DiagnosticReport, Specimen.collection, Composition.date …, type dateTime / instant) has only the year or month R3 incomplete-value yes error A Quantity that is the element's value (valueQuantity, doseQuantity …) has no value; a medicine given only as free text, with no code and no structured dose R4 unconfirmed-as-confirmed yes error / warning A Condition not marked provisional / differential / unconfirmed while the record's sentences about it say it is not established (待排除, 尚未確立, 鑑別診斷, r/o, differential, not established) → error; only hedged (疑似, 可能, possible, suspected) → warning. No error when the record also confirms it (確診 / 證實 / confirmed) or mentions it without a qualifier R4 symptom-for-unconfirmed-diagnosis yes warning A Condition coded with an ICD-10 symptom code (R00–R99) while the record's (main) diagnosis says "to be ruled out …", and no Condition in the input is provisional / differential (when the record's primary diagnosis slot decides it, the slot rule below reports an error instead) R4 unconfirmed-as-confirmed (primary diagnosis slot) yes error / warning The record's primary diagnosis slot (Dx / Diagnosis / Impression / Assessment / A: / 診斷 / 主診斷 / 臆斷 …) is not established as a whole — differential only (a 鑑別診斷 / DDx / r/o heading), a slot-level cue (未下診斷, 診斷未定, no definitive diagnosis, "no diagnosis until the rapid test", "diagnose after the culture result"), or every item under a cue — and a Condition is not provisional / differential / unconfirmed: it is one of the differential items, its code.text copies the differential list, it is a symptom code (ICD-10 R00–R99, a SNOMED finding by its semantic tag, or a concept the record names only in the complaint / HPI / examination) standing in for the main diagnosis, or it is another diagnosis the record does not establish → error (hedged only: 疑似 / possible → warning). Comorbidities the record establishes elsewhere (past history, plan, a plain item of another primary slot) are not reported R4 information-absent (no diagnosis) yes error A structured record has no diagnosis slot at all (or an empty 「診斷：」) and a Condition (not provisional / differential, not a problem-list-item) is named only in the complaint / HPI / examination, or nowhere in the record R1 information-absent (stated absence, identifier without value) yes error The record writes the field as absent (病歷號：申請中, 採檢日期：無法辨識, 血糖：機器錯誤，未得數值, 處方：待藥師確認), no other line gives it a value, and the Bundle has one → information-absent when the value is not in the record, value-from-other-event when it is another event's (the visit date used as the specimen date). An identifier with a system but no value: information-absent when the record has no such number, incomplete-value (with the number) when it has R5 ungrounded-value yes error (warning for record-keeping times, derived quantities, reference ranges) Every Identifier.value, date / dateTime / instant and Quantity.value must be found in the record (identifiers also in site_config): a normalised match or an explicit derivation (below). Not found → "this value is not in the record", with evidence listing what was searched, the normalised forms tried and the nearest record candidates. A date in the record whose time is not (the typical record date + a filled-in T00:00:00) is an error too; a date-only value matching a record date passes. 0 / negative / 999 values the record does not state are also called out as placeholders R5 value-from-other-event yes error / warning The value is in the record but belongs to another time point, event or field: the record says the first reading failed ("機器錯誤、未得數值") and the second reading's value is written at the first reading's time → error; two readings' values and times swapped → warning; a date the record states only as a past event (上次 / 曾 / previous) or as the birth date → error; a number the record gives as another identifier (the admission number written as the MRN) → error. Reported only when determinable

How R1 avoids false positives: the value must consist ENTIRELY of absence predicates (lexicon record-checks-lexicon, Chinese and English, including the generated variants "尚未 / 還沒 / 待 / 無法 × 取號 / 建檔 / 提供 / 帶來 …" and "…中" / "…失敗"), field nouns (病歷號, 身分證, ID, date …), fillers (家屬說, 目前, yet …) and punctuation, with at least one predicate; any other content (another word, a run of three or more digits) means it is not absent. So 「家族史不詳」 only matters in the one field it is written into, and 「不明原因發燒」, "Hypertension, unspecified" or 「王不明」 are never read as absence. Codes of HL7 / FHIR code systems (gender = unknown, v3-NullFlavor UNK …) are real codes and are not checked. Nil words (無 / none / N/A / -) count only in identifier, date, quantity, name and reference fields.

R2 formats and check digits (system URLs from the identifier slices of TW Core IG v1.0.0 Patient-twcore / Practitioner-twcore)

Format System Rule tw-national-id http://www.moi.gov.tw 1 letter + 1/2 + 8 digits; check digit: the letter maps to a two-digit number (A=10 … in the order ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVXYWZIO), tens ×1 and units ×9, then the 8 digits ×8…×1, plus the check digit; the sum is a multiple of 10. A second character 8/9 points to the resident-certificate system tw-resident-certificate http://www.immigration.gov.tw New format (from 2021-01-02): 1 letter + 8/9 + 8 digits, national-ID check digit; old format (valid until 2030-12-31): 2 letters (second A–D) + 8 digits, the second letter contributes the units digit of its letter value (A→0 … D→3), otherwise as the national ID tw-nhi-card (TW Core defines no system URL; set it in site_config) 12 digits (spaces / hyphens between groups allowed) tw-passport (set in site_config) 9 digits

site_config syntax (one rule per line, in the same text as the other facility settings): identifier-format <system> <format>, where <format> is a format name above or a JavaScript regular expression matched against the whole value, e.g. identifier-format https://hospital.example.tw/mrn [0-9]{7,8}, identifier-format https://hospital.example.tw/nhi-card tw-nhi-card. A site rule replaces the built-in rule of the same system; an invalid regular expression is ignored and listed in record_checks.notes. When only the check digit fails and the record (or site_config) states exactly this value, the issue is a warning (the record itself carries that number — verify it at the source).

How R3 searches the record: dates — every record line (conversion-target, site-settings and family-history lines excluded) is searched for day-precision dates within the same year / month (western, ROC 民國, 年月日 and month-day forms); found → "the record has a more complete value ''" with the record lines, none → "the record does not provide a more complete date". Quantities — lines mentioning the item's name (code.text, display, vital-sign aliases) are searched for a number with a compatible unit after the name. Medicines — lines mentioning the medicine name are searched for a dose (number + mg / g / mcg / mL / IU / tab …), and the name text itself is checked for a dose. evidence states the search scope and result. History-type times (Condition.onset, Procedure.performed, Immunization.occurrence, MedicationStatement.effective …) and date-typed elements (birthDate) are not precision-checked.

R4 scope: the Condition's names (code.text, displays, ICD-10 code) are located in the record and qualified per sentence (。；;): prefix cues (待排除, r/o, 鑑別診斷, 疑似 …) govern up to the next comma, postfix cues (尚未確立, not established, ? …) the same clause or a short clause right after it ("A、B、C，尚未確立"); a whole line of a rule out section counts as explicit. A cue inside a bracket qualifies only the concept inside the bracket: in "A：Elevated PSA（未確立惡性腫瘤）" 未確立 modifies the malignancy, so an Elevated PSA Condition is not reported (an established malignancy Condition is); a bracket holding only a cue ("肺炎（待排除）", "(r/o)", "(?)") qualifies the item before it.

How the primary diagnosis slot is read: the text after the heading (lexicon diagnosisSlot, Chinese + English; 次診斷 / comorbidities are never primary) and its continuation lines (numbered items) are split into items at top-level separators (、 ； , ／ vs 或 …); a leading prefix cue (鑑別 A／B／C, 待排除 A、B, r/o A vs B) governs the items after it on the same line, a trailing cue-only item on a line (…，尚未確立) governs the items before it; a line saying 已排除 / ruled out / 不支持 lists excluded items (neither established nor open). An unqualified item of any primary slot that matches the Condition always counts as established.

How R5 finds values (recordChecks/recordValues.ts): only the record body (the 【轉換目標】 conversion target and the 院所設定 section never count); identifiers are also searched in the whole site_config. - Identifiers: NFKC, case-insensitive, without - _ . / spaces; whole tokens, contiguous joins of separator pieces, leading zeros, a label glued in front (MRN00775310). System-assigned identifiers (urn:uuid, Bundle / Composition / Claim identifiers) are not checked. - Dates: Gregorian, ROC (114/06/10, 民國114年6月10日), 年月日, slashes, month-day (with the record's years), English month names; times as HH:MM(:SS), 上午 / 下午 N 點 M 分, am / pm, HHMM right after a date; a value in another offset is also compared in the site timezone (site_config timezone:, default +08:00). Derivations: 入院第 N 天 / hospital day N / HD#N (admission + N−1), 術後第 N 天 / POD#N (operation + N), 第 N 天, N 天前 / 後, 昨天 / 前天 / 今天 / 隔天 / 次日 / yesterday / next day, N weeks / months before / after, a complaint duration (咳嗽 3 天 → 3 or 2 days before), a course on a treatment line (處方 … 7 天 → start + 6 or 7), N 年前 / N 年 (years), an age (54 歲 → birth year), "N minutes / hours later / before". Chinese numerals are read (入院第三天). Anchors are the record's own dates: the admission date for hospital-day expressions, the operation date for post-op ones, else a date on the same line, else the nearest preceding dated line (birth dates excluded); Encounter.period.start and Patient.birthDate must be dates the record states. Record-keeping times (authoredOn, recordedDate, issued …) only warn about an ungrounded date and their time is not checked; timestamps the tools / documents write themselves (Bundle.timestamp, Composition.date, Provenance.recorded …) are not checked. - Quantities: every number outside dates and times (so a 0 or a 14 is never grounded by "08:00" or "2025/03/14"), with its unit, Chinese numerals, 半, fractions; it must have a compatible unit (when both units are known), or convert (mass / volume / length / time, °F ↔ °C, glucose mg/dL ↔ mmol/L, 10^3/uL ↔ /uL), BMI from height and weight, an explicit product (500 mg x 2). Derived quantities (dispenseRequest.quantity, expectedSupplyDuration, Claim item quantities) also accept a product of numbers on one line and only warn when not found; reference ranges warn; denominators are not checked.

Output

  • Each issue: severity, code (above), path, message (Chinese / English), message_zh, message_en, rule (R1–R5), source: "record-checks", evidence (the basis of the verdict), and located_quotes for the rules that need the record.
  • fhir_validate_bundle / fhir_validate_resource: issues go into entries[i].issues (Bundle-level ones into issues); an error makes entries[i].valid and data.valid false (conformanceValid / groundingValid keep their meaning); data.record_checks = {ok, errors, warnings, rules, source_text, notes?} is added when source_text is given or anything was found. Without source_text only R1 and R2 run (the stated absences and identifiers without value of R1, and R3–R5, need the record); without source_text and without any finding the output is byte-identical to the output before this layer (no record_checks, no extra provenance fields).
  • fhir_author_resources: as fhir_validate_resource, in results[].issues (an error makes the status invalid); the optional source_text (not stored on the context) adds R3 / R4; site_config format rules apply.
  • fhir_assemble_bundle: as fhir_validate_bundle (R3 / R4 with source_text), issues tagged with key / field.
  • fhir_finalize_bundle: optional source_text; results in data.record_issues and data.record_checks (the Bundle and changes are unchanged), plus a warning when any is an error.
  • fhir_finalize_resource: optional source_text; issues go into data.validation.issues (an error makes validation.valid false); the draft is never changed by them.
  • The same rule holds for every tool above: without source_text and without findings the output is unchanged.
  • When the layer reports, provenance gains recordChecksVersion, recordChecksLexicon, recordChecksLexiconSha256. The record text is never logged.

docs.title: Tool versions
docs.text:
Tools whose behaviour is pinned by fixtures carry their own version (node-server/src/toolVersions.ts), bumped whenever their output for the same input changes. health_check reports the current values under tools_version; every other tool uses the server version (version, currently 1.1.0).

Tool Version fhir_validate_bundle 1.12.0 (record checks v15.1: with source_text every identifier / date / quantity value must be in the record (ungrounded-value), values of another time point / event / field (value-from-other-event), stated absences and identifiers without value, the primary diagnosis slot, bracket-scoped cues; output without source_text unchanged); 1.11.2 (normalize_ids + repair="content" as fhir_finalize_bundle 1.3.2); 1.11.1 (content repairs with normalize_ids + repair="content" as fhir_finalize_bundle 1.3.1); 1.11.0 (record checks: information-absent / identifier-format always; with source_text also precision, values, free-text medicines and unconfirmed diagnoses; data.record_checks); 1.10.0 (repair="content" with normalize_ids=true: content repairs before validation, content_changes / repair_issues); 1.9.0 (validator v13: a ValueSet canonical as Coding.system is an error, LOINC property filters decide membership); 1.8.0 (normalized_bundle keeps number spellings; bdl-11 / bdl-12 on a document / message without its head resource carry replace_value / add_resource suggestions; 1.7.0: normalize_ids, ID-class suggestions and id_map / id_changes) fhir_validate_resource 1.9.0 (record checks as fhir_validate_bundle 1.12.0); 1.8.0 (record checks, as fhir_validate_bundle 1.11.0); 1.7.0 (validator v13: a ValueSet canonical as Coding.system is an error with candidates, LOINC property filters decide membership); 1.6.2 (validator v8: unknown HL7-space CodeSystems always errors, whitespace in references, RxNorm displays naming another drug, exception issues for failed lookups / crashes; 1.6.0: issue suggestions / caused_by) fhir_finalize_bundle 1.4.0 (data.record_issues with source_text as the record checks of fhir_validate_bundle 1.12.0); 1.3.2 (evaluator decisions: a display error exposed by the system correction of the same Coding no longer withdraws it; docs.title: FHIR Server Tools
docs.text: This group is used to discover and operate external FHIR R4 servers registered through the admin console. These tools are always registered (independent of data module load status). Adding and editing servers, authentication credentials, and health-check settings all happen in Admin Console → FHIR Servers; the MCP side sees only a safe summary and never obtains or relays tokens, client secrets, or private keys.

docs.title: list_fhir_servers
docs.text: List the available external FHIR servers — the discovery entry point.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description include_disabled boolean No Whether to include disabled (enabled=false) servers, false by default

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: {count, servers: [...]}. Each server carries server_key (use this value when calling the other tools), name, base_url, enabled, default, allowed_resource_types, allowed_operations, fhir_version, supported_resources, auth (informational only), and probe (the most recent connectivity check).

docs.title: get_fhir_server_status
docs.text: Retrieve the status and configuration of a single server, with the same fields as list_fhir_servers.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description server_key string Yes The server's stable identifier (not its name)

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Before calling crud_fhir_server, confirm enabled=true and probe.ok=true. If not, run a metadata operation first or alert the user.

docs.title: crud_fhir_server
docs.text: Perform a FHIR REST operation against a given server.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description server_key string Yes Target server identifier ("default" selects the default server) operation string No metadata by default; metadata / read / search / create / update / patch / delete resource_type string Depends on operation FHIR resource type (such as Patient or Observation) resource_id string Depends on operation Target resource ID (read / update / patch / delete) query_json string Used by search Search parameters as a JSON object string, e.g. '{"name":"Chen","_count":"10"}' resource_json string Required for create / update The full FHIR resource as a JSON string patch_json string Required for patch A JSON Patch array as a string confirm_write boolean Required for writes Write operations (create / update / patch / delete) only execute when this is true token_strategy string No Override the server's default token strategy: auto (default) / fresh / cached

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Operations and resource types are constrained by the server's allowed_operations / allowed_resource_types; anything not permitted is rejected outright.
  • The path is composed from operation / resource_type / resource_id; the caller does not pass a URL directly. Query strings and request bodies come from query_json, resource_json, and patch_json instead — all of them JSON strings, not objects.
  • OAuth tokens are handled by the MCP server on the caller's behalf; the caller never touches them.
  • Client Credentials (including private_key_jwt) obtain tokens per the fresh / cached strategy; Authorization Code uses the encrypted grant stored by the admin console and refreshes automatically on expiry. An Authorization Code server must complete Authorize in Admin → FHIR Servers first.

docs.title: FHIR Condition / Medication Tools
docs.text:
This group converts local ICD-10 diagnoses and Taiwan FDA drug data into FHIR R4 Condition / Medication / MedicationKnowledge resources, with basic validation. For advanced profile- and terminology-level authoring and validation, see FHIR IG Tools.

Maintenance mode: the Condition tools follow the icd module and the Medication tools follow the drug module. While the admin console has that module in maintenance mode, calls return an isError result immediately with error code MODULE_MAINTENANCE (error.message in English, error.message_zh in Traditional Chinese, error.module the module key), effective within about 5 seconds; the tools stay in tools/list. See the API reference.

docs.title: query_fhir_condition
docs.text: Generate a FHIR R4 Condition resource from an ICD-10 diagnosis.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description Example icd_code string No An ICD-10-CM code given directly (Path A, full field support; supply this or diagnosis_keyword) "E11.9" diagnosis_keyword string No Diagnosis keyword (Chinese or English): searched first, then the resource is built (Path B; when both are given the keyword wins) "第二型糖尿病" patient_id string No The Patient reference to link; empty string by default "patient-001" clinical_status string No active (default) / inactive / resolved / remission "resolved" verification_status string No confirmed (default) / provisional / differential / refuted "provisional" category string No encounter-diagnosis (default) / problem-list-item "problem-list-item" severity string No Severity "moderate" onset_date string No Onset date "2026-01-15" recorded_date string No Recorded date "2026-02-01" additional_notes string No Extra notes, written into Condition.note "under follow-up"

At least one of icd_code and diagnosis_keyword must be supplied; with both omitted the tool returns {"error": "Provide either icd_code or diagnosis_keyword"}. Path B (keyword) applies only patient_id, clinical_status, verification_status and severity; the other fields (category, dates, notes) take effect on Path A only.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Maps the ICD-10-CM code into Condition.code.coding automatically, filling in the standard system URI (http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10-cm) and the disease name, then populates clinicalStatus, verificationStatus, category, subject, and the other attributes from the parameters above.

docs.title: validate_fhir_condition
docs.text: Validate the basic structure of a FHIR Condition resource.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description condition_json string Yes The Condition JSON string to validate

docs.title: Response format
docs.text:
{ "valid": true, "errors": [], "warnings": [] }

Unlike validate_fhir_medication, this tool's response carries no resource_type, but adds a warnings array (for recommended fields that are missing, for example). valid reflects only whether errors is empty; warnings do not affect it.

docs.title: query_fhir_medication
docs.text: Generate a FHIR R4 Medication or MedicationKnowledge resource from Taiwan FDA drug data.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example keyword string No Drug keyword: searched first, then the resource is built (Path B; supply this or license_id) "普拿疼" license_id string No License number (Path A; when both are given the license number wins) "衛署藥製字第000480號" resource_type string No Medication (default) or MedicationKnowledge "MedicationKnowledge"

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Coding uses the TFDA license number CodeSystem (https://mcp.fda.gov.tw/fhir/CodeSystem/tfda-license-id) and carries ingredient information. Resources are derived from normalised TFDA data only — RxNorm is not used.

docs.title: validate_fhir_medication
docs.text: Validate the basic structure of a FHIR Medication resource.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description medication_json string Yes The Medication JSON string to validate

docs.title: Response format
docs.text:
{ "valid": true, "resource_type": "Medication", "errors": [] }

These two validation tools perform basic structure and required-field checks only. When profile conformance (IG conformance) validation is needed, use fhir_validate_resource / fhir_validate_bundle instead.

docs.title: Health Supplement Tools
docs.text: This group covers lookup of Taiwan FDA-approved health supplements and condition-driven recommendations.

docs.title: search_health_supplements
docs.text:
A single entry point with three modes:

  • mode="keyword": search product name, company, ingredients, and health claims
  • mode="permit_no": look up by license number, accepting both the full string and digits only — for example A00022 or 000029
  • mode="condition": recommend approved supplements for a disease / ICD context

docs.title: Choosing a mode
docs.text: Mode When to use it What it searches What comes back keyword You know the product name or a claim term, or want to see what exists Product name / company / ingredients / claims A uniform summary list of matching products permit_no You have the supplement license number, or only its trailing digits License number / bare digits An exact match on one product, ideal for confirming approval details condition You want to work back from a disease context to supplements worth considering ICD code / disease name Top-level icd_code and recommended_benefits, with results being the candidate products

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example mode string No keyword / permit_no / condition, keyword by default "keyword" keyword string Yes Search keyword; for condition, a disease name or ICD-10 code "魚油", "A00022", "E11" limit integer No Result cap, 3 by default, 10 maximum (ignored in permit_no mode) 5

docs.title: Response format
docs.text:
Every mode returns the same top-level structure, but only condition mode adds the top-level icd_code and recommended_benefits:

{
  "mode": "keyword",
  "keyword": "魚油",
  "results": [...]
}

keyword mode runs a hybrid BM25 + semantic search; without embeddings it falls back to keyword-only and adds search_mode: "keyword_only" and search_note. Without keyword the tool returns {"error": "Provide keyword"}. The group is registered only while health_supplements.items holds at least 10 rows.

docs.title: Fields on each result
docs.text:
Every mode uses the same fields on each result:

  • permit_no
  • product_name
  • company
  • category
  • benefits
  • approval_date

condition mode additionally populates, at the top level: - icd_code - recommended_benefits

Note: icd_code and recommended_benefits never appear inside individual results[] items — only in the top-level response of condition mode.

docs.title: Usage advice
docs.text:
• To find legally approved products, start with keyword.
  • To verify certificate data, use permit_no.
  • To compile candidate products from a disease perspective, use condition.

docs.title: ICD-10 Tools
docs.text:
This group provides lookup and hierarchy browsing over ICD-10-CM (diagnoses) and ICD-10-PCS (procedures). Data comes from icd.diagnoses / icd.procedures, populated by the icd_import job; the loaded ICD-10-CM edition (for example the complete 2026-04-01 edition loaded from the CMS "Code Descriptions in Tabular Order" file, including 7th characters and placeholder X) is reported by health_check under terminology.icd10cm. The whole group is unregistered while icd.diagnoses holds fewer than 10,000 rows.

Maintenance mode: while the admin console has the icd module in maintenance mode, this group's calls return an isError result immediately with error code MODULE_MAINTENANCE (error.message in English, error.message_zh in Traditional Chinese, error.module the module key), effective within about 5 seconds; the tools stay in tools/list. See the API reference.

docs.title: search_medical_codes
docs.text: Search ICD-10 diagnosis or procedure codes.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example keyword string Yes Search keyword (code, Chinese name, or English name) "糖尿病", "E11", "Appendectomy" type string No Search type, "all" by default.Allowed values: "diagnosis", "procedure", "all" "diagnosis" limit integer No Cap per result class, 3 by default, 10 maximum (50 for an IG CodeSystem) 5 system string No Omit for ICD-10 (by type). icd10cm / icd10pcs, or any CodeSystem of an installed IG: canonical, id or alias words (e.g. nhi_payment = the NHI medical service payment codes). IG CodeSystems go through IG Concept Search and return {keyword, system, codesystem, results[], clauses?, search_mode?} "nhi_payment"

docs.title: How the search works
docs.text: diagnosis runs a hybrid BM25 + vector re-ranking search; procedure is BM25 only; all (the default) does both and returns them under separate diagnoses / procedures keys. Results are ordered by relevance, not alphabetically by code: the candidates are the union of full-text matches (shortest names first) and the nearest vectors, ordered by score-aware fusion — the lexical score measures how far query and name cover each other (a query that is a name beats longer sub-concepts that merely contain it; qualifiers such as "unspecified" / 未明示 cost nothing), the semantic score is the cosine similarity rescaled within the pool, plus a small code-depth prior (a short query prefers I50 / I50.9 over I50.813). The two nearest vectors always stay in the result, so weak keyword hits can no longer push a strong semantic match out of the top-k (the old RRF failure). The vector side deliberately runs an exact scan instead of the HNSW index: the complete ICD-10-CM has many near-duplicate codes that differ only in the 7th character, and HNSW recall collapses on that data. When the embedding endpoint is unavailable or icd.diagnosis_embeddings is empty the search falls back to keyword-only and the response carries search_mode: "keyword_only". When ICD-10-PCS is not loaded, procedures is an empty array with a procedures_note.

docs.title: infer_complications
docs.text: List a code's child codes from the ICD-10-CM hierarchy (pure hierarchy lookup — no clinical inference).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example code string Yes Base diagnosis code "E11"

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: When the user supplies only a vague diagnosis (such as "diabetes"), this tool lists the specific subdivisions under that category (such as nephropathy or retinopathy) to help clarify the condition. With children it returns {base_code, potential_complications_or_specifics} (up to 15); for a leaf code it returns other codes of the same category as {message, related_codes} (up to 10).

docs.title: get_nearby_codes
docs.text: Retrieve the 2 codes immediately before and the 2 after a target code in alphabetical order (ordering neighbours, not semantic matches).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example code string Yes Target code "I10"

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Useful for reviewing codes of differing severity or similar character within the same disease spectrum, which assists differential diagnosis.

docs.title: check_medical_conflict
docs.text: Fetch the full definitions of one diagnosis code and one procedure code side by side for coding QA.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example diagnosis_code string Yes ICD-10-CM diagnosis code "K35.80" (acute appendicitis) procedure_code string Yes ICD-10-PCS procedure code "0DTJ0ZZ" (appendectomy)

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Returns the detailed definitions of both sides for comparison. The tool reports facts only and makes no compatibility judgement — it returns no pass/fail verdict, so deciding whether the pair conflicts is left to the caller.

docs.title: browse_icd_category
docs.text: Browse diagnosis codes by ICD category.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example category string No Category code (first three characters). Omit to return the list of all categories "E11" limit integer No Cap on codes returned when expanding a category, 50 by default, 200 maximum 100

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Without category, returns {"total_categories", "categories": [...]}; with a category (such as E11), returns every diagnosis code under it as {"category", "total", "codes": [...]}. Suitable for listing categories first and then drilling down.

Every tool returns JSON (a JSON string inside the MCP content[0].text block); none of them emit a plain-text format.

docs.title: Lab Tools (Lab / LOINC)
docs.text:
The LOINC surface has been consolidated into four tools: search_loinc, query_loinc, interpret_lab_result, and batch_interpret_lab_results.

Defaults: search_loinc uses mode code and limit 3 (10 maximum); query_loinc uses mode detail; gender always defaults to all. The code / specimen / component modes run a hybrid BM25 + semantic search (code mode uses score-aware fusion with LOINC COMMON_TEST_RANK and status as a prior; analyte families: among the terms of one COMPONENT (without its ^ timing / challenge suffix; per-cell and fraction properties form their own family) the ones the query cannot tell apart — the same query words covered, or, when no query word matched, a similarity within 0.2 — are ordered by COMMON_TEST_RANK, so "hemoglobin" gets 718-7 rather than a molar or arterial variant while "arterial lactate" still gets the arterial term; the 2 most common terms of every pooled analyte join the pool; the plain analyte of a challenge / timing variant joins too ("Renin^baseline" → Renin); panels and ratios (a COMPONENT with /) sink a little unless the query says panel / ratio / / / % / 比值. Analyte synonyms: loinc.component_names holds analyte names from Loinc.csv RELATEDNAMES2 and the zh-CN linguistic variant (folded to Traditional script) — "uric acid" → Urate, "FSH" / 卵泡刺激素 → Follitropin, 泌乳激素 → Prolactin — keeping only names listed on most of the analyte's terms and shared by at most 300 analytes, which drops specimen / timing / class vocabulary; a name of an analyte does not match its ratios (白蛋白 is Albumin, not Albumin/Protein.total) unless the query asks for a ratio or %. Axis words: loinc.axis_names holds the names of every SYSTEM / TIME / METHOD / PROPERTY / SCALE value taken from LOINC itself — Part.csv part and display names ("BldV" = "Venous blood", "24H" = "24 hours") and the Loinc.csv RELATEDNAMES2 names listed on nearly every term of a value ("Venous", "Random" → Pt, "Dipstick" → Test strip, "Percent" → the fraction properties, "Spinal fluid" → CSF). Specimen / timing / method / property / scale words in an English query ("venous lactate", "salivary cortisol", "CSF glucose", "24 hour urine protein", "random urine sodium", "urine glucose dipstick", "HbA1c by HPLC", "neutrophils %") become constraints: within an analyte family the terms that honour them (by axis value, or because their own name already contains the word) come before the most common term, the analyte's most common terms with that specimen / timing join the pool, and a small prior (±0.1) rewards / penalises agreement; when the query names no axis, ranking is as before. When two specimens that exclude each other appear ("urine blood dipstick"), the first is taken as the specimen. Needs migrations 20261024, 20261025 and 20261026 plus a LOINC re-import; without them ranking is as before) and fall back to keyword-only with search_mode: "keyword_only" when embeddings are unavailable. The whole group is unregistered while loinc.concepts holds fewer than 1,000 rows.

Maintenance mode: while the admin console has the loinc module in maintenance mode, this group's calls return an isError result immediately with error code MODULE_MAINTENANCE (error.message in English, error.message_zh in Traditional Chinese, error.module the module key), effective within about 5 seconds; the tools stay in tools/list. See the API reference.

docs.title: 1) search_loinc (search entry point)
docs.text: A single search entry point; mode switches the query intent.

docs.title: Mode: code
docs.text:
• Purpose: find candidate LOINC codes by test name, abbreviation, or keyword
  • Parameters: keyword required, category optional, limit optional
  • Example: search_loinc(mode="code", keyword="HbA1c", category="CHEM", limit=5)

docs.title: Mode: category
docs.text:
• Purpose: list every available LOINC category (filter category names with keyword)
  • Parameters: keyword optional, limit optional
  • Example: search_loinc(mode="category")
  • Example: search_loinc(mode="category", keyword="CHE")

docs.title: Mode: specimen
docs.text:
• Purpose: find candidate test codes by specimen type
  • Parameters: keyword required (specimen name), limit optional
  • Example: search_loinc(mode="specimen", keyword="Urine", limit=5)

docs.title: Mode: component
docs.text:
• Purpose: find related test codes by analyte / component
  • Parameters: keyword required (analyte), limit optional
  • Example: search_loinc(mode="component", keyword="Glucose", limit=5)

docs.title: 2) query_loinc (detail / reference range entry point)
docs.text: A single query entry point; mode switches between detail and reference range.

docs.title: Mode: detail
docs.text:
• Purpose: full concept detail for a single LOINC code
  • Parameters: loinc_code required
  • Example: query_loinc(mode="detail", loinc_code="2345-7")

docs.title: Mode: reference_range
docs.text:
• Purpose: the reference range for a single LOINC code
  • Parameters: loinc_code and age required, gender optional (M/F/all)
  • Example: query_loinc(mode="reference_range", loinc_code="2345-7", age=45, gender="M")

docs.title: 3) interpret_lab_result
docs.text:
Interpretation of a single result.

  • Parameters: loinc_code, value, and age required, gender optional
  • Example: interpret_lab_result(loinc_code="1558-6", value=126, age=45, gender="M")

docs.title: 4) batch_interpret_lab_results
docs.text:
Batch interpretation (an entire report).

  • Parameters: results_json and age required, gender optional
  • results_json format:
[{"loinc_code":"2345-7","value":126},{"loinc_code":"718-7","value":15.2}]
  • Example: batch_interpret_lab_results(results_json='[...]', age=45, gender="M")

docs.title: Suggested order of use
docs.text:
1. Find the code: search_loinc(mode="code" | "specimen" | "component")
  2. Review the detail: query_loinc(mode="detail", ...)
  3. Get a reference range: query_loinc(mode="reference_range", ...)
  4. Interpret values: interpret_lab_result or batch_interpret_lab_results

docs.title: Food Nutrition Tools
docs.text: This group provides nutrient lookup for Taiwan foods, food ingredient compliance lookup, and dietary analysis. Every food name is resolved with hybrid BM25 + semantic embedding (RRF) search, which crosses synonyms and near-synonyms (searching「白米飯」finds「白飯」in the database).

docs.title: query_food_nutrition
docs.text: Look up a food's nutrition information (per 100 g). detailed switches the output mode.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example food_name string Yes Food name (Chinese or English) "白米", "雞胸肉", "salmon" nutrient string No Filter to a specific nutrient (only effective when detailed=false) "粗蛋白", "維生素C", "鈣" limit int No Maximum rows to return (3 by default, 10 maximum; only effective when detailed=false) 5 detailed bool No false (default) for a quick lookup; true for the full categorised panel true

docs.title: Output modes
docs.text:
detailed=false (default) — a flat list, for quick lookups: - Returns at most limit foods - Supports partial-match nutrient filtering (ILIKE) - Output: [{food, category, nutrients: [{item, value, unit}, ...]}, ...]

detailed=true — the full nutrition panel, grouped by category: - Always returns at most 3 rows; limit and nutrient are ignored - Covers energy, macronutrients, vitamins (A / B group / C / D / E / K / niacin / folate), minerals (Ca/P/Fe/Na/K/Mg/Zn/Mn/Cu), and fatty acids (SFA/MUFA/PUFA/trans/EPA/DHA) - Output: [{sample_name, common_name, food_category, nutrients: {category: [{item, value, unit}]}}]

docs.title: query_food_ingredient
docs.text: Search the regulatory classification of a food ingredient or additive to confirm whether it is approved for use in food. The optional category filter narrows the search to one top-level class.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example keyword string Yes Ingredient name (Chinese or English) "薑黃", "turmeric", "卡拉膠", "sorbic acid" category enum No Top-level category filter; omit to search everything "可供食品使用之原料" limit int No Maximum rows to return (3 by default, 10 maximum) 5

docs.title: Allowed category values (major_category)
docs.text: Value Meaning 可供食品使用之原料 Approved for use in food (roughly 1,170 rows) 未確認安全性尚不得使用之原料 Safety unconfirmed, currently not permitted (roughly 532 rows)

docs.title: Output
docs.text: [{name_zh, name_en, major_category, sub_category, note}, ...]

docs.title: search_foods_by_nutrient
docs.text: Rank Taiwan FDA foods from highest to lowest by a given nutrient (per 100 g).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example nutrient string Yes Nutrient name (Chinese or English aliases both accepted) "鈣", "calcium", "蛋白質", "EPA" limit int No Rows to return (20 by default, 50 maximum) 10

docs.title: Alias resolution order
docs.text:
1. The built-in alias table ("蛋白質" → "粗蛋白", "vitamin c" → "維生素C", and so on)
  2. Partial ILIKE match against Taiwan FDA column names
  3. Semantic embedding search (when neither of the above found anything)

docs.title: Output
docs.text: {"nutrient", "unit", "foods": [{food_name, food_code, category, value}, ...]}

docs.title: analyze_meal_nutrition
docs.text:
Compute the overall nutrition totals for several foods in one meal (100 g per food by default).

Each food name is resolved to the closest database entry through hybrid BM25 + embedding RRF search (for example「白米飯」→「白飯」in the database).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example foods list[string] Yes List of food names ["白米飯", "雞胸肉", "青花菜", "豆腐"]

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
{
  "meal_components": {
    "<food_name>": {
      "found": true,
      "food_name": "...",
      "nutrients": {"熱量": ..., "粗蛋白": ..., "...": ...}
    }
  },
  "combined_totals_per_100g_each": {"熱量": ..., "粗蛋白": ..., "...": ...}
}

Foods that cannot be found are marked "found": false; entries that were recognised but could not be resolved carry an "error" explanation.

docs.title: SNOMED CT Tools
docs.text:
The public SNOMED surface consists of four tools: search_snomed_concept, query_snomed_concept, get_snomed_relationships, and query_snomed_mapping.

Maintenance mode: while the admin console has the snomed module in maintenance mode, this group's calls return an isError result immediately with error code MODULE_MAINTENANCE (error.message in English, error.message_zh in Traditional Chinese, error.module the module key), effective within about 5 seconds; the tools stay in tools/list. See the API reference.

docs.title: search_snomed_concept
docs.text: Search SNOMED concept candidates by English clinical term.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Use it first when you only have a text term and do not yet know the concept ID. The tool ranks full-text and embedding candidates with score-aware fusion over every active name of a concept (FSN and synonyms), returning the closest concepts semantically rather than only exact literal matches; a concept whose name the query is ranks first, and inactive concepts sink.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example query string Yes English clinical term "diabetes mellitus" limit integer No Result cap (3 by default, 10 maximum) 5 hierarchy_filter integer No Return only IS-A descendants of one concept (usually a top-level hierarchy concept ID) 404684003

docs.title: What comes back
docs.text: Each row carries concept_id, fsn, preferred_term, active and hierarchy_tag — enough to pick the concept to query next; use query_snomed_concept for the full record.

docs.title: How hierarchy_filter works
docs.text:
hierarchy_filter restricts results to that concept and its IS-A descendants (the concept itself included). The full-text half is always the hierarchy's best literal matches; the vector half depends on the hierarchy's size:

  • ≤ 1,000 concepts (e.g. Heart structure): an exact vector comparison against every member (the same ordering as an unfiltered search).
  • > 1,000 concepts (e.g. Body structure 42,697, Procedure 59,616, Substance 27,725): a walk of the HNSW vector index that keeps only members, bounded to 1,000 visited entries. Membership is one primary-key probe into snomed.concept_ancestors (each concept's IS-A ancestors, built at import). A filtered search therefore costs about as much as an unfiltered one (an exact scan of a large hierarchy used to take 40–130 s); the trade-off is that a query with no literal or semantic tie to the hierarchy (e.g. "fracture of femur" within Substance) can return fewer results, or none, instead of the hierarchy's "least distant" concepts.

Until snomed.concept_ancestors exists (migration 20261028_snomed_concept_ancestors.sql not applied), the descendant set is expanded on every call instead — same results, 0.2–0.5 s more per call (warm cache).

docs.title: query_snomed_concept
docs.text: Retrieve the concept itself plus its hierarchical context (parents / children) in one call.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Use it when you already have a concept ID and want concept details, ancestors, and children together.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example concept_id integer Yes SNOMED concept ID 73211009 include_parents boolean No Return the ancestor chain, true by default false include_children boolean No Return direct child concepts, true by default false parent_limit integer No Cap on ancestors expanded, 10 by default, 20 maximum 20 child_limit integer No Cap on children expanded, 20 by default, 200 maximum 50

docs.title: What comes back
docs.text: concept is always present; ancestors, children, and their counts are attached according to the parameters.

docs.title: get_snomed_relationships
docs.text: Query non-IS-A attribute relationships (semantic attributes).

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Use it to see clinical semantic attributes rather than hierarchy — for example finding site, causative agent, associated morphology, or has active ingredient.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description concept_id integer Yes SNOMED concept ID relationship_type_id integer No Return only one relationship type (e.g. 363698007 finding site)

Returns {concept_id, relationship_count, relationships}, grouped by relationship type, each group with a readable label and its target concepts.

docs.title: query_snomed_mapping
docs.text: A single entry point for bidirectional ICD ↔ SNOMED mapping.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
• mode="icd": keyword is treated as an ICD-10 code, returning snomed_concepts.
  • mode="snomed": keyword may be a numeric concept ID or an English term.
  • Purely numeric: maps directly by concept ID (no embeddings involved)
  • Text: performs a SNOMED search for the best concept first, then maps (this step uses embeddings)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description Example mode string No icd or snomed, icd by default "icd" keyword string Yes ICD code, concept ID, or English term "E11.9", "44054006"
